description:
# Author and verify the dated shelf cards for Journey II (Brownian motion)

**Epic:** `am-ep-discovery-33u` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §5.1–5.3, §9.3, §3.9 (paper 2 margin), §22.1 (traceability only)

## Background

Journey II asks: how can visible wandering reveal invisible molecules? Its shelf holds what a careful reader of the literature could know by the end of 1904 about Brownian motion, kinetic theory, osmosis, drag, and diffusion. Two entries are deliberately wrong turns that become forks (Nägeli's single-impact objection and Exner's speed measurements). One entry, Sutherland, is the canonical test of the shelf rules: his January 1904 Dunedin presentation is a legitimate shelf card, while his June 1905 *Philosophical Magazine* paper appeared between Einstein's submission (received 11 May 1905) and publication (18 July 1905) and is parallel work.

Anachronism controls for this paper: do not say everyone rejected atoms (represent real disagreement and existing molecular reasoning); do not say Einstein explained observations he had studied in detail (the paper's introduction says the available reports were too imprecise for a judgment); do not present Langevin equations or Wiener-process notation (1908 and later) as Einstein's derivation.

The Brownian reference slice (`am-bm-slice-discovery-route-tias`) already authors the cards that Route B and the Exner fork need. This bead completes, verifies, and, where needed, corrects the full shelf. Whichever bead lands first creates a card; the other reuses the same record and id, so no card is duplicated.

## Scope

In scope: one verified HistoricalPremise record per card below, with the fields and rules of `am-disc-knowledge-cards-iw8j`; permitted stages; limits; the paper's own citations where present; the Sutherland split; the list of later items kept off the shelf; reuse and verification of the slice's cards.

Out of scope (owned elsewhere): card rendering and rules (`am-disc-knowledge-cards-iw8j`); the chain (`am-disc-journey-ii-chain-pl6u`); the Perrin dataset (`am-data-perrin-1909-p7ku`); paper 2 margin entries (`am-bm-margin-entries-7fa4`); timeline cards for later items (`am-disc-timeline-xzef`).

## Requirements

Store records under `content/historical-premises/` (journey-neutral card ids in lowercase kebab case; this bead's cards may be grouped in `content/historical-premises/brownian/`). Each record carries the standard fields: citations verified against the original, date with precision, `latestYear`, precise proposition, limits, status, `admittedStages`, `paperCitesOrAsserts` where the paper cites or asserts the item, Einstein-knowledge evidence only with its own citation, and a verification record with an evidence locator.

| Card id | Date (`latestYear`) | Proposition | Limits to state | Status | Candidate citation (verify) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `brown-1828-microscopical-observations` | observed 1827, published 1828 (1828) | Fragments from within pollen grains, and inorganic particles, suspended in water move irregularly | An observation, not a cause | available | R. Brown, Phil. Mag. (n.s.) 4 (1828) 161 |
| `gouy-1888-brownian-motion` | 1888 (1888) | The motion is intrinsic and persistent; faster for smaller particles and in warmer, less viscous liquids; not caused by light, convection, or vibration; Gouy proposed thermal molecular agitation as its cause | Qualitative; no quantitative law | available | G. Gouy, J. Phys. Théor. Appl. (2) 7 (1888) 561 |
| `naegeli-1879-single-impact-objection` | 1879 (1879) | A single molecular impact cannot give a visible particle a perceptible velocity, so molecular agitation cannot be the cause of the motion | States the claim only; the flaw is shown in Fork A, never editorialized on the card | available | C. Nägeli, Sitzungsber. math.-phys. Cl. k. b. Akad. Wiss. München 9 (1879) 389 (verify volume and pages) |
| `exner-1900-particle-speeds` | 1900 (1900) | Measured particle "speeds" are far too small for kinetic theory | States what was measured; that the measured quantity depends on the observation interval is shown in Fork B | available | F. M. Exner, Ann. Phys. (4) 2 (1900) 843 |
| `maxwell-1860-equipartition` | 1860 to Boltzmann's gas-theory work (year of the latest cited source) | In thermal equilibrium the mean kinetic energy of translation is the same for every kind of particle, whatever its mass (written today as $\tfrac32 k_BT$) | Classical equipartition; the symbol $k$ as a named constant is Planck's (1900–1901) notation and the card says so | available | J. C. Maxwell, Phil. Mag. (4) 19 (1860) 19; L. Boltzmann, Wien. Ber. 58 (1868) 517 or *Vorlesungen über Gastheorie* (1896–1898) (choose and verify) |
| `vanthoff-1887-osmotic-pressure` | 1877, 1887 (1887) | Dissolved molecules exert an osmotic pressure obeying the gas law | Dilute solutions | available | W. Pfeffer, *Osmotische Untersuchungen* (1877); J. H. van 't Hoff, Z. phys. Chem. 1 (1887) 481 |
| `stokes-1851-sphere-drag` | 1851 (1851) | A sphere moving slowly through a viscous fluid feels a drag $6\pi\eta a v$ | Low Reynolds number, continuum fluid, no slip at the surface | available | G. G. Stokes, Trans. Camb. Phil. Soc. 9 (1851) 8 |
| `fick-1855-diffusion-equation` | 1855 (1855) | The diffusion equation governs how concentration changes | A macroscopic law with no molecular mechanism | available | A. Fick, Ann. Phys. (Pogg.) 94 (1855) 59 |
| `siedentopf-1903-ultramicroscope` | developed 1902, published 1903 (1903) | The ultramicroscope makes particles below ordinary microscope resolution visible | Reconcile the plan's 1902 date with the publication; the card's date is the publication | available | H. Siedentopf and R. Zsigmondy, Ann. Phys. (4) 10 (1903) 1 |
| `loschmidt-1865-molecular-number-estimates` | 1865, 1900–1901 (1901) | Estimates of molecular size and of the molecular number exist (Loschmidt's gas-kinetic estimate; Planck's value from radiation constants) | Different methods with different and large uncertainties | available | J. Loschmidt, Wien. Ber. 52 (1865) 395; M. Planck, Ann. Phys. (4) 4 (1901) 553 |
| `bachelier-1900-speculation-random-walk` | 1900 (1900) | Random-walk-to-diffusion mathematics, worked out for stock prices in a Paris thesis examined by Poincaré | Unknown to physicists at the time; no evidence that Einstein knew it | available | L. Bachelier, Ann. Sci. École Norm. Sup. (3) 17 (1900) 21 |
| `sutherland-1904-dunedin` | January 1904 (1904) | The diffusion formula for large molecules, with a slip correction, presented at the Dunedin meeting | A legitimate shelf card; record exactly what the documentary record shows was presented, and not the later published derivation | available | W. Sutherland, Australasian Association for the Advancement of Science, Dunedin meeting, January 1904 (verify the record of the talk and its report) |
| `sutherland-1905-phil-mag` | proceedings with a misprint in early 1905; *Phil. Mag.* June 1905 (1905) | The published derivation of the diffusion formula with slip | Appeared between Einstein's submission and publication | parallel-work | W. Sutherland, Phil. Mag. (6) 9 (1905) 781 |

**The paper's own citations (category 3), to verify on the facsimile and record on the cards:** the introduction mentions the "so-called Brownian molecular motion" and says the information available to Einstein was too imprecise to form a judgment (`brown-1828-microscopical-observations`); §3 appears to cite Kirchhoff's lectures on mechanics for the drag formula (`stokes-1851-sphere-drag`); the osmotic argument names van 't Hoff's theory (`vanthoff-1887-osmotic-pressure`). Record each only after checking the page.

**Worth proposing (verify first):** earlier molecular explanations of the motion that show molecular reasoning predated Gouy, such as C. Wiener (1863) and J. Delsaulx with J. Carbonelle (from 1877). Add a card only when its original source is checked; this guards against the invented consensus that "everyone rejected atoms."

**Kept off the shelf** (timeline, margin, or world check only): Smoluchowski (1906); Einstein's second Brownian paper (1906), whose explicit discussion of why a mean velocity is not a meaningful observable belongs in the margin; Svedberg (1906) and Henri (1908) measurements (verify dates); Langevin (1908); Perrin (1908–1909) and his 1926 Nobel Prize; Cunningham's slip correction (1910); Bancelin (1911); ballistic Brownian motion measurements (Li et al. 2010; Huang et al. 2011).

## Technical Approach

- Search the compiled content for cards the slice created; verify them against the originals and complete the missing cards under the same ids. If this bead lands before the slice authors its cards, the slice reuses these records (`br comments add am-bm-slice-discovery-route-tias` with the ids).
- Resolve every candidate citation, especially Nägeli's publication details and the documentary record of Sutherland's Dunedin presentation; record volume, pages, and dates exactly as printed.
- Where an original contradicts the plan's date or proposition, correct the card, record the difference in `verification.discrepancies`, and raise it with `br comments add`.
- Assign `admittedStages` from the Journey II record's stage ids; until those ids exist, list the intended stages by name (the observable, Route A osmotic pressure, Route A configuration integral, Fork A, drag, Route B, Fork B, the world check, the inversion, the physician's door).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Thirteen verified records exist with every standard field; no candidate citation remains unverified; the two Sutherland cards are separate, and the 1905 card has status `parallel-work`.
- [ ] Every `available` card has `latestYear` of 1904 or earlier; the equipartition card's `latestYear` matches its latest cited source.
- [ ] No Journey II stage cites the 1905 Sutherland card without the acknowledged parallel-work flag (compiler-enforced).
- [ ] The ultramicroscope card's date is reconciled against its publication.
- [ ] The paper's own citations are recorded only where verified on the facsimile.
- [ ] Later items are recorded for the timeline and margin and are not attached to any shelf stage.
- [ ] The shelf audit (`audit-shelf.ts`) and the anachronism lint pass.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `content/historical-premises/brownian/brownianShelf.test.ts`: schema validity for every record; `latestYear` rules per status; the 1905 Sutherland card is `parallel-work`; every record has a verification record with an evidence locator; journey-neutral id format; no "Langevin," "Wiener process," "photon," or "spacetime" in card text outside labeled later-lens fields; the Nägeli and Exner cards contain none of a short list of evaluative words ("wrong," "mistaken," "naive," "foolish," "error").
- Compiler integration with the real card rules and epistemic checks: a fixture stage citing `sutherland-1905-phil-mag` without acknowledgment is rejected, and accepted with it; a fixture stage citing a later item (for example a Perrin card) is rejected.
- Duplicate check: attempting to add a second Brown card with the same citation key and proposition is rejected.

### End-to-end tests

- `e2e/journey-ii-shelf.spec.ts`, run through the browser harness once `/discover/brownian-motion` renders the shelf: open the shelf; confirm date order and status labels; open both Sutherland cards and the Brown card's "What the paper itself cites or asserts" section; repeat with JavaScript disabled and at 320 px.

### Structured logging

JSONL to `artifacts/test-logs/journey-ii-shelf/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `cardId`, `latestYear`, `status`, `verified`, `verifierKind`, `citation`, `discrepancyCount`, `browser`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `outcome`, `message`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- The Nägeli and Exner cards state what they claimed, fairly. The failure is shown in the worked forks, not by editorializing on the card.
- Do not imply that Bachelier influenced Einstein; there is no evidence.
- Keep Gouy's proposal distinct from a quantitative theory.
- Keep the 1906 paper's explicit velocity discussion off the 1904 shelf.
- Checking a citation means looking at the scan page; never run OCR locally.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-disc-knowledge-cards-iw8j`: card schema, validators, and rendering.
- `am-cm-anachronism-lint-dl2`: card text is linted for unlabeled anachronisms.

Unblocks:
- `am-disc-journey-ii-chain-pl6u`: the complete Journey II chain cites these cards.
- `am-dod-brownian-2k4y`: the Brownian definition of done requires every shelf card dated and sourced.
- `am-disc-desk-1904-9hgd` (proposed edge): the desk's premise catalogue lists every shelf card.

title: Build Journey III: the measurement procedure, both forks, the move, electrodynamics, checks, and exercises
description:
# Build Journey III: the measurement procedure, both forks, the move, electrodynamics, checks, and exercises

**Epic:** `am-ep-discovery-33u` · **Batch:** batch-g · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §9.1, §9.4, §8.3, §5.3, §5.4, §7.2, §14.5 (traceability only)

## Background

Journey III: **how could you stop assuming that everyone shares the same time?** It is the journey most exposed to hindsight. By the end of 1904 Lorentz had the transformation mathematics, and Poincaré had discussed the conventionality of simultaneity, described light-signal synchronization, and named the principle of relativity. The journey shows what was on the table, what a reader who took both postulates physically would do differently, and why the ether program is treated fairly: it reproduces the formulas and is not declared refuted by the kinematics alone. The journey covers both halves of the paper; a train animation plus a Lorentz matrix is not a complete treatment.

The journey is labeled "A route you could take." Its world checks are honest about what they can and cannot discriminate: aberration and Fizeau's coefficient were already explained within ether theories, and the later confirmations test predictions that Lorentz's completed theory and Einstein's kinematics share.

## Scope

In scope: the complete Journey III record `content/arguments/journeys/special-relativity.yaml` for `/discover/special-relativity`.

Out of scope (owned elsewhere): shelf cards (`am-disc-journey-iii-shelf-5z6q`); instruments SR-01 to SR-13; shelf instruments (`am-disc-shelf-michelson-fizeau-dauq`); datasets; the no-algebra entrance (`am-srk-first-encounter-471z`); placing the predict-perturb-explain task at the end of the reading chapter (`am-disc-ppe-teachback-wnp7`, which references this record).

## Requirements

**The nagging fact (SR-02 in apparatus mode).** "Nature does not care whether the magnet or the coil moves; the theory does." SR-02 shows the two classical descriptions of the same relative motion producing the same current to first order in $v/c$, one through an electric field that carries energy and one through an electromotive force with no corresponding energy.

**The first honest question.** "What if the principle of relativity is exactly true for electrodynamics too, and the speed of light is the same for every observer, and I follow both wherever they lead?"

### The chain

- **Two postulates and nothing else.** No ether, no electron model, no contraction hypothesis.
- **Make a measurement procedure (SR-01).** What does "at the same time" mean for two clocks a kilometer apart? Only light can carry the comparison. Adopt the convention Poincaré had discussed (1898) and described operationally with light signals (1900); the paper cites no one. Bounce a signal and assume equal travel times, $t_B - t_A = t'_A - t_B$. Keep an event ledger; distinguish an event from its reception. The no-algebra entrance (a signal leaves at 0, returns at 10, and the reflection is assigned 5, a stated convention rather than a measurement of an unknowable one-way time) is this stage in arithmetic.
- **Make the ordinary assumption explicit (`shelf-maxwell-galilean` in 1904 mode and SR-04's Galilean step).** Test $x' = x - vt$, $t' = t$ on slow objects (it works) and on light, $x = \pm ct$ (it does not preserve the light speed). Substituting into the wave equation makes a term appear. The conflict is between stated commitments, and the reader decides what to reconsider.
- **Watch simultaneity slip (SR-03).** Two events simultaneous in one frame are not simultaneous in another, by an amount proportional to their separation and to $v$: clocks synchronized in their own frame and separated by proper distance $L$ are out of step by $vL/c^2$ in the platform frame. Lorentz had this mathematics and did not take it physically: he kept a true time and treated the other as local. The margin cites Lorentz's own later acknowledgment (*The Theory of Electrons*, 2nd ed., 1916; verify) and presents historians' assessments of how far Poincaré's 1900 and 1904 views departed from Lorentz's, with citations, rather than asserting a verdict.
- **Fork A (after simultaneity).**
  - (a) *Lorentz 1904:* keep the ether and the true time; the transformation is a calculational device. Worked: it produces the same formulas, and the page says so. It accounts for each null result through compensating effects rather than making undetectability a principle; that is an interpretive difference, not a failed prediction. Outcome `empirically-equivalent-not-refuted`, scope note: "for the kinematic and optical predictions compared here, with the completions of Poincaré's June 1905 note (parallel work)."
  - (b) No privileged frame: every frame's clocks are as real as every other's. Outcome `papers-route`.
- **The move, side door (SR-04).** Construct the map from the postulates: begin with $x' = a(v)(x - vt)$, $t' = b(v)t + d(v)x$; requiring both light directions to stay $x' = \pm ct'$ gives $b = a$ and $d = -av/c^2$; applying the inverse gives $a(v)a(-v)(1 - v^2/c^2) = 1$; isotropy gives $a(v) = a(-v)$; the positive branch connected to the identity gives $a = \gamma$. Complete the transverse step honestly instead of copying $y' = y$. Read the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}\gamma & -\gamma v\\ -\gamma v/c^2 & \gamma\end{pmatrix}$: determinant 1, eigenvectors on the light lines, eigenvalues $\sqrt{(1 \mp v/c)/(1 \pm v/c)}$; rapidity appears only as a labeled later aid. Mark the construction as **the move**. Interval preservation may verify the result only as a `modern-oracle` edge, never as a premise.
- **The front door.** Einstein's §3 reaches the same map with a functional equation for $\tau$ and the synchronization condition; the reading face walks it with every step shown, in his notation ($\tau = \beta(t - vx/V^2)$, $\xi = \beta(x - vt)$, with his $\beta$ being the modern $\gamma$).
- **Read the consequences off the map (SR-03, SR-05, SR-06).** Rods, clocks, velocity composition, and nothing faster than $c$. The difference between an event separation and a rod measurement: at $v = 0.6c$, two events 10 light-seconds apart and simultaneous in the unprimed frame have $\Delta t' = -7.5$ s and $\Delta x' = 12.5$ light-seconds, which is not a rod length because the events are not simultaneous in the primed frame.
- **Fork B: now the electrodynamics.**
  - (a) Maxwell's equations hold exactly only in the ether frame and merely appear to hold elsewhere, with the magnet-and-coil case explained by two mechanisms. Worked: the predicted current agrees with observation, and the page says so. Outcome `empirically-equivalent-not-refuted`, scope note: "the same current for the magnet-and-conductor case to first order in $v/c$, the precision of the observations" (consistent with SR-02).
  - (b) The equations keep their exact form in every frame provided $\mathbf{E}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ mix under a boost (SR-07, SR-08). The asymmetry disappears. In the magnet's rest frame there is no electric field, and the moving coil's charges feel the magnetic force $q\,\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{B}$, which is the "electromotive force"; in the coil's rest frame the same effect is an electric field, $\mathbf{E}' = \gamma\,\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{B}$ for a field perpendicular to the motion (SR-08). The two descriptions predict the same current to first order in $v/c$. Outcome `papers-route`. The page states that the preference for (b) in the paper's introduction rests on removing an asymmetry "not inherent in the phenomena," not on a failed prediction of (a).
- **Transform a wave and a light complex (SR-09, SR-10, SR-11).** Doppler and aberration from the invariant phase; the energy of a light complex changes by the same factor as its frequency; the moving mirror. "File the energy result away for September" links to Journey IV's import card `einstein-1905-light-complex-energy`.
- **Charge, current, the electron (SR-12, SR-13).** A neutral current-carrying conductor is accepted. The historical force conventions are preserved: at $\beta = 0.6$ the source convention's transverse coefficient is $1.5625m$ and the laboratory one is $1.25m$, two definitions rather than two values of one mass.

### Check it against the world

- **Aberration (SR-09, computed live).** Loaded from SR-09's preset `sr-09-earth-orbit-aberration` (Earth's mean orbital speed 29.789 km/s, $\beta \approx 9.9366\times10^{-5}$), the accepted snapshot gives about 20.4956 arcseconds, labeled a modern computation, compared with Bradley's printed value from the shelf card (his figures correspond to about 20.2 arcseconds; transcribe and verify). The first-order effect follows from the phase transformation, and it also followed from the ether theories; the check shows consistency, not discrimination.
- **Fizeau (SR-06, computed live).** The low-speed limit of velocity composition gives the drag coefficient $1 - 1/n^2 \approx 0.437$ for water ($n = 1.333$), compared with the Fizeau 1851 dataset (an 1851 measurement on the shelf). The kinematic derivation is Laue's (1907, labeled later); Fresnel's ether theory also gave the coefficient, so again this is consistency, not discrimination.
- **Later evidence (dated, labeled later, from timeline cards and datasets):** Kaufmann's electron deflections were ambiguous in 1905–1906; Bucherer (1908) favored the Lorentz–Einstein prediction over Abraham's; Ives–Stilwell (1938), muon lifetimes (1941), flown clocks (1971, published 1972), and satellite clocks are dated on the timeline, not claimed for 1905. The page states that these confirm predictions shared by Lorentz's completed theory and Einstein's kinematics; they do not refute Fork A's branch (a).
- Without JavaScript, each computed check shows its build-time static worked example, labeled as such.

### What Einstein actually wrote

Jumps to paper 3 §1 (simultaneity), §3 (the transformation), §6 (the field transformation and the magnet-conductor reconciliation), §7 (Doppler and aberration), and §8 (light energy), each lighting its named weave predicate from the carried instrument state, or showing the static pointer without it.

### Doors

- **Front door:** §§1–3, the synchronization definition and the functional equation.
- **Side door, linear algebra:** the SR-04 construction.
- **Side door, arithmetic:** the 0, 10, 5 signal ledger (`am-srk-first-encounter-471z`), continuing into the measurement procedure and the construction.
- All doors arrive at the same equation id, the §3 transformation, and the page says so.

### Exercises

Instrumented (four; the framework requires two to five):
1. **Verify the determinant and eigenvectors by hand** (numeric: determinant 1; at $\beta = 0.6$ eigenvalues 2 and 0.5; references from `kinematics.ts`).
2. **Two collinear boosts give a boost; say what happens for non-collinear ones** (numeric: $0.6c$ then $0.6c$ gives $15c/17 \approx 0.8824c$; numeric: successive perpendicular boosts of $0.6c$ give a speed of $0.768375c$ with a rotation of $12.6804°$; explanation part: non-collinear composition includes a rotation).
3. **Derive the desynchronization $vL/c^2$** (expression equivalence, with declared variables $v$, $L$, $c$ and the stated sign convention that the rear clock leads).
4. **The speed at which a clock loses one second per day** (numeric: $1 - \sqrt{1-\beta^2} = 1/86\,400$ gives $\beta = \sqrt{\varepsilon(2-\varepsilon)} \approx 4.811\times10^{-3}$ with $\varepsilon = 1/86\,400$, about $1.442\times10^{6}$ m/s; the reference uses the cancellation-free form).

Explanation item (one):
5. Explain the magnet-and-coil asymmetry in three sentences without the word ether. The constraint is part of the prompt and of the comparison criteria for the reader's own check; no code inspects the reader's text.

### The predict-perturb-explain task (`ppeTask`)

- **Prompt:** "Two transformed events have a larger spatial separation; why is that alone not a rod measurement?"
- **Predict:** the reader chooses whether the 12.5 light-second separation is the rod's length in the primed frame (yes; no; it depends on which events are chosen), stored locally and never scored.
- **Perturb:** in SR-03, change the observer speed (an `observer-change` that preserves the run and events) and then select endpoint events that are simultaneous in the primed frame, through the instrument's action contract.
- **Explain:** an explanation part with comparison criteria (a rod length needs endpoint positions recorded at the same time in the frame doing the measuring; the original events are not simultaneous in the primed frame; choosing simultaneous endpoints gives the contracted length).
- `am-disc-ppe-teachback-wnp7` places this same record at the end of the relativity §§3–5 reading chapter.

**Added in review (relativity alignment of embedded instruments).**
- **Nagging fact.** The stage embeds SR-02 through preset `sr-02-apparatus-nagging-fact` (mode `sr-02:apparatus`, resolution withheld). It shows the two classical descriptions of the same relative motion; the §6 resolution caption sits in a closed native disclosure the reader may always open, so the stage never reveals the 1905 resolution by default.
- **Arithmetic side door.** The door embeds the no-algebra entrance by record id `entrance-special-relativity` from `am-srk-first-encounter-471z`, with host `returnTo` and `continueTo` targets (`continueTo` is the measurement-procedure stage). The door record keeps lens `arithmetic`, its entry and summary, and `arrivesAt` equal to the §3 transformation equation id.
- **Aberration world check.** The value comes from SR-09's accepted snapshot of `sr-09-earth-orbit-aberration`, never from a separate calculation here, so the journey and the instrument show one snapshot. Bradley's own figures are read from card `bradley-1729-aberration` (his printed ratio of about 10,210 to 1, about 20.2 arcseconds, pending verification). The roughly 1.5 percent difference is presented as Bradley's measurement, not as agreement.

## Technical Approach

- Author the journey record referencing shelf cards; SR-01 to SR-13 presets and teaching tapes ("the boost to 0.6c"); `shelf-maxwell-galilean` in 1904 mode; derivation-chain step ids with the SR-04 construction marked as the move (from `am-srk-equations-30cq`); weave predicates; exercises; the predict-perturb-explain task; the door equation id.
- The aberration and Fizeau checks bind exact quantity ids from SR-09 and SR-06 accepted snapshots and cite the dated card and dataset.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The nagging fact opens `sr-02-apparatus-nagging-fact` with the resolution withheld, the arithmetic door embeds `entrance-special-relativity` with working `returnTo` and `continueTo`, and the aberration check shows SR-09's snapshot identity beside Bradley's card values.
- [ ] Fork B (b) assigns the frames correctly: in the magnet's rest frame the coil's charges feel $q\,\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{B}$ with no electric field, and in the coil's rest frame the effect is the electric field $\mathbf{E}' = \gamma\,\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{B}$; a copy test fails on the reversed assignment.
- [ ] The journey validates as `complete` with every skeleton element.
- [ ] Fork A (a) and Fork B (a) are labeled empirically equivalent within their stated scopes and not refuted; neither is phrased as a failure.
- [ ] The SR-04 construction is marked as the move and includes the scale-factor and transverse steps; interval preservation appears only as a verification oracle.
- [ ] The 10 light-second event pair is presented as not a rod measurement.
- [ ] Aberration and Fizeau checks are computed live and framed as consistency checks; later evidence is dated and framed as shared by both accounts.
- [ ] All three doors end at the same equation id; four instrumented exercises, one explanation item, and the predict-perturb-explain task work.
- [ ] Spacetime diagrams and rapidity appear only as labeled later aids; the nagging fact embeds SR-02.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `content/arguments/journeys/specialRelativity.test.ts`, with the real compiler, framework checks, `kinematics.ts`, `events.ts`, and `waves.ts`: validation as `complete`; outcome types and scope notes; door equation ids; exercise roles and counts; references: determinant 1; eigenvalues 2 and 0.5 at $\beta = 0.6$; $15/17$; the perpendicular composition speed $0.768375c$ and rotation $12.6804°$; $\beta = 4.811238\times10^{-3}$ and $v = 1.442373\times10^{6}$ m/s (relative $10^{-6}$) from the cancellation-free form; the 10 light-second fixture ($\Delta t' = -7.5$ s, $\Delta x' = 12.5$ light-seconds).
- `worldChecks.relativity.test.ts`: aberration 20.4956 arcseconds from preset `sr-09-earth-orbit-aberration` ($v = 29.789$ km/s, relative $10^{-4}$), labeled a modern computation and never presented as Bradley's value; Fizeau coefficient 0.43722 for $n = 1.333$; transverse coefficients $1.5625m$ and $1.25m$ at $\beta = 0.6$; the Bradley comparison reads the card's transcribed value, never a literal.
- `copy.relativity.test.ts`: no evaluative words in Fork A (a) or Fork B (a) copy; the later-evidence text contains the shared-predictions statement.

### End-to-end tests

- `e2e/journey-iii.spec.ts`, run through the browser harness: walk every stage; operate SR-02 at the nagging fact; take both branches of both forks; construct the move; confirm that an observer change inside SR-03 does not restart its run; follow each source jump and return; enter through the arithmetic door and reach the same equation; answer exercises 1 and 3; complete the predict-perturb-explain task and reload; lanes keyboard only, 320 px, reduced motion, no WebGL, JavaScript disabled, WebKit.

### Structured logging

JSONL to `artifacts/test-logs/journey-iii/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `runId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `journeyId`, `stageId`, `forkId`, `branchId`, `outcomeType`, `doorId`, `instrumentId`, `instanceId`, `snapshotVersion`, `commandClass`, `quantityId`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `comparisonKind`, `constantSetId`, `executionLabel`, `resultStatus`, `browser`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `message`. Failing browser tests retain a screenshot, trace, DOM snapshot, and console log.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Never frame Lorentz or Poincaré as foolish; the fork outcomes and scope notes carry the nuance.
- Michelson–Morley is on the shelf, not presented as the documented sole cause of the paper.
- Contraction is not what a camera sees; optical appearance is a separate later deep dive.
- A consistency check is not a discriminating test; say which one each check is.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-disc-journey-iii-shelf-5z6q`: verified cards.
- `am-disc-journey-framework-umbg`: skeleton and route.
- `am-disc-exercise-checker-i4h2`: exercises.
- `am-disc-shelf-michelson-fizeau-dauq`: the Galilean substitution and the Fizeau shelf instrument.
- `am-sr-01-clock-sync-jbfn`, `am-sr-03-rod-simultaneity-0l5i`, `am-sr-04-lorentz-map-px1k`, `am-sr-05-moving-clocks-2zka`, `am-sr-06-velocity-composition-7ni4`, `am-sr-07-field-equations-xxes`, `am-sr-08-field-frame-change-5ibt`, `am-sr-09-doppler-aberration-rabd`, `am-sr-10-light-complex-kek0`, `am-sr-11-moving-mirror-wnz1`, `am-sr-12-charge-current-bgq0`, `am-sr-13-electron-dynamics-b6v7`: the stages' instruments.

Proposed additional prerequisites:

description:
# Author and verify the dated shelf cards for Journey III (relativity)

**Epic:** `am-ep-discovery-33u` · **Batch:** batch-e · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §5.1–5.4, §9.4, §3.9 (paper 3 margin), §22.1 (traceability only)

## Background

Journey III asks: how could you stop assuming that everyone shares the same time? Its shelf is the richest and the most dangerous for hindsight. By the end of 1904 Lorentz had the full transformation mathematics, and Poincaré had discussed the conventionality of simultaneity, described synchronization with light signals, and named the principle of relativity. The journey must show exactly what was on the table and what was different about taking both postulates physically, without ridiculing the ether program, which reproduces the formulas and is not declared refuted by the kinematics alone.

The relativity paper cites no one, so "the paper cites or asserts it" is almost always false here; the paper's own assertions (the magnet-and-conductor asymmetry, the unsuccessful attempts to detect motion relative to the light medium) are recorded as category-3 notes without implying citations. Einstein-knowledge evidence, when used, is cited separately: for example his later statements to R. S. Shankland that Fizeau's experiment and stellar aberration weighed more with him than Michelson–Morley.

Anachronism controls: Michelson–Morley is not the documented sole cause of the paper; spacetime diagrams are Minkowski's 1908 aid; the train-and-embankment picture is Einstein's 1917 illustration; contraction is not what a camera sees.

## Scope

In scope: one verified HistoricalPremise record per card below, with the fields and rules of `am-disc-knowledge-cards-iw8j`; the dynamo-context note; category-3 notes; Einstein-knowledge evidence where cited; the list of later items kept off the shelf.

Out of scope (owned elsewhere): card rendering and rules (`am-disc-knowledge-cards-iw8j`); the chain (`am-disc-journey-iii-chain-hpr7`); shelf instruments (`am-disc-shelf-michelson-fizeau-dauq`); the Fizeau, Kaufmann, Bucherer, and Ives–Stilwell datasets (`am-data-fizeau-1851-tgl8`, `am-data-kaufmann-1902-1906-52ya`, `am-data-bucherer-1908-w3mf`, `am-data-ives-stilwell-1938-61lp`); paper 3 margin entries (`am-sr-margin-entries-tn4l`); the Bern page's clock-coordination argument (`am-disc-bern-bridge-6euz`).

## Requirements

Store records under `content/historical-premises/` (journey-neutral card ids in lowercase kebab case; this bead's cards may be grouped in `content/historical-premises/relativity/`), with the standard fields and a verification record with an evidence locator.

| Card id | Date (`latestYear`) | Proposition | Limits to state | Status | Candidate citation (verify) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `galileo-1632-ship` | 1632 (1632) | The laws of mechanics look the same below decks whether the ship moves uniformly or not | Mechanics only | available | G. Galilei, *Dialogo* (1632), Second Day |
| `maxwell-1865-equations-ether-frame` | 1865, 1873 (1873) | Maxwell's equations, with light traveling at $c$ relative to the ether in the period's interpretation; they do not keep their form under $x' = x - vt$, $t' = t$ | The ether framing is interpretation; the change of form is demonstrated by the shelf instrument, not asserted | available | J. C. Maxwell, Phil. Trans. 155 (1865) 459; *Treatise* (1873) |
| `faraday-1832-induction` | 1831–1832 (1832) | Moving the magnet or moving the coil produces the same induced current for the same relative motion, while the theory of the period explains the two cases with two mechanisms | The same current to the precision of the observations; the two classical accounts agree to first order in $v/c$. The dynamo-patent remark is context, never evidence of Einstein's path. Category 3: the paper's introduction opens with this asymmetry | available | M. Faraday, Phil. Trans. 122 (1832) 125 |
| `bradley-1729-aberration` | 1729 (1729) | Stars show an annual aberration of about 20 arcseconds, explained by the finite speed of light combined with the Earth's orbital motion | Transcribe Bradley's printed figures: his ratio of light speed to the Earth's orbital speed (about 10 210 to 1) and light time from the Sun (about 8 minutes 12 seconds) correspond to about 20.2 arcseconds; the modern constant is 20.50 arcseconds (verify both before publishing) | available | J. Bradley, Phil. Trans. 35 (1727–1728, issued 1729) 637 |
| `fizeau-1851-drag` | 1851 (1851) | Light in moving water is dragged by about the fraction $1 - 1/n^2$ of the water's speed (Fresnel's coefficient) | Measured and explained within Fresnel's ether theory; not derived kinematically until later | available | H. Fizeau, C. R. 33 (1851) 349; extended account Ann. Chim. Phys. (3) 57 (1859) 385 |
| `michelson-1887-null-result` | 1881, 1887 (1887) | No ether wind is detected to second order in $v/c$ | A null result within the stated precision; the 1881 experiment's sensitivity was later questioned, and the 1887 experiment is the decisive one. Category 3: the paper's introduction refers in general terms to unsuccessful attempts to detect the Earth's motion relative to the light medium, without naming an experiment (verify wording) | available | A. A. Michelson, Am. J. Sci. (3) 22 (1881) 120; A. A. Michelson and E. W. Morley, Am. J. Sci. (3) 34 (1887) 333 |
| `fitzgerald-1889-contraction` | 1889, 1892 (1892) | Bodies moving through the ether contract along the motion by $\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}$, which would hide the wind | A dynamical hypothesis about bodies in the ether | available | G. F. FitzGerald, Science 13 (1889) 390; H. A. Lorentz, Versl. Kon. Akad. Wet. Amsterdam 1 (1892) 74 |
| `lorentz-1895-local-time` | 1895 (1895) | A fictitious "local time" $t' = t - vx/c^2$ makes the equations of moving systems correspond to those of systems at rest to first order in $v/c$ | First order; a calculational variable in Lorentz's framework | available | H. A. Lorentz, *Versuch einer Theorie der electrischen und optischen Erscheinungen in bewegten Körpern* (1895) |
| `poincare-1898-measure-of-time` | 1898 (1898) | The simultaneity of distant events is fixed by convention, chosen for convenience | Verify how explicitly the 1898 essay describes light-signal synchronization, and adjust the proposition to the text; the operational light-signal procedure for moving observers is the 1900 card | available | H. Poincaré, Rev. Métaphys. Morale 6 (1898) 1 |
| `poincare-1900-local-time` | 1900 (1900) | Lorentz's local time is what moving observers obtain when they synchronize clocks by exchanging light signals and assume equal travel times each way | The ether is retained | available | H. Poincaré, Arch. Néerl. (2) 5 (1900) 252 |
| `lorentz-1904-transformation` | 1904 (1904) | The full transformation with contraction, applied to a contractile electron, with the ether kept | A dynamical interpretation with local time as an auxiliary variable; the transformations of charge density and velocity were not yet exact (completed in Poincaré's June 1905 note) | available | H. A. Lorentz, Proc. R. Neth. Acad. Arts Sci. 6 (1904) 809 |
| `poincare-1904-st-louis` | 24 September 1904 (1904) | "The principle of relativity" named as one of the general principles of physics | A programmatic statement in a lecture | available | H. Poincaré, Bull. Sci. Math. (2) 28 (1904) 302 |
| `kaufmann-1901-electron-mass` | 1901–1903 (1903) | The inertia of fast electrons rises with speed; Abraham's rigid electron and Lorentz's contractile electron compete to explain it | The interpretation of the data was contested | available | W. Kaufmann, Nachr. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen (1901, 1902, 1903) (verify pages); M. Abraham, Ann. Phys. (4) 10 (1903) 105 |
| `poincare-1905-june-note` | 5 June 1905 (1905) | The group property of the transformations and corrected transformations of charge density and velocity | Appeared before the relativity paper's receipt (30 June 1905) but after the 1904 cutoff | parallel-work | H. Poincaré, C. R. 140 (1905) 1504 |

**Einstein-knowledge evidence to attach** (always category 2, always cited separately): R. S. Shankland's reports of conversations in which Einstein said that the observations of stellar aberration and Fizeau's measurements on light in moving water had influenced him most (R. S. Shankland, Am. J. Phys. 31 (1963) 47; verify), attached to the Fizeau and Bradley cards.

**Worth proposing (verify first):** W. Voigt (1887, Göttinger Nachrichten), a transformation that keeps the wave equation's form; J. Larmor (1897, 1900, *Aether and Matter*), a transformation to second order with time dilation. Either card is added only after its original is checked; both are available by 1904 and bear on what "the transformation was already known" means.

**Kept off the shelf** (timeline, margin, or world check only): Poincaré's Palermo paper (received July 1905, published 1906); Laue (1907), deriving Fizeau's coefficient from velocity addition; Minkowski (1908); Kaufmann's 1905–1906 data; Bucherer (1908); Einstein's 1917 train illustration; Lorentz's later acknowledgment that he had regarded local time only as an auxiliary quantity (*The Theory of Electrons*, 2nd ed., 1916; verify), which belongs in the margin; Ives–Stilwell (1938); muon lifetimes (1941); flown clocks (Hafele and Keating, flights in 1971, published 1972); satellite clocks.

## Technical Approach

- Write and verify the fourteen records; resolve the Kaufmann citations, the 1898 wording question, and Bradley's printed figures against the originals; record volume, pages, and dates exactly as printed.
- Where an original contradicts the plan's date or proposition, correct the card, record the difference in `verification.discrepancies`, and raise it with `br comments add`.
- Attach `admittedStages` from the Journey III record's stage ids; until those ids exist, list the intended stages by name (the nagging fact, two postulates, the measurement procedure, the Galilean test, simultaneity, Fork A, the move, the consequences, Fork B, waves and the light complex, charge and the electron, the world check).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Fourteen verified records exist with every standard field; the June 1905 Poincaré card is `parallel-work`.
- [ ] The Poincaré 1898 proposition matches the original text after verification.
- [ ] Bradley's card carries his printed figures, and the modern 20.50 arcseconds is identified as a modern value.
- [ ] Einstein-knowledge evidence appears only with its own citation and never merges with availability; category-3 notes never imply that the paper cites anyone.
- [ ] Later items are recorded for the timeline and margin and not attached to shelf stages.
- [ ] The shelf audit and anachronism lint pass (no "spacetime diagram," "Minkowski," "light cone," or "train and embankment" in card text outside labeled later-lens fields).

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `content/historical-premises/relativity/relativityShelf.test.ts`: schema validity; dates and statuses; verification records with evidence locators; journey-neutral id format; Einstein-knowledge evidence separate and cited; category-3 notes present on the Faraday and Michelson–Morley cards and containing no citation keys; the anachronism vocabulary scan; the Lorentz 1904 and FitzGerald cards contain none of a short list of evaluative words ("failed," "wrong," "mistaken," "naive").
- Compiler integration with the real card rules and epistemic checks: a fixture stage citing `poincare-1905-june-note` without acknowledgment is rejected, and accepted with it.

### End-to-end tests

- `e2e/journey-iii-shelf.spec.ts`, run through the browser harness once `/discover/special-relativity` renders the shelf: confirm date order and the parallel-work flag; open the Fizeau card and see the cited Shankland evidence as a separate section; open the Faraday card's "What the paper itself cites or asserts" section; JavaScript disabled and 320 px.

### Structured logging

JSONL to `artifacts/test-logs/journey-iii-shelf/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `cardId`, `latestYear`, `status`, `verified`, `verifierKind`, `hasEinsteinEvidence`, `hasCategory3Note`, `browser`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `outcome`, `message`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Treat Lorentz and Poincaré with precision and respect. The Lorentz cards must not be phrased as failures, and how far Poincaré's view departed from Lorentz's is a historians' question for the margin, with citations.
- Keep the dynamo-patent remark as context; Galison's argument about clock coordination belongs on the Bern page, labeled as an argument.
- That the equations do not keep their form under a Galilean substitution is demonstrated by the shelf instrument, not asserted.
- Checking a citation means looking at the scan page; never run OCR locally.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-disc-knowledge-cards-iw8j`: card schema, validators, and rendering.
- `am-cm-anachronism-lint-dl2`: card text is linted for unlabeled anachronisms.

Unblocks:
- `am-disc-journey-iii-chain-hpr7`: the chain cites these cards.
- `am-dod-relativity-105y`: the relativity definition of done requires every shelf card dated and sourced.
- `am-disc-desk-1904-9hgd` (proposed edge): the desk's premise catalogue lists every shelf card.

title: Build Journey IV: two ledgers, the fork, the check against the world, doors, and exercises
description:
# Build Journey IV: two ledgers, the fork, the check against the world, doors, and exercises

**Epic:** `am-ep-discovery-33u` · **Batch:** batch-d · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §9.1, §9.5, §8.4, §3.6, §7.2, §14.5 (traceability only)

## Background

Journey IV: **can emitting light change inertia?** Three printed pages make the argument short, and brevity makes a missing premise easy to hide, so this journey is reviewed with the same seriousness as the long ones. The route imports exactly one 1905 result with provenance, the relativity paper's §8 light-energy transformation, and never assumes its conclusion: the body's internal energies stay symbolic, and the additive-constant premise is stated as a premise rather than disguised as a theorem. The formula $E = mc^2$ does not appear in the paper; the paper says that a body giving off energy $L$ as radiation loses mass $L/V^2$.

The journey is labeled "A route you could take." Its shelf is "the end of 1904, plus paper 3."

## Scope

In scope: the complete Journey IV record `content/arguments/journeys/mass-energy.yaml` for `/discover/mass-energy`.

Out of scope (owned elsewhere): shelf cards (`am-disc-journey-iv-shelf-ff7g`); ME-01 to ME-03 and the 1906 box extension (`am-me-01-two-ledgers-g1re`, `am-me-02-coefficient-dtmi`, `am-me-03-system-boundary-0arb`, `am-me-03-box-extension-kiei`); the no-algebra entrance (`am-me-first-encounter-kejt`); energy-source card values (ME-03 and `massEnergy.ts`); placing the predict-perturb-explain task at the end of the reading chapter (`am-disc-ppe-teachback-wnp7`, which references this record).

## Requirements

**The nagging fact.** "A body that emits light in one direction recoils. If it emits equal pulses in opposite directions it does not recoil, and yet something about its motion has changed, because the two pulses carry different energies to a moving observer."

**The first honest question.** "If I already know how the energy of a light pulse changes between frames, what does energy conservation force me to say about the body that emitted it?"

**Admitted import.** The record lists `einstein-1905-light-complex-energy` in `admittedImports`, and every stage that uses it shows the import card with its provenance and a link to the relativity paper's §8.

### The chain (front door; ME-01, ME-02)

1. **The deliberately minimal experiment.** A body at rest emits two equal pulses in opposite directions; the symmetry removes recoil from the rest-frame bookkeeping and isolates an energy change.
2. **Two ledgers.** With $L$ the total emitted energy in the rest frame, $E_0, E_1$ the body's energies before and after in that frame, and $H_0, H_1$ in a frame moving at $v$: the pulses carry $\tfrac{L}{2}\gamma\left(1 - \tfrac{v}{c}\cos\varphi\right)$ and $\tfrac{L}{2}\gamma\left(1 + \tfrac{v}{c}\cos\varphi\right)$ in modern notation, summing to $\gamma L$ for every emission angle. The printed form uses $V$ for the speed of light and writes the factor as a square root; the concordance notes that Einstein's $\beta$ is the modern $\gamma$. Balances: $E_0 - E_1 = L$ and $H_0 - H_1 = \gamma L$.
   - Rotating the emission axis in ME-01 is a `setup-change` (a new identified run with a different emission geometry): the reader watches each pulse energy change while the sum $\gamma L$ does not.
   - Changing the moving observer's speed is an `observer-change`: the run id and event ids stay the same, and nothing restarts.
3. **The subtraction.** $(H_0 - E_0) - (H_1 - E_1) = L(\gamma - 1)$; every cancellation is a selectable operation. $E_0, E_1, H_0, H_1$ stay symbolic or carry explicitly arbitrary offsets that cancel; they are never initialized with $Mc^2$ or $\gamma Mc^2$.
4. **The stated premise.** Each frame-energy difference equals the kinetic energy plus the same additive constant before and after emission. The source asserts this; the cancellation is not an independent derivation of the assertion (the margin presents Ives 1952 and Stachel and Torretti 1982).
5. **The low-speed expansion with its domain visible (ME-02).** $K_0 - K_1 = L(\gamma - 1) \approx \tfrac12\frac{L}{c^2}v^2$. At $v = 0.6c$ the exact difference is $0.25L$ and the quadratic approximation $0.18L$; the reader moves toward low speed and watches the coefficient stabilize. Four outputs stay distinct: the exact difference; the quadratic approximation; the finite-speed proxy $2L(\gamma-1)/v^2$, which exceeds $L/c^2$ by about $\tfrac34(v/c)^2$ at small speed (1.3889 $L/c^2$ at $0.6c$); and the limiting coefficient $L/c^2$, a typed `analytic-limit` at $v = 0$.
6. **The move.** Identifying the limiting coefficient of $v^2/2$ as a mass loss of $L/c^2$ within the admitted premises, marked in the derivation chain. The page distinguishes the positive mass lost, $M_{\text{before}} - M_{\text{after}} = L/c^2$, from the signed change $\Delta M = -L/c^2$.
7. **The generalization.** The paper's statement that the mass of a body is a measure of its energy content, separated from the specific radiation argument and from the later modern formulation.

### The fork (after the move)

- (a) *Poincaré 1900:* the center-of-mass theorem fails for radiation unless the radiation is treated as a fictitious fluid carrying mass $E/c^2$. Worked honestly as bookkeeping. Outcome `empirically-equivalent-not-refuted`, with the scope note: "for the center-of-mass bookkeeping of emission and absorption treated in Poincaré's 1900 paper."
- (b) Energy itself has inertia. Outcome `papers-route`.

### Check it against the world (ME-03)

- **Framing.** These cards compute what the relation implies from cited modern energy values. They are consequences, not tests: the mass changes are far too small to weigh outside nuclear processes. The first quantitative nuclear checks (Cockcroft and Walton 1932; Bainbridge 1933) are dated later evidence on the timeline and are named here as such.
- **Cards,** each computed live by ME-03's owner from its cited value (with a build-time static worked example without JavaScript):
  - One radium-226 alpha decay releases about 4.87 MeV, so a mole of radium loses about 5.2 mg of mass in that single step. The paper's own remark was conditional: a test might succeed with bodies whose energy content varies strongly, such as radium salts.
  - The Sun radiates about $3.83\times10^{26}$ W, so it loses about $4.3\times10^{9}$ kg (about four million tonnes) every second.
  - Burning a kilogram of coal (about 24–35 MJ) loses $(2.7\text{–}3.9)\times10^{-10}$ kg, a few tenths of a microgram. The plan's "less than a nanogram" holds per gram, not per kilogram; the corrected figure is used.
  - A candle of about 80 W (a cited value stated as an assumption) loses about 3.2 ng per hour through the energy it emits.
  - A 100 W bulb running for a year loses about 35.1 μg.

### What Einstein actually wrote

Jumps to the paper's two-ledger passage, the subtraction and kinetic-energy identification, the low-speed expansion, the general statement, and the radium remark, each lighting its named weave predicate from the carried instrument state or showing the static pointer; the import card links to the relativity paper's §8.

### Doors

- **Front door:** the paper's argument above.
- **Side door, arithmetic (required):** the no-algebra entrance (`am-me-first-encounter-kejt`): two before-and-after accounting sheets with unknown internal quantities as covered boxes, where subtracting the sheets shows the inaccessible details are not needed. $Mc^2$ is never placed inside a covered box.
- **Side door, programmer (required):** the photon-in-a-box argument (`am-me-03-box-extension-kiei`). A box of mass $M$ and length $\ell$ recoils at $E/(Mc)$ for a time $\ell/c$ and shifts by $E\ell/(Mc^2)$, so mass $E/c^2$ must have moved with the light if the closed system's center of mass stays put. It is labeled "Einstein's 1906 argument, crediting Poincaré 1900," with its approximations stated (rigid box, nonrelativistic box motion, transit time $\ell/c$). The door's premises (radiation carries momentum $E/c$; the center-of-mass theorem for a closed system) are shelf cards; the 1906 paper is cited as the source of the route, never as a premise, and the argument is never merged into the 1905 ledger.
- All three doors arrive at the same equation id, the paper's mass-loss statement ($L/V^2$ in the printed notation), and the page says so.

### Exercises

Instrumented (four; the framework requires two to five):
1. **Mass lost by a 100 W bulb in a year** (numeric: $100 \times 3.156\times10^{7}$ J divided by $c^2$, about $3.5\times10^{-8}$ kg; reference from `massEnergy.ts`).
2. **Show the $\cos\varphi$ cancellation** (expression equivalence: $\tfrac12\gamma\left(1 - \tfrac{v}{c}\cos\varphi\right) + \tfrac12\gamma\left(1 + \tfrac{v}{c}\cos\varphi\right)$ against $\gamma$, with declared variables $\varphi \in [0, \pi]$ and $v/c \in [-0.95, 0.95]$).
3. **Compute the recoil displacement of the box** (numeric: $E\ell/(Mc^2)$ for the authored $E$, $\ell$, $M$ stated in the prompt; reference `photonInBox` in `massEnergy.ts`).
4. **What the finite-speed proxy is and is not** (numeric: at $0.6c$ the proxy is $2(0.25)/0.36 \approx 1.389\,L/c^2$ against the limit $L/c^2$; plus an explanation part).

Explanation item (one):
5. Explain why the equal-and-opposite emission was chosen.

### The predict-perturb-explain task (`ppeTask`)

- **Prompt:** "A body's unknown internal energy appears in both ledgers; which subtraction removes it, and which premise makes the subtraction useful?"
- **Predict:** the reader chooses which difference removes the unknown energies (candidates: $E_0 - E_1$; $H_0 - H_1$; $(H_0 - E_0) - (H_1 - E_1)$), stored locally and never scored.
- **Perturb:** in ME-01, use the premise probe ("the additive constant is allowed to change") and change the observer's speed, through the instrument's action contract, and watch which conclusion survives.
- **Explain:** an explanation part with comparison criteria (the unknown internal energies cancel in the difference of differences; the conclusion about mass needs the stated premise that each frame-energy difference is kinetic energy plus the same constant; relaxing the premise leaves the subtraction true but no longer about inertia).
- `am-disc-ppe-teachback-wnp7` places this same record at the end of the mass–energy reading chapter.

## Technical Approach

- Author the journey record referencing the shelf cards and the admitted import; ME-01 to ME-03 presets and the teaching tape "the two pulses"; the box extension's preset for the programmer door; derivation-chain step ids with the move marked (from `am-me-equations-0mgx`); weave predicates; exercises; the predict-perturb-explain task; the door equation id.
- World-check cards bind the exact quantity ids of ME-03's card outputs; no literals.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The journey validates as `complete`; its only post-1904 premise is the admitted import, shown with provenance.
- [ ] No ledger value is initialized with $Mc^2$ or $\gamma Mc^2$ (tested against the ME-01 snapshot).
- [ ] The additive-constant premise is stated as a premise.
- [ ] Exact, quadratic, proxy, and limit outputs are displayed distinctly, with $0.25L$ against $0.18L$ at $0.6c$.
- [ ] Rotating the emission axis creates a new identified run; changing the observer speed keeps run and event ids.
- [ ] The fork's branch (a) is labeled empirically equivalent within its stated scope and not refuted.
- [ ] Energy-source cards compute from cited values, are framed as consequences rather than tests, and the coal card shows the corrected magnitude; Cockcroft–Walton and Bainbridge appear as dated later evidence.
- [ ] Three doors end at the same equation id, the box door carries its 1906 label and credit, and the page states that the routes meet.
- [ ] Four instrumented exercises, one explanation item, and the predict-perturb-explain task work.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `content/arguments/journeys/massEnergy.test.ts`, with the real compiler, framework checks, and `massEnergy.ts`: validation as `complete`; the import rule; door equation ids; exercise roles and counts; references: 100 W for $3.156\times10^{7}$ s gives $3.5115\times10^{-8}$ kg; the proxy at $0.6c$ is 1.388889; the cancellation identity holds at the checker's sample points; `photonInBox` with $E = 1$ J, $\ell = 1$ m, $M = 1$ kg gives $1.11265\times10^{-17}$ m.
- `worldCheck.massEnergy.test.ts`: card mass changes derive from their cited inputs (radium 5.23 mg per mole; Sun $4.259\times10^{9}$ kg/s from $3.828\times10^{26}$ W; coal $2.670\times10^{-10}$ and $3.894\times10^{-10}$ kg for 24 and 35 MJ; candle 3.20 ng per hour at 80 W; bulb 35.1 μg; relative tolerance $10^{-3}$); an uncited card fixture is refused.
- `noncircularity.massEnergy.test.ts`: a historical ledger fixture initialized with $E_0 = Mc^2$ fails `circular-rest-energy`; the adversarial fixture "the low-speed proxy is the exact mass coefficient at every speed" fails at $0.6c$.
- `commandClasses.massEnergy.test.ts`: axis rotation yields a new `runId`; an observer speed change keeps `runId` and every event id and consumes nothing.

### End-to-end tests

- `e2e/journey-iv.spec.ts`, run through the browser harness: walk the ledgers; rotate the axis by typed entry and confirm the sum is unchanged; change the observer speed and confirm the run identity; select each cancellation; step toward low speed; take both fork branches; read the check cards and their framing; follow the import link to relativity §8 and back; enter through each side door and reach the same equation; answer exercises 1 and 2; complete the predict-perturb-explain task and reload; lanes keyboard only, 320 px, reduced motion, JavaScript disabled, WebKit.

### Structured logging

JSONL to `artifacts/test-logs/journey-iv/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `runId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `journeyId`, `stageId`, `forkId`, `branchId`, `outcomeType`, `doorId`, `instrumentId`, `instanceId`, `snapshotVersion`, `commandClass`, `quantityId`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `comparisonKind`, `constantSetId`, `executionLabel`, `resultStatus`, `browser`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `message`. Failing browser tests retain a screenshot, trace, DOM snapshot, and console log.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Do not begin by asserting that each pulse is "mass converted to energy."
- The mass of a closed system is conserved; the body's rest mass falls because energy left it.
- Two equal opposite pulses have nonzero invariant mass as a system; that is a later modern explanation, not a hidden premise of 1905.
- The 1906 box is a later argument and is labeled so; it never enters the 1905 ledger.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-disc-journey-iv-shelf-ff7g`: verified cards and the admitted import.
- `am-disc-journey-framework-umbg`: skeleton and route.
- `am-disc-exercise-checker-i4h2`: exercises.
- `am-me-01-two-ledgers-g1re`: the ledgers.
- `am-me-02-coefficient-dtmi`: the low-speed coefficient and the move.
- `am-me-03-system-boundary-0arb`: the check against the world.
- `am-me-first-encounter-kejt`: the arithmetic side door.
- `am-me-03-box-extension-kiei`: the programmer side door. That bead is labeled batch-h, but this batch-d journey and `am-dod-mass-energy-oxh2` both depend on it and its only prerequisite is ME-03; a relabel to batch-d is proposed.

Unblocks:
- `am-dod-mass-energy-oxh2`, `am-disc-cross-journey-exercises-j53n`, `am-tour-evening-and-course-5kcb`, `am-disc-batch-h-exit-audit-r8xq`.
- `am-disc-ppe-teachback-wnp7` (proposed edge): places this journey's predict-perturb-explain record.
