DNS records are DNS-only (grey cloud) at launch. **Nothing in the plan or in these beads authorizes changing DNS, connecting a domain, or deploying.** Every mode of the release script that deploys or moves an alias requires an authorization file quoting the user's explicit written authorization from the current conversation, and the DNS, scaffold deploy, preview, and launch steps are human gates.

## Scope and Children

- `am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt`: adapt the donor's `verified-production-deploy.ts`, `deployment-target.ts`, `deployment-verification.ts`, and smoke test into a tested, fail-closed release entry point with publication profiles (`scaffold`, `preview`, `launch`), modes (`--dry-run`, full release, `--candidate-only`, `--promote <deployment>`), authorization files, and gate selection from the shared registry. Writes code and tests only; never deploys.
- `am-rel-vercel-setup-ituk`: human gate. Create and link the Vercel project, record its protection and retention settings, pin its identity in the script, and deploy the empty scaffold to `annus-mirabilis-seven.vercel.app` (Batch A exit evidence).
- `am-rel-release-manifest-3gna`: generate and validate the release manifest, including a determinism digest that proves two builds of one commit carry the same content.
- `am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y`: run the full candidate check suite against the deployed, unpromoted assets.
- `am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre`: post-promotion smoke test, automatic coherent rollback, retention of verified deployments, and the cache and MIME policy.
- `am-rel-cloudflare-dns-e3tm`: human gate. Configure the Cloudflare zone for Vercel (apex and www, CAA, DNSSEC, null MX, SPF, DMARC, canonical redirect) and verify which deployment the attached domains serve.
- `am-rel-preview-policy-cf6g`: the honest public preview (complete Brownian and mass–energy papers, others clearly in preparation), shipped only after the license decision and only with authorization.
- Related, in `am-ep-later-gap`: `am-rel-cloudflare-hosting-experiment-n7re`, a bounded experiment that runs only for a concrete reason.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `bun scripts/verified-production-deploy.ts` is the only supported deploy path; its unit tests pass with fixed fixtures; direct `vercel deploy --prebuilt --prod` is documented as forbidden.
- [ ] The release script selects its gates from the shared gate registry by profile and refuses when a required step is unavailable.
- [ ] The empty site has deployed to `annus-mirabilis-seven.vercel.app` under recorded user authorization, closing the Batch A exit condition.
- [ ] Every candidate carries a schema-validated release manifest whose hashes match the deployed bytes and whose determinism digest identifies its content independently of when it was built.
- [ ] Candidate checks load all four complete paper texts, representative foundation pages, and every instrument bundle, and include one no-JavaScript source-text check, one accepted WASM result per numerical capability, and one deliberate typed refusal, all against deployed assets.
- [ ] The launch promotes exactly the audited candidate (`--promote`), after rerunning candidate checks against it.
- [ ] A post-promotion smoke test runs after every promotion and triggers a coherent rollback on failure.
- [ ] Rollback restores a matching site, content, and kernel set; old HTML never references incompatible new WASM; immutable content-addressed assets are cached long-term; manifests and HTML never reference a removed artifact; the project's retention settings keep every recorded rollback target and audited candidate.
- [ ] The Cloudflare zone matches §18.2 and was changed only under recorded authorization.
- [ ] No publication of the translation or new prose (preview, launch) happened before the license decision.
- [ ] No release step changes classic-patents.com; the two sites fail and recover independently.

## Sequencing

1. Batch A: `am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt` once the donor scripts are extracted (`am-scaf-extract-scripts-7jm`) and the gate registry exists (`am-scaf-quality-gates-ci-4xx`); then `am-rel-vercel-setup-ituk` under authorization.
2. Batch C (when content and the slim WASM artifact exist): `am-rel-release-manifest-3gna`, then `am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y`, then `am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre`.
3. Optional preview after the Brownian and mass–energy papers pass their definitions of done, the license decision is recorded, and the site surfaces it depends on exist: `am-rel-preview-policy-cf6g`.
4. Batch I: `am-rel-cloudflare-dns-e3tm` under authorization; `am-launch-readiness-audit-sc9b` deploys an unpromoted candidate with `--candidate-only`; `am-launch-final-product-test-nzhn` tests that candidate; `am-launch-public-release-5nkq` promotes it with `--promote`.

## Considerations

- The donor script hardcodes Classic Patents project ids, hostnames, Wright routes, and a lock port. Every constant is replaced, never copied; a copied project id would deploy to the wrong project. The forbidden identity list in `docs/DONOR_AUDIT.md` is scanned by tests.
- The donor clears `.next` before building. AGENTS.md Rule 1 forbids agents deleting files without written permission, so the adapted script either records the user's explicit approval for clearing its own build outputs or builds into a fresh per-release directory and proves freshness by timestamp.
- The donor runs its full source-reader sweep after moving aliases. The plan requires candidate validation before promotion, so the full sweep moves before promotion and only the short smoke test runs after.
- Shared `.next` and `.vercel/output` directories make concurrent builds and direct prebuilt deploys unsafe; the lock and conflicting-build scan exist for that reason.
- Some donor Vercel CLI calls (for example `vercel curl`) may not exist in the locked CLI version; the stack decision records availability and the scripts keep such calls behind one adapter with a documented replacement (the Deployment Protection bypass header, secret from an environment variable, never logged).
- Deleting a Vercel deployment requires the user's written permission (Rule 1 applies to remote artifacts too), and so does changing the project's deployment retention settings.
- Never require SharedArrayBuffer or cross-origin isolation (COOP/COEP) for the site to work; one dedicated worker per active heavy experiment suffices.

title: Experiment runtime: accepted snapshots, command classes, worker protocol, identities, tapes
description:
# Experiment runtime: accepted snapshots, command classes, worker protocol, identities, tapes

**Type:** epic · **Batch:** A (contracts) and B (scheduler, fallbacks, lifecycle, tapes, browser conformance) · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §12.5–12.11, §10.1, §10.6, §11.4, §16.4, §17.4, §19.4 "Experiment controller", §19.7 P0 (traceability only)

## Background

Every Annus Mirabilis instrument (33 core rows plus shelf instruments, the reasoning workbenches, and the Avogadro lab) runs on this runtime, so its contracts decide whether the site can be scientifically honest while interactive.

The donor museum's `src/physics/usePatentPhysics.ts` keeps module-global maps keyed by patent id (`listenersMap`, `stateMap`, `tickMap`, `changeMap`) and increments a control-change tick. That tick counts UI events, not solver steps. One global map per experiment id cannot host two independent instances of the same experiment, a frame change that must not restart the run, or a stochastic trajectory that must survive re-rendering and face switches. Annus Mirabilis needs all three: relativity instruments change observers without changing the world, Brownian ensembles must keep particle identities across 2D and 3D views and URL reloads, and inference instruments must hold observation data fixed while an estimator changes.

This epic replaces the ownership layer instead of patching it. The governing ideas:

- **Numerical truth has one owner.** A single owner advances or evaluates each laboratory instance and publishes immutable accepted snapshots. Plots, equations, scene geometry, tables, and accessibility summaries all consume the same snapshot. React components format quantities and project accepted coordinates into pixels; they never recompute diffusion, transformed coordinates, or emitted energy from slightly different parameter copies.
- **A change of description is not a change of world.** Six executable command classes keep observer, measurement, estimator, and presentation changes from restarting experiments or consuming randomness.
- **Stale work never overwrites newer work, for every kind of change.** Every command receives a per-instance logical `actionIndex`. Physical inputs (`inputRevision`) and descriptions (`observerRevision`, `measurementRevision`, `estimatorRevision`) each have requested and accepted counters, and publication is ordered by `(acceptedActionIndex, stepIndex)`. Checking `runId` and `inputRevision` alone is not enough: a late response for an older frame speed has the same run and the same physical inputs as a newer one, and without the action index it would put coordinates for 0.6c beneath a 0.8c label.
- **A result is not always a number.** Typed output statuses (`value`, `symbolic`, `analytic-limit`, `underdetermined`, `not-applicable`, `outside-domain`), typed request refusals that keep the last legal state, and separate execution outcomes replace `NaN`, infinity, zero, and silent clamps.
- **Determinism is stated precisely and fallbacks do not lie.** Reproducibility holds for the same admitted model, executable, parameters, constant set, seed, stream semantics, and logical actions. Execution labels are earned per accepted snapshot.
- **Identities survive JavaScript.** 64-bit seeds and draw indices travel as canonical decimal strings, never as rounded JSON numbers.

Shared vocabulary used by every child (defined in the first child that needs it and imported by the rest): the identity set and `ExperimentView` read model (`am-rt-snapshot-store-aft`); the command envelope, revision effects, and scientific digests (`am-rt-command-classes-dzp`); output statuses, request refusals, refusal codes, execution outcomes, and uncertainty kinds (`am-rt-typed-results-mqb`); the `U64` type and stream allocation registry (`am-rt-u64-identities-7ce`). `renderTime` belongs to the runtime identity set but lives in a per-view frame record, never inside an immutable snapshot, because it advances every display frame. `simulatedTime` is a canonical SI time for time-evolving runs and an explicit `not-time-evolving` marker for closed-form evaluations, never a stand-in zero.

## Scope and Children

- `am-rt-snapshot-store-aft`: the instance-scoped accepted-snapshot store, the placement-keyed instance registry that lets a face switch reattach to a running owner, the full identity set with ordering rules, `useSyncExternalStore` stability, and the runtime fixture runner `scripts/e2e-runtime-contracts.ts`.
- `am-rt-command-classes-dzp`: `setup-change`, `physical-intervention`, `observer-change`, `measurement-change`, `estimator-change`, `presentation-change` as executable command types with revision effects, invariants, canonical scientific digests, and replay-grid rules.
- `am-rt-typed-results-mqb`: output statuses, request refusals with domain kinds and the refusal-code registry, execution outcomes, partial-result rules, uncertainty kinds, and reader-facing explanations.
- `am-rt-u64-identities-7ce`: unsigned 64-bit seeds and draw indices through JSON, URLs, `BigInt`, and WASM, plus the logical stream allocation registry whose kernel ids mirror the FrankenSim binding decision.
- `am-rt-worker-protocol-gaq`: the versioned request, response, refusal, and execution-outcome schema with a strict, context-aware decoder and a reusable conformance suite.
- `am-rt-worker-scheduler-7tl`: dedicated worker loading, host and WASM worker entries, bounded chunks, coalescing, supersession, stale rejection, bounded recovery, and performance marks.
- `am-rt-determinism-fallbacks-8i4`: the reproducibility contract, the four public execution labels derived from accepted provenance, engine selection, and truthful fallbacks.
- `am-rt-memory-lifecycle-5ws`: buffer ownership, WASM memory-growth safety, disposal, visibility pausing, concurrency limits, degradation policy, and checkpoint-validated recovery.
- `am-rt-control-tapes-0gc`: control tapes with model identity, command-class events ordered by `actionIndex`, prediction events, digests, compatibility refusals, and the teaching-tape format and audit.
- ``am-rt-browser-conformance-09i5``: the runtime's browser conformance lanes against runtime fixture experiments and the pinned slim artifact, in every supported engine, so the §19.4 closure is proven in real browsers before any instrument depends on it.

Out of scope: the numerical laws themselves (`am-ep-reference-sln` and `am-ep-frankensim-9kg`), instrument controls and views (`am-ep-instruments-8gi`), page composition (`am-ep-reader-k0z`), and the paper journeys that re-assert runtime contracts on real instruments (`am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu` and the later paper e2e beads).

## Success Criteria

- [ ] The §19.4 closure for the experiment controller holds in real browsers, first on runtime fixtures (``am-rt-browser-conformance-09i5``) and then on BM-01, BM-05, and BM-06 (`am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu`): a stale response is rejected; two instances of one experiment are independent; an observer change preserves the run; a measurement change preserves the latent path.
- [ ] Every rendered view exposes the full identity set: `instanceId`, `runId`, `inputRevision` and `acceptedInputRevision`, the observer, measurement, and estimator revisions (requested and accepted), `actionIndex` and `acceptedActionIndex`, `stepIndex`, `simulatedTime`, `snapshotVersion`, `renderTime` (frame record), `modelVersion` and `artifactDigest`, `seed` and `streamVersion`, and no view reads physics from anywhere else.
- [ ] Numerical, graphical, equation, and tabular views of one instance display identical `data-snapshot-version` values (asserted end to end).
- [ ] No late response for any command class (physical, observer, measurement, or estimator) can replace a newer accepted snapshot; this is tested with out-of-order responses in Bun workers and in browsers.
- [ ] Face changes, 2D and 3D switches, remounts, and route transitions within a page never restart a running experiment, mount a second owner, or consume new randomness.
- [ ] Every non-numeric outcome is a typed output status, a typed request refusal that keeps the last legal state, or an execution outcome, each with an ordinary-language explanation and a next action; no `NaN`, infinity, or zero stands in for any of them, and no numerical-scheme or budget refusal is worded as a physical impossibility.
- [ ] Seeds survive JSON and URL round trips at and above $2^{53}$ and at $2^{64} - 1$; invalid seeds are refused.
- [ ] Worker refusal, unavailable WASM, stale responses, context loss, crashes, and restart never produce false results, and the static book stays readable throughout.
- [ ] The execution label says "Ideal model, computed with FrankenSim" only when an accepted FrankenSim result produced the displayed snapshot.
- [ ] Control tapes replay to the same scientific digest for the same model, seed, stream version, constant set, and logical actions; the teaching-tape format, validator, and audit exist; "Einstein's 0.8 micron" exists for the reference slice, and the audit enforces the other four named tapes as their instruments register.
- [ ] Every child has a Bun end-to-end suite in `scripts/e2e-runtime-contracts.ts` that runs without a browser, and every runtime suite writes JSONL through the shared logger from `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`.

## Sequencing

1. **Batch A contracts.** `am-rt-snapshot-store-aft` first (after the scaffold, the donor runtime-utility extraction, and the logging library). Then `am-rt-typed-results-mqb`, followed by `am-rt-command-classes-dzp` (command refusals such as `off-replay-grid` use the shared refusal shape). `am-rt-u64-identities-7ce` runs in parallel with the store once the scaffold, the logging library, the experiment schemas, and the FrankenSim capability audit exist (its kernel ids mirror the audit's stream-key decision). `am-rt-worker-protocol-gaq` follows typed results and identities; the slim WASM artifact's malformed-output checks use its decoder.
2. **Batch B execution.** `am-rt-determinism-fallbacks-8i4` after the slim artifact exists (it adds the "fallback label is never FrankenSim" check to `scripts/verify-wasm-artifacts.ts`). `am-rt-worker-scheduler-7tl` after determinism, the protocol, and command classes, then `am-rt-memory-lifecycle-5ws`. `am-rt-control-tapes-0gc` runs in parallel with the scheduler once command classes, identities, and the extracted donor tape exist. ``am-rt-browser-conformance-09i5`` runs last, after the e2e harness, the scheduler, memory lifecycle, tapes, determinism, and the slim artifact.
3. All ten children must be real, tested, and used by BM-01, BM-05, and BM-06 before the Brownian reference slice can exit (`am-bm-slice-exit-demo-5922`, which consumes both the conformance evidence and the slice journey).

## Considerations

- This is P0 innovation work (§19.7): "Typed results, exact identities, command classes, and safe snapshot ownership." Expand beyond the slice's needs only after a changed observer demonstrably preserves the world and stale results and rounded seeds demonstrably cannot corrupt it.
- Implement the contracts completely but keep APIs minimal until `am-bm-slice-retrospective-pp09` shows which abstractions helped. Do not invent a general simulation framework. Every identity field is implemented now, because later retrofits of identity break replay and permalinks.
- **Closable acceptance.** A child's acceptance criteria never require an instrument that depends on that child. Each child proves its contract with runtime fixture experiments in Bun and lists the browser assertions ``am-rt-browser-conformance-09i5`` runs and the instrument-level obligations `am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu` re-asserts.
- **Donor reuse with known traps** (from `am-scaf-extract-runtime-utilities-99y`, at the pinned donor revision):
  - `controlTape.ts` seeds its host digest with `(2166136261 ^ seed ^ tick) >>> 0`, so seeds are coerced to 32 bits and seeds differing only above bit 32 collide; its `seed` is a JavaScript number and its events carry a UI `tick`. The adapted tape hashes canonical bytes and uses `actionIndex`.
  - `transport.ts` offers a `"shared-memory"` buffer mode and `BoundedBufferPool(…, useSharedMemory)`, and exports a module-global `globalTransportBus`. The runtime never requires `SharedArrayBuffer` or cross-origin isolation and never routes instance state through a global bus.
  - `BoundedBufferPool.acquire` evicts the oldest active lease under pressure. That is incompatible with buffers exposed by published immutable snapshots; snapshot buffers are reference-counted and never evicted.
  - `genericWasm.ts` keeps a module-global `source` that flips to `"wasm"` after a module loads. Labels derive from accepted snapshot provenance instead.
  - `tickScheduler.ts` re-anchors when the backlog exceeds `maxCatchup` (default 3), silently dropping ticks. Dropping display frames is fine; scientific stepping is driven by executed logical steps, so re-anchoring slows playback (shown to the reader) and never skips simulated time.
- A placement-keyed registry of instance-scoped stores is not the donor's global map: it maps a stable placement (route, anchor, experiment, slot) to one instance so a remount reattaches, while two placements of the same experiment get two independent instances.
- Never require `SharedArrayBuffer` or cross-origin isolation for the first version.
- `Math.random` never appears in a frame loop or scientific path. Host-fed time comes through the tick scheduler; render time is never a physical input.

title: Application scaffold, donor extraction, and quality gates
description:
# Application scaffold, donor extraction, and quality gates

**Type:** epic · **Batch:** A · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §2.3, §2.4, §15.1, §15.2, §16.4, §17.3, §19.1; AGENTS.md Rule 2 (traceability only)

## Background

Batch A of the delivery plan (§19.1) asks for a working, empty application before any visual polish: create the repository, copy the proven donor modules named in the reuse table (§2.3), and get `typecheck`, `lint`, `build`, and the architecture test green with an empty corpus. This epic delivers that foundation. Every later epic (content model, reader, runtime, instruments, test infrastructure, design, accessibility, release) builds on it.

The foundation follows four constraints from the plan and AGENTS.md:

1. **Start from a small, attributable extraction, not a fork.** Copy only the donor files the reuse table names, from the revision pinned in `docs/DONOR_AUDIT.md`, with the attribution header template recorded there, including the OpenAI/Anthropic rider language; strip patent-specific logic and every donor identity (hostnames, Vercel project ids, the lock port, third-party origins); port their tests. A shared "museum framework" is extracted only after a second concrete use establishes its interface.
2. **App Router purity is a build gate.** A `src/pages` directory (even empty), a second App Router root, legacy Pages Router file names, or rogue scratch files in the root or source tree corrupt Next.js static generation and route manifests or clutter the repository; the architecture gate makes that impossible to ship.
3. **The book is static-first.** The initial reading route never pulls in Three.js, pdf.js, or WASM; the scaffold's layout and home page stay light so later budgets (first-route JavaScript at most 200 KiB compressed) are reachable. One shared check proves the absence from the first build onward.
4. **One gate registry.** Local runs, CI, and the release script run the same named gate steps; a step that does not exist yet reports `not-available`, never `passed`, and a release profile refuses when a step it requires is not available.

## Scope and Children

- `am-scaf-nextjs-app-bu2`: the Next.js App Router application with strict TypeScript, Biome, Bun tests, pinned Node.js and Bun versions, the planned directory layout, error and not-found routes, an honest placeholder home page, and the shared initial-route graph check `scripts/perf/initialRouteGraph.ts`; builds with an empty corpus.
- `am-scaf-architecture-gate-l1p`: the architecture test that fails on `src/pages`, a second app root, App Router special files outside `src/app`, legacy Pages Router file names, unapproved root files, and scratch files in the source tree.
- `am-scaf-extract-runtime-utilities-99y`: attributable extraction of the donor's physics utilities (control tape, tick scheduler, transport, parameter aliases, generic WASM loader, units, intervals, energy ledger, coverage manifest, spec-clause weave, WASM artifact test helpers).
- `am-scaf-extract-ui-components-c31`: attributable extraction of donor UI seams (LaTeX renderer, colorized equation starting point, PDF facsimile viewer, Three.js studio, chrome, theme toggle, search palette, Open Graph routes, error boundaries, robots, sitemap), with every third-party request stripped.
- `am-scaf-extract-scripts-7jm`: attributable extraction of the donor's verified release scripts and browser-acceptance contract with their tests, neutralized so they cannot touch the donor's domains.
- `am-scaf-quality-gates-ci-4xx`: the typed gate registry, the local runner (`bun run gates`), release-profile requirements, and the GitHub Actions workflow, which never deploys.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `bun run format:check`, `bun run test`, and `bun run build` pass on a fresh clone with an empty corpus, using the Node.js and Bun versions pinned in `package.json`.
- [ ] The architecture gate runs before every build and fails with an actionable message on each violation class.
- [ ] Every extracted donor file carries the attribution header from `docs/DONOR_AUDIT.md`, and its donor path and pinned revision are recorded in that document's "Extracted files" section.
- [ ] No string from the forbidden donor identity list appears outside attribution comments, and no item from the do-not-port list (patent claims, disputes, categories, lineages, era filters, broadsides, narration player, iOS app, wizard reports, Wright-default dispatch) exists in the repository.
- [ ] The gate chain runs locally and in GitHub Actions on push and pull request, retains logs on failure, reports unavailable steps honestly, and never deploys.
- [ ] `scripts/perf/initialRouteGraph.ts` proves the initial route's dependency graph contains no Three.js, pdf.js, or WASM, and fails on a seeded import.

## Sequencing

1. `am-scaf-nextjs-app-bu2` first (needs `am-gov-decision-stack-versions-6ax`).
2. Then in parallel: `am-scaf-architecture-gate-l1p`, `am-scaf-extract-runtime-utilities-99y`, `am-scaf-extract-ui-components-c31`, `am-scaf-extract-scripts-7jm` (the extractions also need `am-gov-donor-audit-0wa`).
3. `am-scaf-quality-gates-ci-4xx` after the architecture gate.

Downstream consumers unblocked by this epic include `am-cm-id-scheme-8bn`, `am-rt-snapshot-store-aft`, `am-rt-u64-identities-7ce`, `am-read-shell-routes-3ua`, `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`, `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh` (after the script extraction and the gate registry), `am-design-themes-typography-288q`, `am-a11y-baseline-1cg5`, `am-plat-local-storage-km8f`, `am-fs-slim-artifact-0yh`, `am-src-download-script-15ar`, `am-src-ocr-orchestrator-u1e0`, `am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt`, `am-edit-voice-lint-trmf`, `am-cm-audit-scripts-d34`, and ``am-gov-license-inventory-w6yz``.

## Considerations

- Extraction is not a license to port patent concepts under new names; every extracted module must fit the argument-centered content model or be left behind with a recorded reason.
- The three extraction beads and the architecture gate run in parallel and all record rows in `docs/DONOR_AUDIT.md`; each appends only to its own subsection and reserves the file through Agent Mail while editing.
- Keep generated artifacts out of the repository root; scratch work belongs in a session scratch directory.
- Commands named in README.md and AGENTS.md must match the scripts this epic creates; update those documents in the same change if names differ (including `bun run gates`).
- Tests in this epic follow the donor's practice of fixed fixtures and never create or delete temporary files (AGENTS.md Rule 1).

title: Facsimiles, rights, provenance receipts, cloud OCR drafts, and reviewed German ledgers
description:
# Facsimiles, rights, provenance receipts, cloud OCR drafts, and reviewed German ledgers

**Epic:** (top level) · **Batch:** starts in Batch A and continues in parallel with implementation · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §3.1, §3.2, §4.1–§4.4, §4.6, §17.2, §17.3, §19.1 (traceability only)

## Background

Annus Mirabilis is an interactive critical edition of Einstein's four 1905 *Annalen der Physik* papers (plus the dissertation as a companion record). Every later layer of the site (the German edition, the English translation, the four readings, the semantic equations, the instruments, the discovery journeys) points back to an exact passage in a pinned historical source. If the source layer is wrong, unpinned, or of unclear rights status, everything built on it inherits the defect, and a scientific edition cannot recover its credibility by polishing the explanations.

This epic owns the bottom of the stack, inherited from the Classic Patents source-edition system and made stricter because the edition is bilingual and mathematical:

1. **Rights**: a written policy and a controlled vocabulary so each asset (scan, translation, prose, code, font, dataset) carries its own rights status, publication decision, and a separate determination of whether its page images may be sent to a cloud OCR service. The German texts are public domain; scans are not the text; existing English translations are not reused.
2. **Surveyed and pinned facsimiles**: candidate scans researched and classified before any code exists, then one immutable scan per document pinned in a fixed order of preference, with SHA-256, host checksums, page count, and a provenance receipt written before any editorial copy.
3. **Provenance receipts in one format**: machine-readable front matter plus required sections, checked by one checker, extended by later beads, and compiled into `/sources`.
4. **Cloud OCR drafts**: bounded, checkpointed jobs on cloud GPT-5.6 Luna workers through a documented, user-authorized interface, and only for scans whose terms permit it. **OCR never runs on the development host**, with no exceptions and no local fallback. OCR output is research evidence only.
5. **Reviewed German ledgers**: diplomatic transcriptions, corrected line by line against page images with every equation retyped by the editor, then read completely a second time. Agents record correction and the second read; the status "reviewed" comes only from the human-gated German source review in `am-ep-editions-1wa`. The ledger is comparison evidence with page markers; the visitor-facing German edition is built from it in `am-ep-editions-1wa`.

Completeness is never a hand-maintained percentage. It is measured against the per-paper source manifests that `am-ep-editions-1wa` builds from these assets.

## Scope and Children

- `am-src-rights-policy-1dp`: rights and attribution policy plus the `SourceAsset` rights, publication, and cloud-processing vocabulary.
- Proposed scan-survey bead (slug `am-src-scan-survey-sqnu`): candidate scans, verbatim terms, legibility, identifiers, and witnesses for the four papers, before any code.
- `am-src-download-script-15ar`: `scripts/download-facsimiles.ts`, which fetches, verifies, and pins scans and refuses to replace a pinned file.
- Proposed receipt-format bead (slug `am-src-receipt-format-npo5`): the receipt format, checker, survey check, and generated-section writer.
- `am-src-ocr-dispatch-interface-m1ur`: the human-gated record of how cloud OCR is dispatched, at what cost, with what data handling, and with what authorization.
- `am-src-ocr-orchestrator-u1e0`: `scripts/ocr-ledgers.ts`, the provider-independent orchestration of bounded cloud OCR jobs, which can never run OCR locally.
- Proposed adapter bead (slug `am-src-ocr-cloud-adapter-7wa1`): the concrete cloud adapter and its single authorized smoke call.
- `am-src-facsimile-light-quanta-t4n`, `am-src-facsimile-brownian-mox`, `am-src-facsimile-relativity-kav`, `am-src-facsimile-mass-energy-cat`: pin each paper's scan and write its provenance receipt (`ap-17-132`, `ap-17-549`, `ap-17-891`, `ap-18-639`).
- `am-src-facsimile-dissertation-2mp`: the companion dissertation `ap-19-289` and its 1911 correction `ap-34-591`, only after the companion decision.
- `am-src-ocr-light-quanta-k8w`, `am-src-ocr-brownian-n6q`, `am-src-ocr-relativity-8ty`, `am-src-ocr-mass-energy-3yo`: cloud OCR drafts per paper.
- `am-src-ledger-light-quanta-sxi`, `am-src-ledger-brownian-8cw`, `am-src-ledger-relativity-sby`, `am-src-ledger-mass-energy-z7z`: hand-corrected diplomatic ledgers per paper.
- `am-src-ledger-dissertation-ppm7`: scoped cloud OCR drafts and ledgers for the dissertation and its correction, if the companion ships.

Out of scope: source inventories, German edition blocks, translation, alignment, gloss, and translation and German source review (`am-ep-editions-1wa`); schema code (`am-cm-schemas-source-1en`); the facsimile viewer (`am-read-facsimile-face-er0`); the public `/sources` page (`am-design-sources-about-zumd`); review records and the generated editorial acceptance section of receipts (`am-edit-review-records-hofz`); the companion record itself (`am-companion-dissertation-record-nbvv`).

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `docs/RIGHTS.md` and `docs/rights-vocabulary.yaml` exist with the rights, publication, and cloud-processing vocabularies and their constraints, and every pinned asset record uses them.
- [ ] A survey record exists for each of the four papers before its pin, with verbatim terms, proposed classifications, legibility checks, confirmed identifiers, and witness availability.
- [ ] Each of the four papers has a pinned facsimile and a receipt that passes the receipt checker: SHA-256, host checksums where listed, page count, source URL, verbatim terms, retrieval date, rights fields, embedded text layer status, a complete page map, and witnesses including German Wikisource availability.
- [ ] No pinned file was ever replaced or deleted; `download-facsimiles.ts` refuses replacement and its tests prove it; `--verify` passes for every published asset, and local-only assets are verified on the host that holds them.
- [ ] Every OCR draft came from a cloud job recorded in the receipt (job ids, page ranges, worker identity, model, dates), and only for scans recorded as `cloudProcessing: permitted`. No local OCR process was ever started.
- [ ] Each paper has a ledger at `public/papers/transcripts/<key>-reviewed.txt` (or the recorded non-public location if scan terms forbid redistribution of derived page text, which should not arise for public-domain text) that passes `am-edn-ledger-validator-edv`, with all mathematics retyped and compared against page images, a complete second read recorded, and `ledgerStatus: corrected-second-read` in the receipt. The status becomes `reviewed` only when the human German source review records acceptance.
- [ ] Printed constants, numbers, and glyphs are transcribed from the facsimile, never from memory (for example $\alpha = 6.10\times10^{-57}$ and $\beta = 4.866\times10^{-11}$ in the light paper; $k = 1.35\times10^{-2}$ and $N = 6\times10^{23}$ in the Brownian paper; the electron mass written $\mu$ in §10 of the relativity paper).
- [ ] The Batch A exit evidence holds for the source layer: every original source unit has a pinned, locatable source.

## Sequencing

1. Immediately and in parallel: `am-src-rights-policy-1dp`, and `am-src-ocr-dispatch-interface-m1ur`, whose request goes to the user on day one because only the user can answer it.
2. After the rights policy, and in parallel with the donor audit, stack decision, and scaffold: the scan survey (no code needed).
3. After `am-scaf-nextjs-app-bu2`, in parallel: `am-src-download-script-15ar`, the receipt-format bead, and `am-src-ocr-orchestrator-u1e0`.
4. After the orchestrator and the user's dispatch details: the adapter bead and its single authorized smoke call.
5. After the survey, the download script, and the receipt format: the four facsimile beads in parallel. The Brownian paper is the most urgent (it feeds the Batch B reference slice), then mass–energy (smallest, first complete paper), then relativity and light quanta. The three volume-17 papers may share one parent scan.
6. OCR drafts per paper after its facsimile and the adapter; ledgers per paper after the OCR draft and `am-edn-ledger-validator-edv`.
7. `am-src-facsimile-dissertation-2mp` waits for `am-gov-decision-companion-at-launch-936`, `am-src-ledger-dissertation-ppm7` follows it, and neither ever delays the four papers.

Transcription work for all four papers proceeds in parallel with implementation from Batch A onward, using the ids frozen by the inventories.

## Considerations

- The facsimile is immutable once pinned. The bibliographic key, PDF filename, ledger filename, edition files, and receipt must match. Diagnose a surprising reading; never swap the scan.
- A host's possession of a scan is not a rights determination. Record every stated terms statement verbatim. Host metadata about the underlying work's copyright status is not a license for the scan.
- US public domain covers works published in 1930 or earlier as of 2026 (the plan's "before 1929" wording is outdated but not wrong); life-plus-70 terms for Einstein (died 1955) expired at the end of 2025. Recheck at publication; the papers themselves are unaffected.
- Parsed PDF text layers are frequently unreliable for these scans and are never accepted for an equation. Many library scans embed the host's own OCR text; receipts record its presence, and project scripts never read it.
- Hosts regenerate derived files; pins prefer original uploads and record host checksums.
- Identifier traps found while planning: Crossref records `10.1002/andp.200590007` as the 2005 reissue of the light-quanta paper, not of the mass–energy paper as plan §3.1 says; microfilm items label segments as "issues" that differ from the journal's issue numbers; as of 2026-09-14 German Wikisource transcribes only the relativity paper, so receipts record witness absence explicitly.
- Human gates in this epic: the dispatch interface, every `cloudProcessing: unknown` case, and ledger acceptance. Machine drafts never self-certify.

title: Test infrastructure: structured logging, browser acceptance harness, lanes
description:
# Test infrastructure: structured logging, browser acceptance harness, lanes

**Type:** epic · **Batch:** A (harness core), B (the slice real-device check), I (the pre-launch device check) · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §2.2, §13.1, §13.4, §16.4, §17.1, §17.3, §17.4, §17.6 (traceability only)

## Background

A release must answer five questions separately: is the historical text complete and accurate; is the explanation mathematically and physically sound; does the instrument calculate and display the stated model correctly; can a visitor operate and understand the actual page; does the explanation help a reader overcome the intended obstacle (§17.1). No single artifact answers all five. This epic supplies the shared machinery for the third and fourth questions: a structured logging standard every unit and browser suite uses, a real-browser acceptance harness adapted from the donor's vertical-slice design, and the real-device checks that emulation cannot replace. The donor design checks source identities, exact routes, URL-restored views, actual controls, refusal behavior, 320-pixel screens, keyboard and touch, reduced motion, and retained failure evidence, while never pretending browser checks replace numerical or editorial review (§2.2).

The logging standard exists because failures in this project are often subtle: a stale snapshot shown under new labels, a seed rounded through JSON, a fallback labeled as WASM, a tolerance that is relative near a true zero. Diagnosing those requires every test to record identities, seeds, expected and actual values, tolerances, comparison kinds, and the execution label, in one machine-readable format. Two rules keep that format unambiguous: `logRunId` identifies one execution of a suite and names its file (`artifacts/test-logs/<suite>/<log-run-id>.jsonl`), while `logRunId` always means an experiment realization as defined by the runtime contract and appears only when an experiment is involved; and tolerance verdicts come from the single tolerance module `src/units/tolerance.ts`, never from a second formula in test helpers.

The harness must exist early. Themes, accessibility, reader, equation, and platform beads in Batches A and B all verify their work "through the harness," so the harness cannot wait for the reader shell. It therefore self-tests on static fixture pages that implement a documented DOM readiness contract, and the real pages adopt that contract as they are built.

## Scope and Children

- `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`: the JSONL test logging library, the event schema (with `logRunId` distinct from `logRunId`), bitwise and tolerance assertion helpers that delegate tolerance verdicts to `src/units/tolerance.ts` (delivered by ``am-ver-tolerance-module-ho90``), evidence fields, and the log summarizer.
- `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: the Playwright paper acceptance harness with every lane, the DOM readiness contract, contract primitives and reusable page and instrument checks self-tested on static fixtures, production-build serving, tested evidence retention, the CLI, and its CI workflow.
- ``am-test-real-device-slice-check-bize``: a real-device check of the Brownian reference slice on a low-cost Android phone and an iPhone with Safari, before the shared reader and equation architecture is frozen, including the CPU-slowdown calibration measurement for the `mobile-low-cost` profile (human gate).
- `am-test-real-device-check-iju4`: the small real-device check of all four papers on low-cost Android and iPhone Safari before launch (human gate).

Consumers: `am-ver-scenario-registry-om3`, `am-ver-statistical-policy-grj`, `am-ref-constants-xik`, `am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu`, `am-me-e2e-qbbm`, `am-srk-e2e-4qkd`, `am-lq-e2e-x7z0` (and through them `am-bm-e2e-complete-gmdb` and `am-sre-e2e-xmj6`), `am-plat-perf-budgets-s3ww`, `am-plat-resource-stress-9zgu`, `am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y`, and the reader, design, equation, accessibility, and platform beads whose end-to-end tests run through the harness (for example `am-read-shell-routes-3ua`, `am-design-themes-typography-288q`, `am-a11y-baseline-1cg5`, `am-eq-static-katex-7da`).

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Unit, scenario, and browser suites write JSON lines with the fields defined in AGENTS.md "Testing and Logging Standards" to `artifacts/test-logs/<suite>/<log-run-id>.jsonl`, and the schema rejects a test-run id placed in `logRunId`.
- [ ] Numeric assertions state their tolerance and comparison kind, log both values, take tolerance verdicts from `src/units/tolerance.ts`, and compare bitwise values by exact bit pattern.
- [ ] The harness runs against a production build in every lane: desktop, tablet, 320-pixel touch, WebKit, keyboard-only, reduced motion, high zoom, no WebGL, JavaScript disabled, and print.
- [ ] The DOM readiness contract is documented in `docs/PAPER_E2E_HARNESS.md`, and readiness is semantic (ready markers and accepted snapshot attributes), never sleep-based.
- [ ] Failing browser tests retain a screenshot, trace, DOM snapshot, console log, and network log, and the failure-reporting path itself is tested.
- [ ] A real-device check of the reference slice is recorded before `am-bm-slice-retrospective-pp09` freezes the shared architecture, and a real-device check of all four papers is recorded with devices, tester, date, and findings before launch.

## Sequencing

1. `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp` first (needs `am-scaf-nextjs-app-bu2` and ``am-ver-tolerance-module-ho90``).
2. `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh` next (needs the logging library, `am-scaf-extract-scripts-7jm`, and the gate registry from `am-scaf-quality-gates-ci-4xx`); it no longer waits for the reader shell. Paper-specific e2e beads bind the harness to real pages as each paper matures.
3. ``am-test-real-device-slice-check-bize`` after `am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu` and `am-gov-decision-device-profiles-1zm`; it blocks `am-bm-slice-retrospective-pp09`.
4. `am-test-real-device-check-iju4` after all four paper definitions of done and the slice check.

## Considerations

- "No mocks of the code under test": tests exercise real numerical owners, the real compiler, and real pages. Browser APIs unavailable in Bun are injected as dependencies rather than mocked globally. Harness self-tests use static fixture pages as inputs, because there the code under test is the harness.
- Never rerun a flaky statistical test until it passes; fix the seed policy or the tolerance derivation.
- Browser lanes are slow; they run as a separate CI workflow, never dropped from the definition of done or the release profiles.
- The DOM readiness contract names attributes other beads must emit (`data-ready`, `data-view`, `data-instance-id`, `data-run-id`, `data-snapshot-version`, `data-input-revision`, `data-accepted-input-revision`, `data-pending`, `data-execution-label`); a real page that lacks one fails its paper journey with a message naming the missing attribute.

title: Scenario registry, fixture and adversarial audits, statistical policy, precision display
description:
# Verification: scenario registry, fixture and adversarial audits, statistical policy, precision display

**Type:** epic · **Batch:** A (tolerance module, registry, precision display), B (statistical policy), D (no-circularity), H (quantity records), I (closure audits and final circularity) · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §13.1–13.5, §6.5, §17.1, §17.3 (traceability only)

## Background

A physics site can be green in CI and still wrong. Verification here is **quantity-specific**: for each numerical output the project records the model, assumptions, dimensions, independent reference, tested domain, error criterion, and evidence. An engine-wide "validated" badge never stands in for those records. Five questions stay separate because they need different evidence and a failure must name the layer that needs repair: mathematical identity checks, numerical convergence, statistical calibration, comparison with observations, and historical source fidelity.

Three kinds of fixtures are kept distinct in data and in the reader's view:

- **Historical fixtures** test that the site reproduces what Einstein printed from his stated inputs:
  - Avogadro's number $6.17\times10^{23}$ from Planck's printed constants;
  - about 4.3 V for $\nu = 1.03\times10^{15}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$, in the printed representation;
  - a Brownian displacement of $0.795\,\mu$m at 1 s and $6.16\,\mu$m at 60 s with the constants Einstein used, printed "0,8 Mikron" and "ca. 6 Mikron" (0.794 and 6.15 μm with the modern $k_B$);
  - the dissertation's three printings: about $2.1\times10^{23}$ (1905 thesis, $k = 1$), about $4.15\times10^{23}$ (1906 *Annalen* supplement, $k = 1$), and about $6.56\times10^{23}$ (1911 correction, $k = 5/2$).
- **Modern golden scenarios** test calculations and plumbing from modern constant sets (the photoelectric neutral case, the Brownian baseline, boosts, composition, Doppler, the mirror, transverse coefficients, the mass–energy coefficient).
- **Identities** test invariants (energy ratio equals Doppler ratio within $10^{-12}$; apparent speed doubles when the interval is quartered).

A fourth family, **adversarial fixtures**, are deliberately plausible wrong results that must fail for the intended reason. They target the most likely implementation and explanatory errors; they are not a claim that the suite proves all physics.

## Scope and Children

- `am-ver-tolerance-module-ho90`: the single tolerance and comparison module `src/units/tolerance.ts` (`withinTolerance`, `compareBitwise`, `classifyWithTolerance`, `validateToleranceSpec`), imported by the logging helpers, the scenario registry, the precision display rules, the exercise checker, and reference tests.
- `am-ver-scenario-registry-om3`: `content/scenarios/*.yaml` plus a runner that executes every scenario against reference evaluators (and WASM owners in cross-owner mode) and emits JSONL evidence, with transcription states, editorial inputs, printed representations, and an ownership checklist for every §13.3 and §13.5 row.
- `am-ver-precision-display-5e5`: precision, uncertainty, constant-set labeling, and the display wording of tolerance verdicts; it consumes the tolerance module and implements no comparison.
- `am-ver-statistical-policy-grj`: reproducible statistical test sets with prespecified tolerances, adequate sample sizes, and a ban on rerunning flaky tests until they pass.
- `am-ver-no-circularity-audit-6vj`: executable checks that no historical route or instrument assumes its own conclusion, active for the Brownian inference path and the mass–energy ledger, with pending rules for the relativity route and the photoelectric bench.
- `am-ver-no-circularity-final-i9qn`: activates and passes the relativity-route and photoelectric-bench checks against finished content before launch.
- `am-ver-fixture-table-audit-nh5`: every §13.3 fixture and golden scenario exists, is labeled by kind and constant set, and passes (or the companion fixtures are explicitly deferred).
- `am-ver-adversarial-audit-1ef`: every §13.5 adversarial fixture fails for its intended reason.
- `am-ver-quantity-records-fby2`: a verification record for every displayed computed output.

Out of scope: writing the evaluators and their per-module fixtures (`am-ep-reference-sln`), browser acceptance lanes (`am-ep-test-infra-yeb`), editorial review of prose (`am-ep-editorial-13x`), and the constant-set records (`am-ref-constants-xik`).

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Every scenario declares its kind, constant set, units, equations, owner, tolerance, and comparison kind (`bitwise` or `tolerance`), and the runner writes one JSONL record per assertion.
- [ ] All fifteen §13.3 rows exist as scenarios and pass with their declared constant sets; the molecular-dimensions row passes as three fixtures from three printings through `am-ref-viscosity-suspension-c9lp` or is explicitly deferred by `am-gov-decision-companion-at-launch-936`; no historical row whose printed inputs are still pending transcription is ever reported as passing; every editorial input and suspected misprint is recorded.
- [ ] All fifteen §13.5 adversarial rows exist and fail for their stated reason, with the light-complex row using the discriminating fixtures (longitudinal rays and a ray transverse in the moving frame).
- [ ] No statistical test can be retried into passing; tolerances are computed from sampling distributions before the run.
- [ ] Displayed precision follows the question and inputs; stored value, formatted value, input precision, statistical interval, numerical error estimate, and measurement uncertainty are never conflated; every displayed value names its constant set; one tolerance module (`src/units/tolerance.ts`) serves display, logging, and scenario comparisons.
- [ ] The no-circularity checks pass for the Brownian inference path (including discovery and real-data modes), the mass–energy ledger, the historical relativity route, and the photoelectric bench, with no rule left pending at launch.
- [ ] Every displayed computed output has a quantity-specific verification record, and no "validated" badge exists anywhere.

## Sequencing

1. **Batch A.** `am-ver-tolerance-module-ho90` first (it needs only the scaffold). Then, in parallel, `am-ver-scenario-registry-om3` (after the logging library, constant sets, and experiment schemas) and `am-ver-precision-display-5e5` (after typed results and the quantity registry), so every reference evaluator writes its fixtures into one format from its first commit.
2. **Batch B.** `am-ver-statistical-policy-grj` lands with the Brownian slice.
3. **Batch D.** `am-ver-no-circularity-audit-6vj` closes with the mass–energy paper, after Journey II, Journey IV, BM-07, the kitchen real-data mode, and the audit scripts exist.
4. **Batch H.** `am-ver-quantity-records-fby2` matures after every paper's instruments and lanes exist.
5. **Batch I.** `am-ver-fixture-table-audit-nh5`, `am-ver-adversarial-audit-1ef`, and `am-ver-no-circularity-final-i9qn` gate `am-launch-readiness-audit-sc9b`.

## Considerations

- **Corrected light-complex fixture.** The plan's adversarial row "test a transverse ray, where the packet-volume factor differs from $1/\gamma$" is wrong for a ray transverse in the unprimed frame: there $q = \gamma(1 - \beta\cos\varphi) = \gamma$ and $1/q = 1/\gamma$, which coincides with material contraction. The discriminating fixtures at $\beta = 0.6$ are longitudinal rays ($1/q = 2$ and $0.5$) and a ray transverse in the moving frame ($\cos\varphi = \beta$, $1/q = \gamma = 1.25$), each against $1/\gamma = 0.8$.
- **Printed constants, editorial inputs, and misprints.** Historical fixtures take constants exactly as printed in the pinned facsimiles, transcribed before a fixture is frozen.
  - Paper 1 §2: Planck's $\alpha = 6.10\times10^{-57}$ and $\beta = 4.866\times10^{-11}$ (CGS). A comparison witness prints $\alpha = 6.1\cdot10^{-56}$, which gives $6.17\times10^{22}$; only $6.10\times10^{-57}$ reproduces the printed $N$, so if the facsimile shows $10^{-56}$ the fixture records a suspected typographical error, uses the corrected value, and keeps the original on the source face. $R = 8.31\times10^{7}$ and $L = 3\times10^{10}$ appear not to be printed in §2 and are declared editorial inputs (sensitivity: $6.1858\times10^{23}$ with $R = 8.314\times10^{7}$ and $L = 2.998\times10^{10}$).
  - Paper 1 §8: the 4.3 V check follows the printed representation, $\Pi E = R\beta\nu - P'$ with the gram-equivalent charge $E = 9.6\times10^{3}$ in electromagnetic CGS units and $\Pi\cdot10^{-8}$ in volts (4.338 V); the esu and statvolt computation (4.306 V) is a documented modern restatement, and the witness's "Π·10⁷ = 4.3 Volt" is a suspected misprint.
  - Paper 2 §5: $N = 6\times10^{23}$, the viscosity $k = 1.35\times10^{-2}$ poise, and the particle diameter 0.001 mm as printed; $R$ appears not to be printed there, so $R = 8.31\times10^{7}$ is the editorial input printed in the light-quanta paper; 17 °C is declared as 290.15 K (or 290 K) by the site.
- **The 6.1 μm figure.** The plan's table lists 6.1 μm at 60 s, which is the modern-$k_B$ value (6.146687 μm) at two figures. With Einstein's constants the value is 6.156365 μm (6.2 μm at two figures). Every scenario declares its constant set, every display names it, and displays follow the precision rules.
- **The dissertation fixtures.** With one data set the values would differ only by $\sqrt{2.5} \approx 1.581$ (because $N \propto \sqrt{k}$ for the viscosity coefficient $k$), so $2.1\times10^{23}$ and $6.56\times10^{23}$ necessarily come from different inputs. The 1906 supplement's improved data give about $4.15\times10^{23}$ with $k = 1$, and $4.15 \times 1.581 \approx 6.56$; each fixture encodes exactly the inputs its printing gives.
- **Numerical stability.** Near-cancellation quantities use stable forms ($1 - \sqrt{1-\beta^2} = \beta^2/(1 + \sqrt{1-\beta^2})$, $\gamma - 1 = \gamma^2\beta^2/(\gamma + 1)$, `expm1` for spectra), and chi-square quantiles use a robust inverse regularized incomplete gamma tested against tabulated values.
- **Modern constants and inference.** In the 2019 SI, $R = N_A k_B$ with $N_A$ exact by definition, so an "inference of $N$" computed with modern constants is a consistency check, not an independent count; the circularity audit checks how real-data and discovery modes present this.
- Choose tolerances per quantity and regime: a relative tolerance alone fails near a true zero, an absolute tolerance alone fails across orders of magnitude, and near-cancellation classification may legitimately return an indeterminate result.
- A probability confidence interval is not an interval-arithmetic enclosure, and a numerical error bar is not a measurement uncertainty. Preserve upstream evidence semantics exactly.

title: Refactor the colorized equation component around exact quantity ids, operations, legends, and keyboard interaction
description:
# Refactor the colorized equation component around exact quantity ids, operations, legends, and keyboard interaction

**Epic:** `am-ep-equations-y76` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §1.5 item 3, §2.2, §2.3, §4.7, §11.4, §15.5, §15.6, §16.2, §19.4 (traceability only)

## Background

The donor's `src/components/ui/ColorizedEquation.tsx` (with `colorPalette.ts`, `equationValueFormatting.ts`, and `src/types/equation.ts`) implements the dual-coding idea this site inherits: an equation whose terms are colored and matched to fragments of a plain-language sentence, with term chips (`aria-pressed`), arrow-key navigation across the formula, an active-variable inspector, a "Pattern Mode" for color-blind readers, and live telemetry values. Its data model is `ColorizedEquation { id, patentId, title, category, rawLatex, colorizedLatex, plainEnglishSentence: SentenceFragment[], variables: EquationVariable[], pedagogicalNote, ... }`, where each `EquationVariable` carries a hand-assigned `ColorVariant` (one of nine: crimson, sapphire, emerald, amber, amethyst, cyan, coral, rose, teal), a `symbol`, a free-text `role`, a `unit`, and an optional `telemetryKey` or `telemetryMetricLabel`.

Four things must change for a bilingual scientific edition:

1. **Identity.** Variables are looked up by human label and permissive token matching. Here identity is the exact **term id** plus the canonical **quantity id**, resolved from the expression tree (`am-eq-expression-tree-8kl`).
2. **Color meaning.** Color attaches to the canonical quantity id and its declared role, never to a letter or a per-equation hand choice: $E$ is not permanently one color.
3. **Operations.** Readers may know what $T$ means but not why it sits in a denominator or why a logarithm appears. Selecting an operation must be as supported as selecting a symbol.
4. **Forms.** One equation can appear in its printed form, its modern (rename-only) form, and labeled alternate forms (a Gaussian-to-SI conversion, a modernization). The component must show the right form for the face and the reader's choices, and must never present a unit conversion or a modern argument as a change of letters.

## Scope

In scope: the refactored component (server-rendered static structure plus a small client island); the data contract it consumes; term and operation selection; the navigation model shared with the term explorer; the selection store shared with other views in the same argument context; the colorized plain-language sentence; the legend; the notation strip; form selection by face and reader state; display of the four kinds of meaning; pattern and monochrome identity; keyboard, pointer, and touch interaction.

Out of scope: live values (`am-eq-live-bindings-2se`); spoken forms and the assistive term explorer (`am-eq-spoken-forms-w4f`, which reuses this bead's navigation model); the six-rung interaction ladder (`am-eq-interaction-ladder-8ab`); the palette tokens and role list (`am-design-semantic-color-8vbq`); derivation chains and their renderer (`am-eq-derivation-chains-r4c` and its renderer bead); code colorization (`am-inst-show-the-code-4brv`); the notation, unit-layer, and perspective controls (`am-read-perspective-toggle-abd`); authoring alternate forms (paper equation beads).

## Requirements

### Data contract (replaces the donor's `ColorizedEquation` type)

- `equationId` and its qualified form (`<route slug>/<equation id>`), anchor, printed number, notation scope; precomputed static KaTeX markup from `am-eq-static-katex-7da` for the printed form, the modern (rename) form, and each alternate form.
- `terms[]`: `termId`, `quantityId`, `colorRole` (the registry role, or an argument-context override with its recorded reason per `am-design-semantic-color-8vbq`), authored short name, authored role explanation for this occurrence, display unit and dimension from the registry, frame tag, and the forms in which the term occurs.
- `operations[]`: `opId`, authored explanation of what the operation does here (for example "dividing by the drag coefficient: more resistance to motion means slower spreading"), and the forms in which it occurs.
- `sentence[]` per form: fragments `{ text, termId?, opId? }` forming the colorized plain-language sentence.
- `notationStrip`: printed-to-modern mappings for this equation's symbols, each with its concordance operation, collision severity (`danger` or `caution`), and whether this equation holds the section's first use (precomputed by the compiler from the concordance `firstUseAnchor`).
- `alternateForms[]`: `id`, `relation` (`unit-conversion` or `modernization`), authored `label`, and the derivation or modern-lens link.
- `meaning`: the four kinds of meaning for the equation and, where they differ, per term: logical role (definition, assumption, derivation, heuristic inference, empirical observation, qualification), historical status (available before the cutoff, introduced in this paper, later development, pedagogical reconstruction), model status (exact within the stated model, approximation, idealized representation, calibrated empirical model, unsupported outside the domain), execution status (static illustration, host calculation, accepted FrankenSim/WASM result, unavailable or refused).
- No `patentId`, no hand-assigned color, no telemetry label keys. The payload is route-local; the component never imports an aggregate registry.

### Forms by face and reader state

- **Source and translation faces** (`german`, `english`, `parallel`, `gloss`) use `notationPolicy: "printed-only"`: the printed form only and no toggle affordance. The notation strip stays available as a disclosure so readers can learn Einstein's glyphs.
- **Explanation faces** use `notationPolicy: "reader-choice"`. The printed form is the default. The modern rename form appears when the reader's notation state is `modern`. A `unit-conversion` alternate appears only when the reader chooses the SI unit layer for this equation or globally. A `modernization` alternate appears only under the modern perspective. Each alternate shows its label as visible text ("converted from Gaussian units", "modern argument, later lens") and links to its derivation or modern-lens record.
- Switching forms keeps the selected term or operation when its id exists in the new form. When it does not (an operation present only in the printed structure), the selection clears, a polite status message says so, and focus stays on the formula.

### Interaction and navigation

- The formula is **one** focus stop, and Tab leaves it.
- **Tree navigation**, implemented once in `src/equations/components/navigation.ts` and reused by the term explorer of `am-eq-spoken-forms-w4f`: Left and Right move among siblings in printed reading order; Down enters the first child of a selected operation; Up returns to the enclosing operation; Home and End go to the first and last sibling; Enter or Space selects; Escape clears the selection and returns focus to the formula root.
- Pointer and touch select directly. Every selectable node has a target of at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels: either its glyph hit area, padded where the padding does not overlap a neighbor, or its legend chip (always at least 24 by 24), which acts as the equivalent control under WCAG 2.2 success criterion 2.5.8 and performs exactly the same selection.
- Selecting a term highlights **exactly** its instances: the glyph occurrences bound to the same quantity id in this argument context, the matching sentence fragments, the legend row, and every subscriber of the selection store (linked graphs, scenes, tables, and code in the same argument context). Selecting an operation highlights the operation's subexpression and its sentence fragment.
- Terms bound to different quantities that share a glyph are never co-highlighted.

### Selection store (`src/equations/components/selectionStore.ts`)

- An external store keyed by `{ paper, argumentContext }`, where the argument context is the argument node or section block that scopes an equation, its graphs, and its code listings together.
- Its snapshot is `{ selectedNodeId, kind: "term" | "operation", quantityId, formId, version }`, and `getSnapshot` returns the same object reference until the selection changes, as `useSyncExternalStore` requires.
- Consumers subscribe and never keep private copies: this component, the term explorer, `am-inst-2d-view-kit-u75r` series and tables (matching `data-quantity-id`), `am-inst-show-the-code-4brv` identifiers, the derivation renderer, and the interaction ladder.
- Pages that show equations from more than one paper use qualified ids, so a paper 1 $\beta$ and a paper 3 $\beta$ on one page cannot collide.

### Legend and notation strip

- The legend lists each quantity in the equation with its symbol in the current form, name, role, display unit, and frame, and shows identity through label, shape or outline, and pattern as well as color.
- The notation strip shows the printed-to-modern mappings for the symbols in this equation, always keeping the printed symbol beside the modern one. Dangerous collisions ($\beta$ as the modern $\gamma$; $k$ as viscosity in paper 2) are called out prominently on first use in a section and link to the concordance entry.
- When an alternate form is displayed, the strip names its relation and links to the derivation ("converted from Gaussian units"; "modern argument, later lens").

### Color and identity

- Role classes (`am-role-<role>`) map to tokens from `am-design-semantic-color-8vbq`; no inline hex colors.
- Identity never depends on color. Underline style, outline, or pattern plus text labels are always present in the legend; the donor's pattern mode becomes a stronger optional emphasis, not the only accessible path.
- Red never simply means "bad"; a negative value is not an error.
- Monochrome print and forced-colors modes remain intelligible.

### Equation card (`src/equations/components/EquationCard.tsx`)

- Every face assembles an equation the same way: the `SemanticEquation` (formula, legend, sentence, notation strip, meaning labels) inside an `EquationCard` with named slots.
- The slots are filled by downstream beads, so this component never imports them:
  - `derivation`: the "Show the derivation" disclosure from the derivation renderer bead.
  - `ladder`: the rung panel from `am-eq-interaction-ladder-8ab`.
  - `code`: the show-the-code disclosure from `am-inst-show-the-code-4brv`.
- A slot without content renders nothing, and never renders an empty box.
- Page anatomy's "pin this equation" (`am-read-page-anatomy-l0b`) pins the whole card.

### Static-first

Without JavaScript, the equation, legend, sentence, notation strip, meaning labels, and alternate-form disclosures render as static content with real links; only selection hydrates.

## Technical Approach

- `src/equations/components/SemanticEquation.tsx` (server component), `SemanticEquationIsland.tsx` (client), `selectionStore.ts`, and `navigation.ts`, with `buildLegend.ts` and `buildSentence.ts` running in the compiler.
- Port the donor's formula keyboard handler, chips, decoder, and inspector patterns; replace the data model and lookup logic; delete nothing from the donor repository.
- Precompute legend, sentence, strip, and first-use data in the compiler; the island receives ids only. Record the island's compressed size in the performance report (target at most 10 KiB compressed) so the initial reading route stays within 200 KiB.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The component renders every fixture equation in its printed form, its modern rename form, and each alternate form from route-local payloads, with no aggregate imports.
- [ ] Source and translation faces show only the printed form; explanation faces follow the notation, unit-layer, and perspective states, and every displayed alternate carries its visible label.
- [ ] Selecting a term highlights exactly its authored meaning in the equation, sentence, legend, and a linked test view, and nothing else (including a same-glyph, different-quantity fixture and a two-paper page).
- [ ] Operation selection works for the denominator of $D = k_BT/(6\pi\eta a)$ and the logarithm in the radiation entropy law.
- [ ] Keyboard-only, pointer, and touch interaction reach every selectable node through the tree navigation model; the formula is a single tab stop with a clear exit.
- [ ] Every selectable node has a conforming target (glyph or legend chip) of at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels.
- [ ] Legend identity survives grayscale rendering and forced-colors mode; the four kinds of meaning appear as text, never color alone.
- [ ] With JavaScript disabled, the full static content is present.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `selectionStore.test.ts`: the same snapshot reference until a change; context isolation; exact quantity-id matching; same-glyph, different-quantity isolation; qualified ids on a two-paper fixture page.
- `navigation.test.ts` on the fixture tree of $D = k_BT/(6\pi\eta a)$: from $D$, Right reaches the right-hand side; Down on the denominator enters $6$, then Right reaches $\pi$, $\eta$, and $a$ in order; Up returns to the denominator; Home and End; Escape returns to the root.
- `buildLegend.test.ts` and `buildSentence.test.ts`: derived data from fixture records; collision callouts appear only on the section's first use.
- `forms.test.tsx`: printed-only on source faces; the rename form under notation state `modern`; the §6 SI alternate only under the unit layer, with its label; the §10 modernization only under the modern perspective; selection persists when ids exist in the new form and clears with a status message otherwise.
- `SemanticEquation.render.test.tsx` with real fixture payloads (no mocked component logic): static markup, legend rows, meaning labels as text, notation strip, alternate-form disclosures.
- `keyboard.test.tsx`: roving selection order, Enter, Space, Escape, focus return.

### End-to-end tests

- `e2e/equations/semantic-equation.spec.ts` on the harness fixture page (`am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`), with the same checks repeated in `am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu`. Select $\eta$ in a Brownian equation and assert that every highlighted element in the equation, sentence, legend, and linked graph carries the same `data-quantity-id`. Select the denominator operation. Toggle notation and confirm the selection persists by id. Measure the bounding box of every selectable node's glyph or chip target (at least 24 by 24).
- Lanes: 320 px touch, keyboard-only, forced colors (`forcedColors: "active"`), grayscale emulation (each legend row keeps a distinct identity cue), JavaScript disabled (static content present), and print. axe runs as a supplement only.

### Structured logging

JSON lines with `equationId`, `termId` or `opId`, `quantityId`, `argumentContext`, `formId`, `highlightTargets` (counts per view), `notation`, `viewport`, `inputMode`, `targetSizePx`, and `outcome`, plus the standard fields (`timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `browser`, `reducedMotion`, `jsEnabled`, `durationMs`, `message`). Failures retain screenshots of the equation region, an accessibility-tree snapshot, a DOM snapshot, and the console log. Path: `artifacts/test-logs/equations-colorized/<logRunId>.jsonl`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Do not port the donor's per-equation `ColorVariant` assignment; it encodes meaning by letter and drifts between equations.
- Highlight scope is the argument context, not the whole site: a quantity id may appear in many papers, but selection should not light unrelated sections.
- A unit conversion shown under the notation toggle would teach that SI is a change of letters; the form rules above prevent it.
- A legend chip used as the equivalent target must do exactly what the glyph does, including focus return.
- Keep the island small; the initial reading route stays within its JavaScript budget.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-eq-static-katex-7da` (static markup and markers the island attaches to); `am-design-semantic-color-8vbq` (role tokens and non-color identity rules). The e2e harness is reached through `am-eq-static-katex-7da` once that bead's proposed harness dependency is applied.

Unblocks: `am-eq-live-bindings-2se` (values attached to selected terms); `am-inst-show-the-code-4brv` (identifier colors shared with terms); `am-read-results-face-uzh` (result cards reuse this component); `am-read-perspective-toggle-abd` (form switching on explanation faces). The derivation renderer and `am-eq-interaction-ladder-8ab` subscribe to its selection store.

title: Build derivation chains with step, reason, tool, marked move, and a small tested set of transformation rules
Render derivation chains with the marked move, reasons at the reader's Detail, and returnable tool links
description:
# Render derivation chains with the marked move, reasons at the reader's Detail, and returnable tool links

**Epic:** `am-ep-equations-y76` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §1.4 item 4, §6.2, §6.4, §6.7, §7.8, §15.4, §15.6, §16.2, §19.2 (traceability only)

## Background

Every equation card carries a "Show the derivation" disclosure with the move highlighted (plan §15.6). The Batch B exit demonstration requires a reader to open "the derivation of the square-root time dependence" and return to the source without losing position (§19.2).

`am-eq-derivation-chains-r4c` supplies verified chains as data: steps, rules, reasons at three readings, tools, premises with edge types, and marked moves. This bead turns them into the reader-facing view.

It was split from that bead in review for a scheduling reason. The verifier is pure logic that the paper equation beads need early. The view needs static math, the colorized component and its selection store, the Detail axis, the return stack, and the foundation drawer. Keeping them together would have held every paper's chain authoring behind reader infrastructure.

## Scope

In scope:

- `DerivationChain.tsx` (server component) and a small island for step focus, highlighting, and per-step expansion;
- the "Show the derivation" disclosure on equation cards;
- the boxed move, reasons at the current Detail, approximation labels, and selectable cancellations;
- tool links through the return stack and the "where Einstein does this" source link;
- the front-door and side-door route choice;
- the "Show the code" slot;
- static and print output, and the nonvisual step list.

Out of scope:

- chain data, rules, and verification (`am-eq-derivation-chains-r4c`);
- the missing-step explorer panel (`am-reason-missing-step-explorer-rsl4`, which opens from a step);
- the foundation drawer (`am-found-library-infra-002t`);
- code extraction (`am-inst-show-the-code-4brv`, which fills the slot);
- the interaction ladder's rungs (`am-eq-interaction-ladder-8ab`, which reuses this renderer for "Show the next step");
- authoring chains (paper equation beads).

## Requirements

### Rendering

- **Card slot.** The chain renders as the "Show the derivation" disclosure in the `derivation` slot of the `EquationCard` from `am-eq-colorized-component-1z8`, so every equation card on every face carries it the same way.
- **Step list.** A static ordered list of steps (`<ol>`) with KaTeX markup precomputed by `am-eq-static-katex-7da`. Each step shows the expression before and after, with the changed subexpression highlighted. Highlighting uses the same term and operation ids, role classes, and selection store (`src/equations/components/selectionStore.ts`) as `am-eq-colorized-component-1z8`, and always pairs an outline with a text cue, never color alone.
- **Reasons at the reader's Detail.** R0, R1, and R2 reasons are all in the static HTML with `data-reading`, using the mechanism of `am-read-detail-axis-sfc`. A per-step "show every step" expansion opens R2 for that step without changing the global Detail.
- **The move.** It is boxed and labeled "The move" in text. Its theme styling comes from `am-design-themes-typography-288q` tokens: red emphasis in Annalen, lamplight amber in Kramgasse Night, a chalk box in Slate. It is announced as the move to assistive technology.
- **Approximations.** Approximation steps show their variable, order, and domain as visible text (for example "to first order in $v/c$, valid when $v \ll c$").
- **Cancellations.** Cancellations and subtractions are selectable operations; the mass–energy subtraction requires this.
- **Unverified steps.** An `authored-unverified` step in a preview build carries a visible "step not yet verified" marker. Published builds never contain one; the chains bead's publication gate prevents it.
- **Tool and source links.** Each step's tool opens its foundation through `openClarification` from `am-read-return-stack-oxa`. The source anchor links to "where Einstein does this" on the reading face, with the alignment highlight.
- **Several routes to one target.** The disclosure offers the front door (the source-order route) and the side doors (for example the variance-of-a-sum route), each labeled by route kind. Discovery and pedagogical routes carry "A route you could take"; source-order routes describe what the paper does.
- **Modern verification oracles.** Steps or edges of kind `modern-verification-oracle` appear only under the modern perspective, visibly labeled as a later check, and never inside a historical route's list.
- **Show the code.** The slot renders the disclosure provided by `am-inst-show-the-code-4brv` when present, and nothing otherwise.
- **Direct links.** A step opened from the ladder, the missing-step explorer, or a direct link (`?open=derivation-step:<chainId>/<stepId>`, registered as a clarification kind with the return stack) scrolls to that step and focuses it.

### Keyboard and assistive technology

- The step list uses standard list semantics.
- An optional step-focus mode is entered from the disclosure: Up and Down move between steps, Enter expands a step, and Escape leaves the mode with focus on the disclosure.
- Each step's accessible text includes:
  - its number;
  - the rule in words;
  - whether it is the move;
  - the spoken forms of the before and after expressions: the authored spoken forms from `am-eq-spoken-forms-w4f` when present, otherwise the colorized plain-language sentence.
- Expanding a step announces once; there is no live-region stream.

### Static-first and print

- Disclosures use native `<details>`, so every step, its R1 reason, and the move label read without JavaScript.
- Per-step R0 and R2 without JavaScript are reached through the static Detail fallback pages of `am-read-detail-axis-sfc`.
- Print expands every step and shows move labels and approximation domains.

## Technical Approach

- `src/equations/derivations/render/DerivationChain.tsx`, `DerivationStep.tsx`, `ChainIsland.tsx`, and `routeChooser.ts`.
- Payloads are precomputed by the compiler: step markup for each form, changed ids, reason readings, and tool and anchor links. The island receives ids only.
- Register the `derivation-step` clarification kind with the return stack.
- Keep the island small and record its compressed size in the performance report.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The Brownian fixture chains render with steps, highlighted changes, the boxed move, reasons at each Detail, approximation labels, tool links, and the source link. The fixtures are the source-order §4 route and the variance-of-a-sum route.
- [ ] A reader can switch between the two routes to the same target, and each route carries its route-kind label.
- [ ] Following a tool link opens the foundation through the return stack, and back returns focus to the same step.
- [ ] The move is labeled in text and announced; highlights are never color-only.
- [ ] Oracle steps never appear in a historical route's list; under the modern perspective they appear labeled as a later check.
- [ ] Every step reads without JavaScript and in print.
- [ ] The 320 px, keyboard-only, reduced-motion, and JavaScript-disabled lanes pass.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `DerivationChain.render.test.tsx`, with real compiled fixture payloads (no mocked chain logic). It checks the static markup, `<ol>` and `<details>` structure, move label text, highlight ids, reasons per Detail, approximation text, and route labels.
- `routeChooser.test.ts`: front-door and side-door ordering; oracle steps filtered by perspective; an unknown route id fails explicitly.
- `stepFocus.test.tsx`: Up, Down, Enter, and Escape; focus return after a clarification closes.
- `a11yText.test.ts`: each step's accessible text includes number, rule, move flag, and spoken forms, with the plain-sentence fallback when a spoken form is absent.

### End-to-end tests
