Failing browser lanes retain a screenshot, trace, DOM snapshot, accessibility-tree snapshot, and console log.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A long prose description alone is not equivalent to being able to investigate.
- If a family's first consumer shows that the base does not fit, change the base through the freeze's versioned change policy. Do not fork a second primitive system.
- A draggable region is not automatically a partition. Choose the family by the question the action answers: a probability of a region is an interval; an entropy comparison at fixed energy and band is a partition.
- Keep equivalent panels usable by everyone, not hidden behind screen-reader-only markup.
- The classification near equal times belongs to the owner and the tolerance module; a primitive that decided simultaneity itself would be a second physics owner.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-inst-interaction-primitives-emwy`: the primitive base and the interval family.
- `am-bm-slice-retrospective-pp09`: the recorded decision about which abstractions to generalize.
- `am-eq-derivation-chains-r4c`: the rule set and step data for `ExpressionActionPicker`.

The action-contract builder (`am-a11y-action-contracts-k75g`), command classes (`am-rt-command-classes-dzp`), the tolerance module (`am-ver-tolerance-module-ho90`), and the e2e harness (`am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`) arrive transitively through these.

Unblocks: `am-me-03-system-boundary-0arb`, `am-sr-01-clock-sync-jbfn`, `am-sr-03-rod-simultaneity-0l5i`, `am-sr-04-lorentz-map-px1k`, `am-sr-08-field-frame-change-5ibt`, `am-lq-04-entropy-workbench-senj`.

title: Build event, interval, partition, coefficient, channel, and expression interactions with nonvisual equivalents
description:
# Build event, interval, partition, coefficient, channel, and expression interactions with nonvisual equivalents

**Epic:** `am-ep-instruments-8gi` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §10.4, §10.5, §15.6, §16.2, §19.2, §19.7 (P0: equivalent nonvisual actions) (traceability only)

## Background

"Sliders suit continuous parameters and nothing else." Many scientific actions are not continuous parameters:
- Simultaneity is a question about choosing events.
- An integral is a question about choosing an interval.
- Entropy at fixed energy is a question about resizing a constrained volume.
- A transformation is a question about coefficients.
- An energy balance is a question about which channel or boundary you include.
- A derivation is a question about which subexpression you transform.

The plan makes nonvisual equivalence a P0 requirement. A reader who cannot drag, cannot distinguish colors, cannot hear, or cannot see a canvas must still perform the **same scientific action**, not read a long description of someone else doing it.

The plan also says not to generalize the framework before the Brownian reference slice shows which abstractions help. The slice needs exactly one of the six interaction families: interval selection, for BM-06. This bead therefore builds the shared typed-action primitive base and the `IntervalSelector`, proven on BM-06. The other five families (event, partition, coefficient, channel, expression) are built in a follow-on bead after `am-bm-slice-retrospective-pp09`, on the base this bead proves, each accepted against its first real consumer (SR-01 and SR-03, LQ-04, SR-04 and SR-08, ME-03). The bead title keeps the whole family set for traceability; the split changes when each family is built, not what the platform delivers.

## Scope

In scope:
- the headless typed-action primitive base in `src/experiments/interactions/`: state, action emission, visual adapters, and nonvisual adapters;
- its integration with the action-contract framework and the runtime command classes;
- `IntervalSelector` for the probability and diffusion family, with visual, keyboard, typed, and screen-reader forms;
- a test fixture experiment for the harness;
- the documentation other families must follow (`docs/INTERACTION_PRIMITIVES.md`).

Out of scope:
- the event, partition, coefficient, channel, and expression families, built after the slice freeze in their own bead;
- the action-contract registry and audit (`am-a11y-action-contracts-k75g`);
- schema-driven sliders (`am-inst-parameter-controls-cmj9`);
- derivation-chain data (`am-eq-derivation-chains-r4c`);
- BM-06 itself (`am-bm-06-gaussian-spread-982y`).

## Requirements

### The primitive base

- **Typed actions.** Every primitive emits a typed action `{ instrumentId, actionId, inputs, commandClass }`, built by the single command builder of `am-a11y-action-contracts-k75g`. The runtime handles it. The visual and nonvisual forms emit identical actions and therefore produce identical accepted snapshots.
- **Headless state.** The base provides headless state (selection, draft, committed) with explicit commit and clear actions. Adapters render that state for SVG or Canvas views built on `am-inst-2d-view-kit-u75r`, and for nonvisual forms (form fields, tables, listboxes).
- **Validation.** Typed entry accepts units through the quantity registry and validates against the owner's domain. Invalid entries explain the problem without issuing an action, and nothing is clamped.
- **Accessibility.** Keyboard operable with visible focus; accessible names and descriptions; usable touch targets at 320 px; no tooltip-only information.
- **Announcements.** Screen-reader summaries are at the scale of the question (for an interval, its limits and probability), never a stream of coordinates. They are announced once per committed action.
- **Command-class wording.** The primitive's copy names which kind of change it performs. Observer changes never create events or restart runs.
- **Registration.** Each primitive registers its action-contract entry so the audit can verify parity.

### `IntervalSelector` (probability and diffusion family)

| Visual action | Equivalent scientific action |
|---|---|
| Drag a selected histogram or density interval | Enter lower and upper limits, inspect the interval probability, compare two named intervals |

- **Semantics.** Closed interval $[x_1, x_2]$ with $x_1 \le x_2$. Entering $x_1 > x_2$ is explained ("the lower limit must not exceed the upper limit") and offers a swap. It is never auto-swapped silently.
- **Named intervals.** Two named intervals can be stored and compared (for example "within one RMS" and "within two RMS"). Each name and its limits travel with the action.
- **Snapping.** Drag snapping, when enabled, is presentation: it snaps to displayed tick values, never to a different stored value. The typed value always wins.
- **Class.** The interval is an `estimator-change` by default; a manifest may declare another class with a reason.

### Guidance for the later families

`docs/INTERACTION_PRIMITIVES.md` records:
- the headless contract;
- the adapter interfaces;
- the parity test pattern;
- the announcement rules;
- the planned visual and equivalent actions of the other five families from the plan's action-contract table (events from a table with a per-frame simultaneity question; ratio entry or half, same, or double at fixed energy and band; axis or component selection with a signed magnitude; an object-inclusion checklist with boundary-crossing energy; a subexpression list with role reading and a justified step).

## Technical Approach

- The headless primitives and adapters live under `src/experiments/interactions/`; the interval family is in `src/experiments/interactions/interval/`.
- A fixture experiment registered only in the fixture build exposes an analytic density whose interval probabilities come from a real reference evaluator, so parity tests exercise a real owner.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The primitive base exists with headless state, visual and nonvisual adapters, commit and clear semantics, and contract registration.
- [ ] `IntervalSelector` has visual, keyboard, typed, and screen-reader forms that emit identical typed actions.
- [ ] Parity: from the same state, the visual action and the nonvisual action produce the same accepted snapshot id and outputs.
- [ ] Keyboard-only and screen-reader smoke tests pass, with no tooltip-only information.
- [ ] Invalid entries (reversed limits, wrong units, out of domain) explain and issue no action.
- [ ] 320 px layouts have no horizontal overflow and have usable touch targets.
- [ ] `docs/INTERACTION_PRIMITIVES.md` documents the base and the planned families.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `interactions.parity.test.tsx`: drive the visual path (pointer drag events on the adapter) and the nonvisual path (typed limits) with the same inputs. Compare the emitted actions field by field, and the resulting snapshots from the real fixture owner, for $[-1, 1]$, $[0, 0]$, and $[-\infty$-like large bound, $0]$ cases.
- `interactions.validation.test.tsx`:
  - unit-aware typed entry: 1 μm and $10^{-6}$ m give the same canonical value;
  - reversed limits are explained with the swap offer and no action;
  - out-of-domain values are explained;
  - no clamping.
- `interactions.commandClass.test.ts`: the declared class reaches the runtime through the real command router.
- `interactions.announce.test.tsx`: one announcement per commit and none during drag.

### End-to-end tests

On the harness fixture page:
- keyboard entry of limits equals a drag selection, with the same probability and snapshot id;
- the screen-reader lane announces the selection summary once per committed action;
- the 320 px touch lane works.

The BM-06 interval lanes run in `am-bm-06-gaussian-spread-982y` and `am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu`.

### Structured logging

JSONL at `artifacts/test-logs/interactions/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `instrumentId`, `actionId`, `family`, `inputMode` (`pointer`, `keyboard`, `typed`, `screen-reader`), `inputs`, `commandClass`, `snapshotVersion`, `outcome`, `message`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A long prose description alone is not equivalent to being able to investigate.
- Do not build the other five families here. Their shapes should come from their first real consumers after the slice retrospective, on the base proven by the interval.
- Keep the nonvisual forms usable by everyone; many sighted readers prefer typing limits.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-inst-parameter-controls-cmj9`: shared validation, units, and command dispatch.
- `am-a11y-action-contracts-k75g`: the contract framework and command builder each primitive registers with.
- `am-inst-2d-view-kit-u75r`: the SVG and Canvas views the visual adapters draw on.

Unblocks:
- `am-bm-06-gaussian-spread-982y`: interval selection.
- The follow-on bead for the event, partition, coefficient, channel, and expression families.

title: Build the /lab/[experiment] standalone workbench route with source and explanation links
description:
# Build the /lab/[experiment] standalone workbench route with source and explanation links

**Epic:** `am-ep-instruments-8gi` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §6.9 (Discover and Experiment are routes), §10.7, §15.1, §15.4, §16.3, §16.4 (traceability only)

## Background

Instruments live inside the reading face at the step they illuminate, but readers also need a standalone workbench: a teacher projecting BM-01, a programmer exploring SR-04's matrix, a reader returning to the photoelectric apparatus. The plan defines `/lab/[experiment]` as that workbench, with source and explanation links, one canonical URL per experiment, and an Open Graph card per laboratory.

The route must remain a book page first: meaningful static HTML without JavaScript, a clear question at the top, and links back to the exact source passages and explanations the instrument serves.

This bead lands after BM-01, so its browser lanes run on a real instrument. Instruments do not depend on this route: every instrument is fully operable inside the reading face.

## Scope

In scope:
- `src/app/lab/[experiment]/page.tsx` with static params from the registry;
- the layout and header;
- source and explanation links;
- the static worked example;
- share and model-note placement;
- metadata and Open Graph hooks;
- not-found behavior;
- print output for the current state.

Out of scope:
- the embed route (`am-inst-embed-route-rnyg`);
- Open Graph image generation (`am-design-og-images-pwok`);
- the essential-for-print policy (`am-plat-print-3orn`, Batch C);
- the instruments themselves.

## Requirements

- **Static params.** `generateStaticParams` comes from registered catalogue entries (those with a manifest).
  - Unknown ids return the App Router not-found page, never another instrument.
  - Catalogue ids without a manifest also return not-found, with the not-found page linking to the paper passage where the instrument will live. No empty lab pages are generated.
- **Page anatomy:**
  - the instrument's explanatory question;
  - the instrument, lazy loaded, with its execution label and model note;
  - "Read this in the paper" links to the anchored source passages (German and English);
  - "Why this matters" links to the explanation anchors from the manifest;
  - the "What this does not model" line;
  - related misconceptions;
  - predict-mode default behavior.
- **Modes.** Modes come through `?mode=` for instruments with registered modes (for example `lq-08:count-model`), validated against the registry. An invalid mode shows a notice and the default mode.
- **Without JavaScript:** the static worked example, the question, the `notModeled` line, and real links remain.
- **Metadata:** title and description from the manifest. `rel=canonical` omits tape and mode noise; modes with distinct scientific content may be canonical subpages if registered.
- **Layout:** single column on phones with the instrument above its explanation; a bounded sticky lab region on desktop that never traps scroll (page anatomy rules from `am-read-page-anatomy-l0b`); no page-level horizontal overflow at 320 px.
- **Print** (Batch B scope): the question, the static representation of the current state with its parameters, snapshot identity, and a caption, the `notModeled` line, and the source links as printed URLs. Expansion of essential explanations under the essential-for-print policy arrives with `am-plat-print-3orn`.

## Technical Approach

- An App Router page with a server-rendered shell, using the dispatcher from `am-inst-registry-dispatcher-66l0`.
- Data comes from compiled route-local payloads, not the aggregate registry.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every registered experiment has a static lab page; unknown ids and catalogue ids without a manifest return not-found.
- [ ] Source and explanation links resolve to existing anchors (build-time check).
- [ ] The JavaScript-disabled render shows the question, the static example, `notModeled`, and the links.
- [ ] The 320 px, keyboard-only, and reduced-motion lanes pass on `/lab/bm-01`.
- [ ] The initial route bundle excludes Three.js, the PDF viewer, and WASM.
- [ ] Print output contains the question, a captioned static state with its snapshot identity, `notModeled`, and source URLs.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `labRoute.params.test.ts`: static params match registered entries; an unknown id and a catalogue id without a manifest (for example `bm-02` in Batch B) are not-found.
- `labRoute.links.test.ts`: anchor resolution against compiled content.
- `labRoute.mode.test.ts`: valid and invalid `?mode=` values.
- `labRoute.metadata.test.ts`: canonical URL without state parameters; title and description from the manifest.

### End-to-end tests

- Lanes for `/lab/bm-01`: desktop, 320 px touch, keyboard only, JavaScript disabled, reduced motion, and print emulation.
- Assertions: the question text, the label, the links, the static worked example with the printed numbers, the captioned state in print, and no horizontal overflow.
- A bundle assertion on the route's initial JavaScript.

### Structured logging

JSONL at `artifacts/test-logs/lab-route/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `route`, `instrumentId`, `mode`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `brokenLinks`, `bundleBytes`, `snapshotVersion`, `outcome`, `message`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- One canonical URL per experiment; slider positions are never canonical pages.
- Keep the lab page from becoming a dense control panel; advanced settings stay in the drawer.
- Do not add a dependency from instruments to this route. The reading face is the primary home of every instrument.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-inst-registry-dispatcher-66l0`: registry and dispatcher.
- `am-read-shell-routes-3ua`: App Router shell, layout, and anchor infrastructure.
- `am-inst-execution-labels-5ywv`: the label and model note placed on the page.
- `am-read-page-anatomy-l0b`: the bounded sticky lab region and phone layout.
- `am-bm-01-tracer-ensemble-hdly`: the first real instrument the lanes run on.

Unblocks: `am-inst-embed-route-rnyg` (embed pages reuse the lab route's composition), `am-launch-readiness-audit-sc9b`.

title: Generate controls, URL-state validation, and domain explanations from the parameter schema
description:
# Generate controls, URL-state validation, and domain explanations from the parameter schema

**Epic:** `am-ep-instruments-8gi` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §10.3, §10.4, §10.7, §12.6, §12.10, §16.2, §16.5 (traceability only)

## Background

A slider that silently clamps a value while its label shows what the reader typed is a small lie that corrupts every conclusion drawn from the instrument. The plan requires one parameter schema per control that declares physical dimension, display unit, valid model domain, numerical domain, pedagogical default, step or logarithmic mapping, and whether the parameter is independent or derived. That single schema generates the control, the validation of shared state, unit formatting, and test cases.

Controls are also where the runtime's command classes meet the reader. Six operations are distinct, with different guarantees: changing initial conditions, intervening mid-run, changing the observer, changing a measurement, changing an estimator, and changing presentation. Each control declares which one it issues.

Controls are generated from the `ParameterSpec` schema and dispatch typed commands. They need neither the registry nor any instrument; instrument views mount them for a registered instance. This lets the control library proceed in parallel with the registry and the view kit.

## Scope

In scope:
- schema-driven control generation in `src/experiments/controls/`;
- typed value entry and step buttons beside sliders;
- domain explanations, including off-grid values for measurement grids;
- per-parameter `parse` and `serialize` functions in canonical SI, used by the permalink encoder;
- the "Experiment settings" drawer;
- reset semantics;
- command-class mapping;
- seed inputs.

Out of scope:
- non-slider interactions (`am-inst-interaction-primitives-emwy`);
- permalink tapes and their URL encoding (`am-inst-permalink-tape-s677`, the single shared-state URL mechanism);
- the runtime command semantics (`am-rt-command-classes-dzp`);
- the registry and dispatcher (`am-inst-registry-dispatcher-66l0`).

## Requirements

### Schema fields (from `ParameterSpec` in the experiment manifest)

- `id`, `label`, `quantityId`, `displayUnit`.
- `modelDomain`: bounds with inclusivity, or an enumerated set, with a reason text for each boundary.
- `numericalDomain`, and `visualRange` (which may be narrower than the model domain).
- `default`.
- `mapping`: `linear`, `log` with its base, or `step` with its step size. A step mapping may reference a grid declared by another parameter, for example an observation interval that must be a multiple of a time resolution.
- `role`: `independent`, or `derived` with `derivedFrom`.
- `commandClass`: `setup-change`, `physical-intervention`, `observer-change`, `measurement-change`, `estimator-change`, or `presentation-change`.
- An accessible name and description.
- A quantization policy (declared step or significant digits in canonical SI), shared with the tapes.

### Suggested teaching ranges

These are admitted by the owners and documented separately from mathematical domains:

- Radiation temperature 500–10 000 K; logarithmic frequency over $10^{11}$–$10^{16}$ Hz.
- Photoelectric work function 1–6 eV, hypothetical unless a cited metal card is chosen; photoelectric frequency 100–2 000 THz.
- **Brownian:** radius 0.1–5 μm in the dilute-sphere model; viscosity 0.5–20 mPa·s as an explicit fluid parameter, and temperature never silently supplies an unmodeled viscosity law; temperature 273–330 K; a gas card refuses, because Stokes drag without the Cunningham slip correction is invalid when the mean free path is comparable to the radius.
- Frame speed: signed $v/c$ within ±0.95 in the core; no inertial observer at $\lvert v\rvert \ge c$.
- Emitted energy: a positive pedagogical range plus normalized ratios.
- Sample counts and time horizons: explicit and finite. A memory or time budget failure is distinct from physical invalidity.

### Control behavior

- **Inputs.** Slider plus typed exact-value input plus step buttons, following the WAI-ARIA slider pattern and its warning about touch assistive technology. Typed entry is always available.
- **Beyond the visual range.** A typed value outside the visual range but inside the model domain is accepted, and the slider shows that the value is beyond its track.
- **Out of domain.** Out-of-domain inputs are **never silently clamped**. The control explains the problem in ordinary language, offers the admissible boundary or a model change, and issues no command until the reader chooses.
- **Off-grid.** A value that is off a declared grid (for example 0.015 s on a 0.02 s grid) is explained the same way. The control offers the nearest admissible grid values and, when the manifest allows, a grid change as a separate setup-change. It is never silently rounded.
- **Derived parameters** display as read-only values computed by the owner.
- **Units** display through the quantity registry. Entry accepts the display unit and documented alternatives (for example mPa·s and Pa·s) with explicit conversion shown next to the field.

### Seeds and trials

- Seed inputs accept unsigned 64-bit canonical decimal strings, per `am-rt-u64-identities-7ce`. Invalid signs, whitespace, leading zeros, exponents, overlong input, and overflow are rejected with a message.
- "Same seed" and "new trial" are separate, labeled actions. A new trial records the chosen seed.

### Drawer and reset

- A scene begins with a useful question and a stable default. Advanced controls, such as a time resolution or recording length, live in an "Experiment settings" drawer.
- Reset restores parameters and the relevant experiment history, and states whether it keeps the seed or starts a new trial.

### Shared state

- Each control provides `parse(text)` and `serialize(value)` in canonical SI with strict validation: known ids, canonical decimal strings, domain and grid checks, and bounded length.
- The permalink encoder (`am-inst-permalink-tape-s677`) uses these functions. Controls do not create their own query parameters on paper routes.
- Invalid shared state is reported by the permalink layer with a visible notice and falls back to defaults. It never crashes and never clamps silently.
- Canonical document URLs are unaffected by control state.

## Technical Approach

- `buildControls(schema)` returns React components and a validation module generated from the same schema. Property tests derive valid and invalid cases from the domains.
- Commands dispatch through the runtime with their declared class. A control never mutates snapshots.
- A test-only fixture manifest exercises every field type without depending on any instrument.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Controls are generated from the schema for all field types; typed entry, step buttons, and the slider stay synchronized.
- [ ] No code path clamps or rounds silently; out-of-domain and off-grid entries produce explanations and admissible options.
- [ ] Every control declares a command class, and a test verifies the runtime receives that class.
- [ ] Seed inputs round-trip $0$, $2^{53}$, $2^{53} \pm 1$, and $2^{64} - 1$, and invalid inputs are rejected.
- [ ] `parse` and `serialize` round-trip every field type in canonical SI at its quantization policy; for example, $1.35\times10^{-3}$ Pa·s and $5\times10^{-7}$ m survive unchanged.
- [ ] Keyboard-only operation, visible focus, accessible names, and the 320 px layout pass.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `controls.schema.test.ts`: generation for each field type; derived read-only behavior; drawer placement.
- `controls.domain.test.ts`: property tests for inside, boundary, and outside values, with no clamp assertions. Off-grid fixtures: 0.015 s on a 0.02 s grid offers 0.02 s and a grid change.
- `controls.units.test.ts`: typed mPa·s and Pa·s entries give identical canonical values and show the conversion.
- `controls.seed.test.ts`: 64-bit decimal handling at the boundary values; rejection of `-1`, ` 1`, `01`, `1e3`, 21-digit input, and $2^{64}$.
- `controls.parse.test.ts`: `parse`/`serialize` round trips at quantization, unknown ids, and oversize input.
- `controls.commandClass.test.ts`: the dispatched class per control, using the real command router from `am-rt-command-classes-dzp`.

### End-to-end tests

On the harness fixture page:
- The keyboard-only lane types an out-of-domain viscosity and asserts both the explanation and that the snapshot's accepted input revision is unchanged.
- The touch lane at 320 px uses the step buttons.
- A screen-reader smoke check verifies names and value text.

The BM-01 viscosity and interval lanes run in `am-bm-01-tracer-ensemble-hdly` and `am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu`.

### Structured logging

JSONL at `artifacts/test-logs/controls/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `instrumentId`, `parameterId`, `inputValue`, `canonicalValue`, `domainStatus`, `gridStatus`, `commandClass`, `inputRevision`, `acceptedInputRevision`, `outcome`, `message`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A control's visual range and its mathematical domain are different facts; document both.
- Changing a camera's physical exposure is a measurement change; moving the rendered microscope viewpoint is presentation; a moving detector is a physical component, not a frame choice. Name these in ordinary language on the control.
- A second URL-state mechanism beside `?tape=` would soon disagree with it; keep one.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-cm-schemas-experiment-fuu`: the `ParameterSpec` schema.
- `am-rt-command-classes-dzp`: typed commands and their classes.
- `am-not-quantity-registry-2f7`: dimensions, units, and formatting.
- `am-rt-u64-identities-7ce`: 64-bit seed validation and transport.

Unblocks:
- `am-inst-interaction-primitives-emwy`, `am-inst-permalink-tape-s677`.
- `am-bm-01-tracer-ensemble-hdly`, `am-bm-05-random-steps-ntzl`.

title: Serialize accepted identities and compact tapes into bounded ?tape= permalinks
description:
# Serialize accepted identities and compact tapes into bounded ?tape= permalinks

**Epic:** `am-ep-instruments-8gi` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P0 (plan contract item; required by the slice instruments) · **Plan sections:** §7.7, §10.7, §12.10, §12.11, §15.1, §16.5 (traceability only)

## Background

A reader should be able to share exactly what they saw: the same experiment, the same seed, the same sequence of controls, and even their prediction, so a teacher can see what a class expected. The plan specifies that a permalink serializes the accepted snapshot's identities and a compact, valid control tape into `?tape=`, with a bounded size. Canonical document URLs never multiply into an index of slider positions.

Permalinks are also an attack surface and a correctness trap. URL state is untrusted input: a malicious or accidental tape must not freeze the page, and a 64-bit seed must never be rounded through a JavaScript number.

`?tape=` is the single shared-state URL mechanism for instruments. Controls supply per-parameter `parse` and `serialize` functions (`am-inst-parameter-controls-cmj9`); this bead encodes, bounds, decodes, and replays.

## Scope

In scope:
- tape encoding and decoding for URLs in `src/experiments/permalink/`;
- validation and bounds;
- restoration by replaying to the accepted snapshot;
- share UI;
- canonical and indexing rules;
- a runtime-fixture instrument for tests.

Out of scope:
- tape semantics, checkpoints, and teaching-tape content (`am-rt-control-tapes-0gc`);
- control validation (`am-inst-parameter-controls-cmj9`);
- CSP and the global security review (`am-plat-security-f644`);
- per-instrument permalink lanes (instrument beads and `am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu`).

## Requirements

### Payload

The tape carries:
- the payload version, experiment id and mode, model version, and constant-set id;
- the seed as a canonical unsigned 64-bit decimal string, the stream version, and the allocation id;
- quantized control events with command classes and logical action indices;
- optional `prediction` events with `promptId`;
- the expected final accepted snapshot identity: the input revision count and the checkpoint digest (`host:` or `blake3:`).

A payload may instead reference an authored teaching tape by id plus a step index, which keeps shared teaching states short.

### Encoding

- Compact JSON or a documented binary layout, compressed and base64url encoded.
- Decimal strings for all 64-bit values; no `BigInt` passed through ordinary JSON.
- Each parameter value is serialized with that control's `serialize` and read back with its `parse`.

### Bounds

- A maximum encoded length of 2 048 characters, a maximum event count of 256 per tape, and per-parameter domain checks through the controls' `parse`.
- Oversize, unknown version, unknown experiment, out-of-domain values, or malformed input produce a visible notice ("This shared state could not be restored: reason") and load defaults. Nothing is silently clamped or truncated.
- The declared bound must hold for realistic states. Test it with BM-01's "Einstein's 0.8 micron" teaching sequence plus a 64-point prediction sketch.

### Restoration

- Replay events through the runtime in logical order.
- If the reproduced checkpoint digest differs from the stored one, show a notice that the run was reproduced under a different model or artifact version, and keep both identities visible in the model note.
- A tape whose stream semantics, allocation id, or constant set no longer match is refused with its typed reason (`am-rt-control-tapes-0gc`) and never silently upgraded.

### Canonical URLs

- Pages with `?tape=` declare `rel=canonical` without the parameter and `noindex` for the tape variant.
- Sitemaps never list tape URLs.

### Share UI

- A "Copy link to this experiment state" action with an accessible confirmation.
- It works without clipboard permission by showing the URL in a selectable field.
- Before copying, the UI states whether the link includes the reader's predictions and offers to leave them out. Predictions otherwise stay on the device.

## Technical Approach

- The encoder and decoder are pure functions with schema validation; replay uses the runtime's tape player.
- Fuzz tests use a fixed seed corpus for decoder robustness.
- Unit round trips use the runtime-fixture seeded walk from `src/testing/runtime-fixtures/`. Real-instrument round trips run in the instrument beads.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Round trip: encode, decode, and replay reproduce the same accepted snapshot identity for the runtime-fixture walk with seeds $0$, $2^{53}$, $2^{53} + 1$, and $2^{64} - 1$.
- [ ] Oversize, malformed, unknown-version, and out-of-domain tapes produce notices and defaults, never crashes or hangs.
- [ ] Prediction events survive round trips, and the share UI can exclude them.
- [ ] Tape URLs are `noindex` and canonicalize to the document URL.
- [ ] Decoder fuzzing over the fixed corpus finds no unhandled exceptions and stays within a declared bound of 5 ms per input.
- [ ] A teaching-tape reference with a step index restores that step.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `permalink.encode.test.ts`: payload fields; decimal-string seeds; compression; the length of the "Einstein's 0.8 micron" sequence with a 64-point sketch stays under 2 048 characters.
- `permalink.decode.test.ts`: every rejection reason with its notice text; a JSON-number seed is rejected; truncated base64url is rejected; 256 events are accepted and 257 rejected.
- `permalink.u64.test.ts`: `9007199254740992`, `9007199254740993`, and `18446744073709551615` round-trip exactly; `18446744073709551616` is rejected.
- `permalink.replay.test.ts`: with the real runtime and the fixture owner, the replayed identity equals the stored identity; a changed model version shows the reproduced-under-a-different-version notice with both identities.
- `permalink.fuzz.test.ts`: the fixed corpus and the time bound.
- `permalink.canonical.test.ts`: `rel=canonical` and `noindex` on tape variants; sitemap exclusion.

### End-to-end tests

On the harness fixture instrument:
- set parameters and a prediction, copy the permalink, open it in a fresh context, and assert identical snapshot identity, overlay, and model note;
- open a truncated tape URL and assert the notice and defaults;
- copy with predictions excluded and assert none restore.

BM-01, BM-05, and BM-06 permalink lanes with boundary seeds run in `am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu`.

### Structured logging

JSONL at `artifacts/test-logs/permalink/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `instrumentId`, `tapeLength`, `eventCount`, `seed`, `restoreStatus`, `rejectionReason`, `checkpointDigestExpected`, `checkpointDigestActual`, `predictionsIncluded`, `durationMs`, `outcome`, `message`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Never hash a rounded decimal display of a seed.
- A tape records logical actions, not render frames; render cadence must not affect restoration.
- Shared links are public once pasted. Tell readers when their predictions are included.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-rt-control-tapes-0gc`: tape format, checkpoints, and prediction events.
- `am-inst-parameter-controls-cmj9`: per-parameter `parse` and `serialize`, domain validation, and 64-bit seed handling.

Unblocks:
- `am-plat-security-f644`: reviews bounded URL state.
- Sharing in every instrument (`am-bm-01-tracer-ensemble-hdly`, `am-bm-05-random-steps-ntzl`, `am-bm-06-gaussian-spread-982y`, and later instruments), `am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu`, `am-disc-shelf-michelson-fizeau-dauq`, and `am-disc-avogadro-lab-pfi7`.

title: Build predict mode with hidden response, candidate curves or sketches, overlay, and tape events
description:
# Build predict mode with hidden response, candidate curves or sketches, overlay, and tape events

**Epic:** `am-ep-instruments-8gi` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P0 (plan innovation tier P1; required by the slice instruments' contract) · **Plan sections:** §6.7, §7.7, §10.7, §12.11, §14.5, §16.6, §19.7 (traceability only)

## Background

Predicting before seeing is one of the cheapest ways to make an interaction teach instead of entertain. The plan specifies a predict mode on every instrument, on by default for first-time visitors:

- before the reader's first change, the response plot is hidden and the reader chooses or sketches what will happen;
- when the reader commits the change, the accepted snapshot draws the real curve over the prediction, and both stay visible.

The design rules come from the plan's reading of the education literature: productive exploration followed by sufficient explanation, never compulsory rediscovery, and never a judgment of the person. An incorrect prediction is a productive starting point, not a usability failure. The explanation is available regardless of the prediction.

Most instruments ask more than one question. BM-01, for example, asks what happens when you watch four times as long and what happens in a liquid twice as viscous, and the Batch B exit demonstration needs the second. Predict mode therefore supports one authored prompt per control or action: the prompt for whichever control the reader engages first appears first, and each other prompt appears the first time its own control is engaged.

## Scope

In scope:
- `src/experiments/predict/` for per-prompt state, the hidden response, candidate curves, freehand sketches, nonvisual prediction forms, and the overlay;
- the first-visit default and exemption handling;
- the `prediction` tape event;
- privacy rules for predictions;
- a fixture instrument for tests.

Out of scope:
- tape infrastructure (`am-rt-control-tapes-0gc`);
- chapter-end predict-perturb-explain tasks (`am-disc-ppe-teachback-wnp7`);
- per-instrument prompt authoring (instrument beads, for example the two BM-01 prompts in `am-bm-01-tracer-ensemble-hdly`).

## Requirements

### Manifest contract

An instrument declares one of two forms:

- `predictMode: { enabled: true, prompts: [...] }`, where each prompt is `{ promptId, controlId or actionId, question, candidates: [three items, each { id, label, description, curve or relation }], sketchAxes?, verbalChoices?, valueTargets? }`.
- `predictMode: { exempt: true, reason }`, for example an event ledger whose first action is itself the prediction. The audit requires a non-empty reason.

The three candidates are plausible models, each with a one-line description; never two foolish options and one right one.

### Behavior

- **Default.** On for first-time visitors of each instrument, remembered per instrument and per prompt through `am-plat-local-storage-km8f`. The reader can turn it off globally or per instrument. A storage failure falls back to "on" without errors.
- **Hidden response.** When a prompted control is engaged (focus, pointer down, or typing) before its first committed change, the response region shows empty axes with labeled units and the question. Derived readouts that would reveal the answer are hidden too. The command issues only when the reader commits the change; predicting is optional, and "skip prediction" is always available.
- **Ways to predict.**
  - Choose one of the three authored candidates.
  - Sketch a freehand line on empty axes: pointer drawing, or keyboard drawing (arrow keys move a cursor, space adds a point).
  - Nonvisual equivalent: choose the expected direction and shape in words (increase, decrease, unchanged; linear, square-root, other), or type expected values at named points.
- **Reveal.** After the first accepted snapshot following the committed change, overlay the real result on the prediction. A visible legend distinguishes "your prediction" from the computed result with non-color identity (label, line style, marker). Both remain until the reader clears them.
- **Per-prompt state.** Each prompt has its own state machine (`hidden` → `predicted` or `skipped` → `revealed` → `cleared`) driven by the instance's first command for that prompt's control. Revealing one prompt never reveals another.
- **Tape event.** Record `{ type: "prediction", instrumentId, promptId, form: "candidate" | "sketch" | "verbal" | "values", payload }` on the control tape. Sketches are simplified to a bounded point set (at most 64 points, with the tolerance documented) before serialization.
- **Privacy.** Predictions are structured choices, sketches, or numbers, never free text. They stay in local storage and enter a `?tape=` URL only when the reader copies a permalink. They are never sent to a server.
- **Feedback language.** It describes the relationship (for example, "the spread grows with the square root of time, so four times as long gives twice the typical distance") and never scores the person, uses red crosses, or implies failure.
- **Explanation access.** "Show me the reasoning" is available before and after predicting.

## Technical Approach

- A predict-state store per instance and prompt, subscribed to the instance's command stream.
- Sketch capture on a Canvas layer over the view kit's axes (`am-inst-2d-view-kit-u75r`), simplified with a documented Ramer–Douglas–Peucker tolerance in axis units.
- Uses `am-plat-local-storage-km8f` for first-visit flags and `am-rt-control-tapes-0gc` for events. Copy is checked by the voice lint (`am-edit-voice-lint-trmf`).
- A fixture instrument, registered only in the fixture build, has two prompts backed by a real reference evaluator.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Predict mode is on for first visits and can be disabled; storage failure keeps it on without errors.
- [ ] Per-prompt behavior works: engaging each prompted control first shows its own prompt, and revealing one never reveals another.
- [ ] Candidate, sketch, verbal, and value predictions work with pointer, keyboard, and screen reader; "skip prediction" is always available.
- [ ] The response and revealing readouts stay hidden until the first accepted snapshot after the committed change.
- [ ] The overlay distinguishes prediction and result without relying on color.
- [ ] Prediction events serialize into tapes, with bounded sketch payloads, and restore from permalinks. Predictions never leave the device except in a permalink the reader copies.
- [ ] Exempt instruments show no predict UI and have a recorded reason; the audit fails on an empty reason.
- [ ] No scoring language appears anywhere in predict-mode copy (voice lint rule).

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `predictState.test.ts`: transitions per prompt; skip; clear; re-predict; two prompts on one instance staying independent; storage-failure behavior (storage throwing on read and on write).
- `predictSketch.test.tsx`: pointer and keyboard sketch capture; simplification bounded at 64 points within the documented tolerance; a 10 000-point input is reduced.
- `predictTape.test.ts`: event serialization and restoration with `promptId`; bounded payload size; free text rejected.
- `predictExemption.test.ts`: manifest validation (three candidates required per prompt; empty exemption reason fails).
- `predictVoice.test.ts`: the voice lint over every predict string, including a planted "Wrong!" fixture that fails.

### End-to-end tests

On the harness fixture instrument:
- First-visit lane: axes hidden; choose a candidate for prompt A; commit a change; assert the overlay and the revealing readouts appear; engage prompt B's control and assert its own hidden state.
- Reload with a permalink and assert both predictions are restored.
- Keyboard-only lane: the verbal prediction path end to end.
- Reduced-motion lane: reveal without animation.
- Blocked-storage lane: predict mode stays on.

BM-01's two prompts are exercised in `am-bm-01-tracer-ensemble-hdly` and `am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu`.

### Structured logging

JSONL at `artifacts/test-logs/predict-mode/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `instrumentId`, `promptId`, `predictState`, `predictionForm`, `sketchPoints`, `tapeEventCount`, `snapshotVersion`, `storageState`, `outcome`, `message`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Being surprised is not the same as learning; predict mode must never delay the explanation.
- Do not equate a matching sketch with understanding; no automatic correctness judgment of free-form predictions.
- The per-instrument contract (prompts or a recorded exemption) is required by the definition of done. The plan's stop rule for this P1 innovation governs richer additions beyond that contract, such as class views of predictions or new prediction forms. Expand those only after observed readers show they resolve a misunderstanding.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-inst-registry-dispatcher-66l0`: instances and manifests.
- `am-rt-control-tapes-0gc`: prediction events on tapes.
- `am-plat-local-storage-km8f`: failure-tolerant first-visit flags.
- `am-inst-2d-view-kit-u75r`: axes, curve classes, and the overlay layer.
- `am-edit-voice-lint-trmf`: the rule that forbids scoring language.

Unblocks: prompts in every instrument bead (BM-01, BM-05, BM-06 in the slice; BM-02 to BM-08, LQ, SR, and ME instruments later), `am-disc-shelf-michelson-fizeau-dauq`, and `am-disc-avogadro-lab-pfi7`.

title: Offer true physical rate with a scale bar where a natural rate exists
description:
# Offer true physical rate with a scale bar where a natural rate exists

**Epic:** `am-ep-instruments-8gi` · **Batch:** batch-h · **Priority:** P2 · **Plan sections:** §10.2 (BM-01 real-time toggle), §10.7, §12.5, §12.6, §16.2 (traceability only)

## Background

Speeding up a random walk makes its shape visible, but it can also mislead: a reader may come away thinking Brownian particles dart about. Einstein's printed estimate says a sphere of radius half a micron in water wanders about 0.8 μm in one second, which is slow and visible in an ordinary microscope. The plan asks every instrument with a natural physical rate to offer a true-rate view, with a calibrated scale bar, beside the sped-up version.

True rate is a **presentation change**. It never changes the stochastic experiment, the time step, the seed, or the statistics; it only changes how accepted snapshots are replayed against wall-clock time.

BM-01 already declares its natural rate and ships the microscope scale bar in Batch B. This bead supplies the playback controller and the toggle, and wires them into BM-01 and the other eligible instruments.

## Scope

In scope:
- a real-rate playback controller in `src/experiments/playback/`;
- the UI toggle;
- time readouts;
- side-by-side true-rate and accelerated views;
- eligibility validation from manifests;
- wiring BM-01, and BM-05 and BM-06 where eligible.

Out of scope:
- runtime stepping (`am-rt-worker-scheduler-7tl`);
- the tape format (`am-rt-control-tapes-0gc`);
- the scale-bar drawing primitive (`am-inst-2d-view-kit-u75r`);
- the kitchen real-data mode's own player (`am-bm-07-kitchen-mode-mays`, which reuses this controller).

## Requirements

- **Eligibility** is declared in each manifest's `realRate` field (per `am-cm-schemas-experiment-fuu`): `{ natural: true, quantity, scaleBar }`. The quantity is the output whose physical rate is shown (for BM-01, `rmsDisplacement1d`); the scale bar gives a calibrated length.
  - Initial eligible set: BM-01 (tracer wandering at microscope scale); BM-05 and BM-06 when their views run against physical time; the kitchen real-data mode (video frame rate).
  - Instruments whose natural rates are unwatchable, such as $0.6c$ motion or optical frequencies, declare `natural: false` and show no toggle.
- **Command class.** The toggle issues a `presentation-change` command. Accepted snapshot identities, run id, seed, and statistics remain unchanged.
- **Playback clock.** Simulated time maps to wall time at 1:1 using host-fed time, and interpolation affects display only. If the replay grid is coarser than the display frame rate, the view holds or interpolates and labels the interpolation as rendering. Playback never requests new draws or steps.
- **Readouts.** A time readout in seconds of simulated time. Side-by-side mode shows the true-rate and accelerated views with their speed factors labeled ("true rate" and "25 times faster").
- **Reduced motion.** True-rate animation does not autoplay. A step control and a static description of the displacement per second are shown.
- **Accessible summary**, computed from the snapshot with its constant set named. Example: "At true rate, a tracer of radius 0.5 μm in water at 17 °C moves a typical 0.79 μm in one second (Einstein's printed values; 0.89 μm with the modern viscosity of water at that temperature)."

## Technical Approach

A playback clock bound to the instance store consumes snapshots on the instrument's declared replay grid and display cadence. No new draws or steps are requested because of playback speed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Eligible instruments show the toggle; ineligible ones do not; manifest validation rejects `natural: true` without a quantity and scale bar.
- [ ] Switching rates leaves snapshot identities, run id, seed, and statistics unchanged.
- [ ] At true rate, the positions drawn at wall-clock time $t$ equal the snapshot's positions at simulated time $t$ on the replay grid.
- [ ] Scale bars are calibrated from snapshot and manifest data; time readouts show simulated seconds.
- [ ] Reduced motion disables autoplay and provides step controls and a textual rate summary.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `realRate.clock.test.ts`: the 1:1 mapping with host-fed time; hold and interpolation labels when the grid is coarser than the frame rate; no step or draw requests from the clock (the runtime's draw counter is unchanged).
- `realRate.invariance.test.ts`: a presentation change leaves the run id, seed, accepted input revision, latent digest, and computed moments unchanged.
- `realRate.eligibility.test.ts`: manifest validation for eligible and ineligible instruments.
- `realRate.summary.test.ts`: summary numbers come from the snapshot. The Einstein preset gives 0.7947833 μm; the modern-viscosity preset gives 0.8871979 μm; the constant set is named.

### End-to-end tests

BM-01 lane:
- toggle true rate;
- advance host time by exactly 1 s through the harness clock;
- assert that the projected pixel positions of the drawn tracers equal the projection of the snapshot's positions at simulated $t = 1$ s, within 1 px;
- assert that the statistics panel and snapshot identity are unchanged;
- in the reduced-motion lane, assert the step controls and the summary appear.

### Structured logging

JSONL at `artifacts/test-logs/real-rate/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `instrumentId`, `playbackRate`, `runId` (the experiment realization), `snapshotVersion`, `simulatedTime`, `wallTime`, `maxPixelDeviation`, `drawCountBefore`, `drawCountAfter`, `outcome`, `message`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Never compute a speed from the rendered polyline; the displayed motion is a rendering of sampled positions.
- Render cadence must never change the experiment.
- "Typical distance in one second" is the RMS displacement, not a speed; the summary must not say "moves at."

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-inst-registry-dispatcher-66l0`: manifests and instance binding.
- `am-rt-control-tapes-0gc`: host-fed time and replay semantics.
- `am-inst-2d-view-kit-u75r`: the scale bar and trajectory layer.
- `am-bm-01-tracer-ensemble-hdly`: the first eligible instrument, whose toggle this bead wires.

Unblocks: BM-01's true-rate toggle, the kitchen mode's video-rate replay, and `am-launch-readiness-audit-sc9b`.

title: Build the exhaustive experiment registry and dispatcher where unknown ids fail explicitly
description:
# Build the exhaustive experiment registry and dispatcher where unknown ids fail explicitly

**Epic:** `am-ep-instruments-8gi` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §2.2, §2.3, §10.1, §10.8, §12.1, §12.5, §12.12, §17.3, §19.6 (traceability only)

## Background

The donor museum defaulted its visual dispatcher to the Wright Flyer, so an unregistered record silently showed another patent's machine. On a scientific edition that failure is worse than a crash: a reader would see a plausible, wrong model and trust it. The plan's rule is absolute: **every experiment id has an explicit case, and an unknown id fails explicitly.**

The registry is also where the ownership rule becomes enforceable. Each instrument binds to one computational owner through the runtime: a reference evaluator, a FrankenSim capability, or an explicit static status. Views consume only accepted snapshots. The dispatcher lazily loads each instrument's views so heavy code never enters the reading route.

The catalogue is built gradually. In Batch B only BM-01, BM-05, and BM-06 have manifests, while readings, first encounters, foundations, and discovery routes already reference other catalogue ids. Those references must resolve to an honest "in preparation" state, never to a dead link, a build failure, or another instrument.

## Scope

In scope:
- `src/experiments/catalogue.ts`: the typed list of every catalogue id and mode;
- `src/experiments/registry.ts`: the entries generated from compiled manifests;
- `src/experiments/owners.ts`: hand-written owner bindings;
- `src/experiments/dispatch.tsx`: the lazy dispatcher;
- manifest loading from `content/experiments/<id>.yaml`;
- the explicit unknown, in-preparation, and unavailable-on-device states;
- the architectural guards that stop views from importing owners or computing physics or statistics.

Out of scope:
- the snapshot store and worker runtime (`am-rt-snapshot-store-aft`, `am-rt-worker-scheduler-7tl`);
- controls (`am-inst-parameter-controls-cmj9`);
- the lab route (`am-inst-lab-route-f8f3`);
- the public preview policy (`am-rel-preview-policy-cf6g`, whose in-preparation wording this bead reuses);
- individual instruments.

## Requirements

### Catalogue and registry

- **Catalogue ids** are a closed TypeScript union: `lq-01` … `lq-09`, `bm-01` … `bm-08`, `sr-01` … `sr-13`, `me-01` … `me-03`, plus shelf instrument ids added when their beads define them. Modes are addressed as `lq-08:count-model` and validated against the registered modes.
- Each catalogue id has an explicit status: `registered` when a compiled manifest exists, or `in-preparation`.
- A `switch` over catalogue ids ends in an exhaustiveness check (`const _exhaustive: never = id`), so adding an id without a case fails typecheck. There is no default case.
- **A registered entry** references its compiled `Experiment` manifest: question, source and argument ids, parameter schema, outputs with statuses and the primary output, views, default scenario, provenance, `notModeled`, acceptance cases, tape model identity, embeddable flag, predict-mode prompts or exemption, and action contract.
- **Owner bindings.** Each registered entry names exactly one owner binding, using the manifest schema's owner kinds:
  - `{ kind: "reference-evaluator", module, function }`;
  - `{ kind: "frankensim", capability, export }` with a named reference-evaluator fallback;
  - `{ kind: "static" }` for a static worked example.

  An entry without an owner or explicit static status fails the build; this rule is shared with the content compiler.

### Dispatcher

- `ExperimentView({ id, mode, instanceId })` resolves the catalogue status and, for registered ids, lazy-loads the view module with `next/dynamic` (`ssr: false` for Canvas and WebGL views). The static worked example from the compiled payload renders in the server HTML, so the page stays meaningful without JavaScript.
- **Unknown ids** (not in the catalogue) render "This experiment is not available here," with the requested id, a link to the paper passage if one is known, and no substitute instrument.
- **Catalogue ids without a manifest** render "This experiment is in preparation," with its explanatory question from the catalogue when authored and a link to the source passage. No controls, numbers, or look-alike scene appear, and an audit lists every in-preparation reference.
- **Unavailable on this device** means no dedicated worker can be created, or WebGL is missing for a 3D-only view. It renders the public label "This experiment is unavailable on this device" plus the static worked example.
- **WASM missing, blocked, or mismatched** does not make an experiment unavailable. The runtime uses the registered reference-evaluator fallback in the worker, and the snapshot is labeled "Ideal model, host calculation" (`am-rt-determinism-fallbacks-8i4`).
- Views receive an `instanceId` and subscribe to the instance store; two mounted instances of the same experiment are independent.

### Architectural guards

- **Import guard.** A lint rule or import-graph test fails if any module under `src/visuals/` or an instrument view directory imports `src/physics/reference/*`, a WASM loader, or a sample-statistics function. Views get numbers only from accepted snapshots.
- **Forbidden-call scan.** A test scans view modules and fails with the file and line if it finds:
  - `Math.random` anywhere in a view;
  - `Math.exp`, `Math.sqrt`, `Math.log`, `erf`, or a loop accumulating sums of squares, outside rendering helpers listed in an allowlist file (`src/visuals/allowlist.json`) that records a reason per helper, such as pixel projection or easing.
- **Manifest parity.** A test enumerates every manifest in `content/experiments/` and asserts a registered catalogue entry exists for it, and that every `registered` status has a manifest.
- **Catalogue parity.** A test asserts the catalogue contains exactly the 33 core ids and the shelf ids defined so far.

## Technical Approach

- The registry is generated at build time from compiled manifests into a typed module. Owner bindings are hand-written in `src/experiments/owners.ts`.
- Dispatcher tests use the real registry and real compiled fixtures, not mocks. Test-only fixture experiments are registered only in the fixture build flag, which the architecture gate proves never ships.
- Adapt the donor `dispatcher.test.ts` pattern, replacing its Wright default with explicit failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every catalogue id has an explicit case; the exhaustiveness check compiles only when all ids are handled.
- [ ] An unknown id renders the explicit "not available here" state, and a test proves no other instrument renders.
- [ ] A catalogue id without a manifest renders the explicit "in preparation" state with no controls or numbers.
- [ ] A manifest without an owner or static status fails the build with an actionable message.
- [ ] Views cannot import reference evaluators, WASM loaders, or statistics functions; the guard fails on a planted violation in a fixture directory.
- [ ] Heavy view modules are absent from the initial reading-route bundle (bundle analysis assertion).
- [ ] Two instances of the same experiment on one page do not share state.
- [ ] With JavaScript disabled, the static worked example appears in place of each registered instrument.
- [ ] A blocked WASM artifact yields the host-calculation fallback, not the unavailable state; a blocked worker yields the unavailable state.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `catalogue.test.ts`: the 33 core ids; mode grammar; status per id; the exhaustiveness check (a type-level test fails to compile when a case is removed).
- `registry.test.ts`: manifests and entries in both directions; owner-binding validity; owner kinds equal to the manifest schema's; mode addressing.
- `dispatch.test.tsx`: the unknown-id state; the in-preparation state; the unavailable-device state; WASM-missing falls back to host; lazy loading; instance independence, using a test-only fixture experiment.
- `viewImportGuard.test.ts`: the import-graph check with a planted violation fixture, including an import of a statistics function.
- `forbiddenCalls.test.ts`: a planted `Math.random` and a planted sum-of-squares loop in fixture views fail, and an allowlisted easing helper passes.

### End-to-end tests

Through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`, on a fixture route in the fixture build:
- an unknown experiment id shows the explicit text;
- a catalogue id without a manifest (for example `bm-02` in Batch B) shows the in-preparation state;
- two instances of the fixture experiment: changing one control leaves the other's snapshot id unchanged;
- the JavaScript-disabled lane shows the static examples;
- the worker-blocked lane shows the unavailable label.

The BM-01 two-instance and fallback lanes run in `am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu`.

### Structured logging

- JSONL at `artifacts/test-logs/registry/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `instrumentId`, `catalogueStatus`, `instanceId`, `ownerKind`, `executionLabel`, `outcome`, `message`.
- Bundle assertions log the route and byte counts.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Resist a generic "fallback instrument." A missing case is a bug that must be visible.
- "In preparation" is honest only if it shows nothing that looks like a result.
- Keep the catalogue finite: modes of a shared workbench are registered as modes, not new ids.
- Do not generalize registry features beyond what the Brownian slice needs until `am-bm-slice-retrospective-pp09`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-cm-schemas-experiment-fuu`: the manifest schema the registry reads.
- `am-rt-snapshot-store-aft`: the instance-scoped stores the dispatcher binds views to.

Unblocks:
- `am-inst-predict-mode-ti7m`, `am-inst-show-the-code-4brv`, `am-inst-lab-route-f8f3`, `am-inst-real-rate-mode-gtez`.
- `am-a11y-action-contracts-k75g`, `am-disc-journey-framework-umbg`, `am-disc-shelf-michelson-fizeau-dauq`, `am-read-results-face-uzh`.

title: Extract and pin kernel source for show-the-code with colorized identifiers and binding tests
description:
# Extract and pin kernel source for show-the-code with colorized identifiers and binding tests

**Epic:** `am-ep-instruments-8gi` · **Batch:** batch-b · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §7.8, §11.7, §12.12, §15.5, §17.3 (extract-kernel-source.ts) (traceability only)

## Background

"For programmers the code is the derivation; for everyone else it is proof that the number on the screen came from a function anyone can read." Every instrument and every derivation chain gets a "Show the code" disclosure. It renders the kernel's actual source (the TypeScript reference evaluator, and the Rust of the FrankenSim owner where it applies), extracted at build time with the function's source hash pinned to the instrument.

Identifiers that correspond to equation terms share the term's color. `gamma` in the code, $\gamma$ in the formula, and "the stretch factor" in the sentence are visibly the same quantity. The compiler also uses this binding as a correctness check: an instrument whose live terms do not appear as identifiers in its pinned kernel source fails the build.

This bead lands after the three slice instruments (BM-01, BM-05, BM-06) and retrofits them. Their manifests already list their kernel functions and identifier bindings; this bead moves those lists into typed fields, pins hashes, and renders the disclosures, so no core instrument is left without one. Show-the-code is not an exit prerequisite of the slice. Its manifest fields are an additive extension to the frozen experiment schema.

## Scope

In scope:
- `scripts/extract-kernel-source.ts` and the build manifest of extracted functions and hashes;
- the typed manifest fields `kernelFunctions[]` and `identifierBindings[]`;
- the disclosure component;
- identifier-to-quantity bindings and colorization;
- the kernel-identifier binding check registered into `verify-content.ts`;
- Rust extraction from the pinned FrankenSim revision;
- the retrofit of BM-01, BM-05, and BM-06.

Out of scope:
- the semantic color system (`am-design-semantic-color-8vbq`);
- equation components (`am-eq-colorized-component-1z8`);
- other compiler semantic rejections (`am-cm-checks-semantic-lic`, which deliberately does not own the kernel-identifier check);
- per-instrument lists for later instruments, which each instrument bead supplies.

## Requirements

### Extraction

- Each instrument manifest and derivation chain names its kernel functions:
  - `{ language: "ts", module, exportName }`;
  - `{ language: "rust", crate, path, fnName, revision }`.
- **TypeScript extraction** uses the TypeScript compiler API to locate the exported function by symbol and emit its exact source text, including JSDoc. It never uses a regex slice.
- **Rust extraction** reads the pinned FrankenSim revision recorded in `docs/FRANKENSIM_BINDING.md` (written by `am-fs-capability-audit-byc`) and locates the function with a Rust parser, or with a documented, tested, robust token scan. It emits exact source.
- **Delegating exports.** When `am-fs-diffusion-owner-sey` moves a law into a generic crate and an `fs-wasm` export only delegates, the manifest names the owner crate's function (the law) and also the export wrapper. The disclosure shows both, labeled "law" and "browser export."
- **Records.** For each extracted function, record `sourceHash` (SHA-256 of the source normalized to LF), file path, line range, and revision. The output is `generated/kernel-sources.json`, consumed by the build.
- **Drift check.** If the source changes without the manifest's pinned hash being updated, the build fails with a message naming the instrument, the function, and the old and new hashes. A FrankenSim re-pin updates hashes in the same adoption commit.

### Bindings and colorization

- The manifest declares identifier bindings such as `{ identifier: "gamma", quantityId: "lorentzFactor" }`. Colorization applies the role color of the quantity id from the semantic color system, with a non-color identity (an underline style, or a label on focus).
- **Binding test.** Every live term of an instrument's equations (exact canonical quantity ids) must have at least one binding whose identifier appears in the extracted source of a listed kernel function. A missing identifier fails the build.
- Hovering or focusing a colored identifier highlights the matching term in the equation and the sentence on the page, when present.

### Disclosure UI

- A "Show the code" disclosure sits beside the model note.
- It is static HTML with build-time syntax highlighting, so it works without JavaScript. Code blocks scroll locally, never the page. A copy button is optional.
- The header shows the function name, file, revision, source hash, and execution context. "This is the function that produced the current snapshot" appears only when the accepted snapshot's per-output provenance names that function for the output being described (see `am-inst-execution-labels-5ywv`). Otherwise the header says which outputs the function computes when it runs.

### Retrofit of the slice instruments

- **BM-01:** `stokesEinsteinD`, `rmsDisplacement`, `apparentSpeed`, `ensembleMoments`, `displacementHistogram` (TypeScript), and `brownian_frames` with its owner law (Rust). Bindings: `diffusion`/`D` → `diffusionCoefficient`; `eta` → `viscosity`; `radius`/`a` → `particleRadius`; `temperature`/`T` → `temperature`; `dt` → `observationInterval`; `rms` → `rmsDisplacement1d`.
- **BM-05:** the kernel samplers (Rust `brownian_frames` kernels 0–2 and TypeScript `brownianFrames`), `kernelDiffusivity`, `randomWalkMoments`, and `coinWalkDistribution`, with their bindings.
- **BM-06:** `gaussianPropagator`, `intervalProbability`, `erf`/`erfc`, `radialPropagator2d`, `radialPropagator3d`, `ftcs1d`, and Rust `diffusion1d_frames`, with their bindings.
- For each of the three: move the lists from the manifest's provenance notes into the typed fields, pin the hashes, render the disclosure, and pass the binding test.

### Compiler rule

Register the rejection "an instrument's live terms do not appear as identifiers in its pinned kernel source" in `verify-content.ts`, which `am-cm-audit-scripts-d34` creates.

## Technical Approach

- The build step runs after content compilation and before the Next.js build; its outputs are deterministic.
- Highlighting uses a build-time highlighter with a restricted grammar set (TypeScript and Rust) and produces sanitized HTML.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Extraction produces exact source text and stable hashes for TypeScript and Rust functions, including delegating exports and their owner laws.
- [ ] A changed kernel without an updated pinned hash fails the build with a clear message.
- [ ] A missing identifier binding for a live term fails the build, and the rule runs in `verify-content.ts`.
- [ ] The disclosure renders statically without JavaScript and highlights bound identifiers with role colors plus non-color identity.
- [ ] The header claims "produced the current snapshot" only when per-output provenance names the function.
- [ ] BM-01, BM-05, and BM-06 each have their disclosure, pinned hashes, and passing bindings.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `extractKernelSource.test.ts`: fixtures for exported functions, overloaded names, re-exports, JSDoc retention, CRLF normalization, and hash stability across two runs.
- `extractRustSource.test.ts`: a fixture crate with nested modules, attributes, a `#[wasm_bindgen]` wrapper that delegates to an owner function, and generic functions.
- `kernelBinding.test.ts`: a planted missing identifier fails with the instrument and quantity id named; correct bindings pass; the BM-01, BM-05, and BM-06 real manifests pass.
- `pinnedHash.test.ts`: editing a fixture kernel without updating the manifest fails with old and new hashes.
- `showTheCode.test.tsx`: static rendering; sanitized HTML (a planted `<script>` in a comment is escaped); owner-match header logic with a composite-provenance snapshot.

### End-to-end tests

- JavaScript-disabled lane: the native `details` disclosure opens and shows highlighted code for BM-06.
- BM-01 lane: focusing the `diffusion` identifier highlights the $D$ term in the equation card.
- A header lane with WASM blocked: the Rust function's header does not claim to have produced the current snapshot.

### Structured logging

JSONL at `artifacts/test-logs/show-the-code/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `instrumentId`, `function`, `language`, `sourceHash`, `revision`, `bindingCount`, `missingBindings`, `producedCurrentSnapshot`, `outcome`, `message`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Never show a function that did not produce the number and imply it did; the owner-match rule prevents that.
- Keep extraction deterministic so release manifests are reproducible.
- A binding test that only checks identifier presence can pass for an unused variable. Pair it with the scenario tests that exercise the function, which the instrument audit already requires.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-inst-registry-dispatcher-66l0`: manifests and owner bindings.
- `am-eq-colorized-component-1z8`: term colors and cross-highlighting hooks.
- `am-cm-audit-scripts-d34`: `verify-content.ts`, where the kernel-identifier check is registered.
- `am-fs-capability-audit-byc`: the pinned FrankenSim revision in `docs/FRANKENSIM_BINDING.md`.
- `am-bm-01-tracer-ensemble-hdly`, `am-bm-05-random-steps-ntzl`, `am-bm-06-gaussian-spread-982y`: the instruments this bead retrofits.

Unblocks: the compiler rule for instrument live terms, and every later instrument's show-the-code requirement (the LQ, SR, ME, BM-02 to BM-08 instruments, `am-disc-shelf-michelson-fizeau-dauq`, `am-disc-avogadro-lab-pfi7`, and the per-paper definition-of-done audits).

title: Adapt the Three.js studio for the few spatial instruments with disposal, context-loss handling, and fallbacks
description:
# Adapt the Three.js studio for the few spatial instruments with disposal, context-loss handling, and fallbacks

**Epic:** `am-ep-instruments-8gi` · **Batch:** batch-e · **Priority:** P2 · **Plan sections:** §2.3 (ThreeStudioScene), §10.9, §12.7, §12.8, §15.5, §16.2, §16.4 (traceability only)

## Background

Three.js is a presentation tool, not a scientific authority. The plan permits it only where the mechanism is spatial and a 2D view genuinely loses information:

- the sphere measured as an ellipsoid with a clock (the SR-03 and SR-05 studio);
- field lines in two frames (SR-08);
- the 1906 photon-in-a-box extension (the optional 3D view of ME-03's box extension);
- an optional spacetime block view (later).

Everything else is SVG or Canvas. Rendering detail and model fidelity are independent settings: a richly rendered body can sit on top of a simple analytic ledger.

The donor museum's `ThreeStudioScene.ts` supplies a proven studio pattern (lighting, camera presets, HUD chips). This bead adapts it to scenes that are driven by snapshots, disposable, and safe under WebGL context loss.

## Scope

In scope:
- `src/visuals/three/studio/`, adapted from the donor with license notices;
- procedural geometry builders for the listed scenes' shared parts: an ellipsoid from snapshot axes, clock faces, field-line tubes from sampled polylines, and box and pulse markers;
- lifecycle management and fallbacks;
- HUD integration with execution labels and semantic colors.

Out of scope:
- the per-scene instruments (`am-srk-sphere-clock-studio-lpxr`, `am-sre-field-lines-studio-4882`, `am-me-03-box-3d-view-ln42`, `am-later-deep-spacetime-block-7dai`);
- the 2D box extension itself (`am-me-03-box-extension-kiei`);
- physics owners.

## Requirements

- **Snapshot-driven.** Scenes read only accepted snapshot data: axes, clock readings, sampled field lines, positions. No physics in render loops; no `Math.random`.
- **Procedural geometry.** Geometry is built from snapshot quantities, never from marketplace model files. Geometry builders are pure functions, testable without WebGL.
- **Lazy and isolated.** Loaded by dynamic import only when a spatial scene is requested; never in the initial reading route.
- **Lifecycle.**
  - Dispose geometries, materials, textures, render targets, controls, and listeners on unmount.
  - Reuse buffers across snapshot updates.
  - Pause rendering when invisible.
  - Limit concurrent WebGL contexts per page (at most two, with an explanatory pause for a third).
- **Context loss.** Handle `webglcontextlost` by pausing the laboratory and showing the static 2D representation and text. On `webglcontextrestored`, rebuild from the current snapshot without restarting the run or consuming randomness.
- **No-WebGL fallback.** Show the 2D view or the static worked example, with the same accessible descriptions and tables.
- **HUD.**
  - The execution label and a model-note link, as text.
  - Numeric readouts formatted from the snapshot.
  - Colorized terms using role colors keyed to quantity ids from the semantic color system, with non-color identity, consistent with the equations.
- **Camera and presets.** Named presets. Camera motion is presentation only and never implies changed physics. Axis scaling is shown when relevant.
- **Reduced motion.** No auto-rotation or animated transitions; the posed scene reflects the current state.
- **Accessibility.** Each scene has a textual description and an inspectable table of the displayed quantities, supplied through the graph-description framework.

## Technical Approach

- Adapt the donor studio (scene setup, lights, camera presets, HUD chips) into a small factory: `createStudio({ canvas, presets, onContextLost })`, returning explicit `update(snapshot)` and `dispose()` methods.
- Use Three.js directly; the donor declares `three`, not React Three Fiber.
- Resource counts come from the real renderer's `renderer.info` and from tracked listeners, never from a substituted renderer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The studio factory provides update and dispose; geometry builders are covered by unit tests without WebGL.
- [ ] 50 mount and unmount cycles show no growth in WebGL contexts, geometries, textures, or listeners.
- [ ] A forced context loss pauses the lab and shows the 2D fallback; restoration rebuilds from the snapshot with the same run id and an unchanged draw counter.
- [ ] The no-WebGL lane renders the fallback with descriptions and tables.
- [ ] The studio code is absent from the initial reading-route bundle.
- [ ] Reduced motion disables automatic camera motion.
- [ ] HUD colors come from the semantic color system, with non-color identity.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `studioGeometry.test.ts`:
  - ellipsoid semi-axes from $R$ and $\beta$ are $(R\sqrt{1-\beta^2}, R, R)$, for example $(0.8R, R, R)$ at $\beta = 0.6$;
  - clock hand angles from readings;
  - field-line tube construction from sampled points;
  - degenerate inputs ($\beta = 0$, a single sample point) handled without `NaN`.
- `studioLifecycle.test.ts`: runs in headless Chromium with a real WebGL context (software rasterizer) and the real Three.js renderer, with no stub. It counts `renderer.info.memory.geometries` and `textures`, live contexts, and registered listeners across 50 mount and unmount cycles.
- `studioHud.test.tsx`: label text; role colors from the semantic color system; non-color identity.

### End-to-end tests

- Chromium and WebKit lanes:
  - mount a fixture scene;
  - force `WEBGL_lose_context`, then assert the pause and the fallback;
  - restore, then assert an identical run id and draw counter.
- A resource stress lane with repeated route changes.
- A no-WebGL lane.
- A reduced-motion lane.

### Structured logging

JSONL at `artifacts/test-logs/three-studio/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `scene`, `runId` (the experiment realization), `snapshotVersion`, `webglContexts`, `geometries`, `textures`, `listeners`, `contextEvents`, `outcome`, `message`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Do not let the studio become a reason to build 3D scenes for 1D phenomena.
- Keep the donor license notice on adapted files.
- A software-rasterized context in CI is slower; keep performance assertions out of these lanes and leave them to `am-plat-perf-budgets-s3ww`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-scaf-extract-ui-components-c31`: the extracted donor studio source.
- `am-rt-memory-lifecycle-5ws`: buffer ownership, visibility pausing, and recovery rules.
- `am-inst-execution-labels-5ywv`: the label and expandable model note in the HUD.
- `am-a11y-graph-descriptions-vxe1`: three-layer textual descriptions and inspectable tables.
- `am-design-semantic-color-8vbq`: role colors keyed to quantity ids.

Unblocks: `am-srk-sphere-clock-studio-lpxr`, `am-sre-field-lines-studio-4882`, `am-me-03-box-3d-view-ln42`, `am-later-deep-spacetime-block-7dai`.

title: Later and unscheduled: the 1906 Brownian follow-up, the 1907 review, printable broadsides, community translations
description:
# Later and unscheduled: the 1906 Brownian follow-up, the 1907 review, printable broadsides, community translations

**Epic:** `am-ep-later-gap` · **Batch:** later · **Priority:** P4 · **Labels:** companion-dissertation · **Plan sections:** §3.7, §19.7 "Later, unscheduled" (traceability only)

## Background

The plan closes its delivery section with work it deliberately leaves unscheduled: "the 1906 Brownian follow-up and the 1907 review article as further companion records; a printable broadside per paper; community translations of the readings against the same alignment." These extend the edition without changing its identity. The molecular-dimensions dissertation establishes the companion pattern first: a companion is labeled as such, never appears on the hero, never becomes a flagship by accretion, and never delays the four papers.

**Why later:** each item depends on patterns proven by the launch (companion records, print styles, review records). **Start only when:** the dissertation companion record exists and has been reviewed, the four-paper edition has launched, and the user chooses one item. When an item starts, split it into its own bead with a full specification.

## Scope

In scope: this bead is a holding record that specifies the three items well enough to split later.
Out of scope: starting any item without the conditions above.

## Requirements

**1. Further companion records.**
- The 1906 Brownian follow-up, "Zur Theorie der Brownschen Bewegung," Ann. Phys. (4) 19, 371–381 (1906), which among other things discusses apparent velocity measured over an observation interval. It is the natural home for that discussion if the 1905 text does not contain it.
