9. **Headers.** `.wasm` responses carry `Content-Type: application/wasm`; the Content-Security-Policy header is present and allows the worker and WASM loading path without broad `unsafe-eval`. Cache-header assertions are registered by `am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre` as check `cache-headers`.
10. **Top-level routes.** At launch: `/`, `/papers`, `/sources`, `/about`, `/timeline`, `/foundations`, `/notation`, `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml` respond 200 with non-trivial bodies.
11. **Profile states.** In `preview`, every unpublished paper shows its honest in-preparation state, and its draft text is absent from HTML, the search index, and machine-readable exports (`am-rel-preview-policy-cf6g`). In `scaffold`, no paper text is served.
12. **Same-origin only.** While loading every page in checks 2 to 5 and 10, the browser makes no request to any origin other than the deployment's own (no third-party scripts, fonts, analytics, or images).

**Flakiness policy.** Transport errors (DNS, connection reset, timeout before first byte) may retry at most twice with backoff, and each retry is logged. Assertion failures never retry.

## Technical Approach

Reuse the Playwright harness, its DOM readiness contract, and the JSONL logger from `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`. Derive routes, block ids, experiment ids, capabilities, and golden values from compiled content and the manifest, never from hand lists, so new content is checked automatically. Run instrument checks with bounded concurrency (at most 4 pages).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every check in the catalogue is implemented, profile-aware, and logged, and the registration interface accepts checks from other beads.
- [ ] Checks run against the candidate URL and fetched bytes, never the local build directory.
- [ ] A failing check refuses promotion, and the release script proves it with an injected failure.
- [ ] The accepted-WASM and typed-refusal checks assert the manifest digest and the refusal semantics, not merely that a page loaded.
- [ ] Retries apply only to transport errors and are logged.
- [ ] The catalogue runs in `--promote` mode against an existing deployment without needing a local build.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `scripts/candidate-checks.test.ts`: route and block-id derivation from fixture content; profile applicability table; transport-versus-assertion retry classification; forbidden-string detection; header policy parsing; SHA-256 comparison of fetched fixtures; manifest digest mismatch refusal; registration of an extra check by id with duplicate-id rejection.
- Check-logic self-tests on the harness's static fixture server: one correct and one deliberately broken fixture per check (for example a page with a `frankensim` label but a mismatched artifact digest, a refusal that renders `NaN`, a page loading a third-party font), each broken fixture failing for its intended reason.
- An integration run of the full catalogue against a local production build of the current commit served by `next start` (no test-only content is compiled into the application).

### End-to-end tests
- Run against a real unpromoted deployment during the first authorized preview or launch candidate (evidence recorded in the release record). Lanes: desktop Chromium for the full catalogue, plus a WebKit pass for checks 2, 3, and 6.

### Structured logging
- `artifacts/test-logs/candidate-checks/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `logRunId`, `profile`, `mode`, `deploymentUrl`, `checkId`, `owner`, `paper`, `anchor`, `instrumentId`, `capability`, `artifactDigest`, `executionLabel`, `resultStatus`, `expected`, `actual`, `comparisonKind`, `attempt`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `browser`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, `message`. Failures retain a screenshot, Playwright trace, DOM snapshot, console log, network log, and the fetched response headers. The run summary goes into the retained release record.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Checking the build directory instead of the deployment is exactly the mistake this bead prevents.
- A loaded WASM file does not earn the FrankenSim label; only an accepted result does, so check 6 must read the snapshot, not the network log.
- Keep the allowlist of console messages small and reviewed; a growing allowlist hides regressions.
- A candidate promoted days after its first checks can be affected by expired bypass secrets or retention; rerunning the catalogue in `--promote` mode is what catches that.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-rel-release-manifest-3gna`: checks compare deployed bytes against the manifest.
- `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`: the browser driver, lanes, DOM contract, and JSONL logging are reused.
- Proposed in review: `am-inst-lab-route-f8f3` (check 5 loads `/lab/<id>`), `am-read-shell-routes-3ua` (check 2 loads paper faces), `am-found-library-infra-002t` (check 4 loads foundation pages), `am-inst-execution-labels-5ywv` (checks 5 and 6 read the execution label), `am-plat-security-f644` (check 9 asserts the Content-Security-Policy).

Unblocks:
- `am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre`: promotion, smoke testing, and rollback follow passing candidate checks.

title: Configure the Cloudflare zone for Vercel with explicit authorization
description:
# Configure the Cloudflare zone for Vercel with explicit authorization

**Epic:** `am-ep-release-as1` · **Batch:** batch-i · **Priority:** P1 · **Labels:** human-gate · **Plan sections:** §18.1, §18.2 (traceability only)

## Background

The domain `annus-mirabilis.com` is registered at Cloudflare, which also serves authoritative DNS. The site itself is hosted on Vercel; registration at Cloudflare does not imply hosting there. The plan fixes the zone configuration: apex and `www` records per Vercel's current instructions, **DNS-only (grey cloud)** at launch so Vercel manages certificates and edge caching without a second proxy layer; CAA records when the zone has any; DNSSEC once records are stable; a null MX with SPF and DMARC reject so nobody can send mail as the domain; and `https://annus-mirabilis.com` canonical with `www` redirecting consistently. Vercel's own guidance warns that putting an extra proxy in front complicates caching, routing, and request visibility. Changing DNS and attaching a domain are outward-facing and the plan does not authorize them, so this is a human-gate bead.

Attaching a domain to a Vercel project makes it serve some deployment of that project, and the deployment it serves is not necessarily the one intended (for example the newest production deployment could be an unpromoted candidate). The configuration is therefore verified by asking what the domain actually serves, and corrected through the verified release script if needed.

## Scope

In scope: attaching both hostnames to the Vercel project, the Cloudflare records, CAA, DNSSEC, mail-spoofing protection, the canonical redirect, verification of what the hostnames serve, and documentation in `docs/RELEASE.md`.
Out of scope: Vercel project creation (`am-rel-vercel-setup-ituk`); what content is promoted (`am-rel-preview-policy-cf6g`, `am-launch-public-release-5nkq`); moving hosting to Cloudflare (`am-rel-cloudflare-hosting-experiment-n7re`).

## Requirements

1. **Authorization.** Obtain the user's explicit written authorization in the current conversation for (a) adding the domains to the Vercel project, (b) each Cloudflare zone change, and (c) any alias move needed to make the domains serve the intended page. Record quotes and timestamps; an alias move also needs an authorization file for the release script.
2. **Timing and holding page.** Attach the custom domains only when the apex will serve an honest page: the in-preparation scaffold placeholder (moved onto the custom domains with `bun scripts/verified-production-deploy.ts --profile scaffold --promote <scaffold deployment> --include-custom-domains --authorization <file>`), an authorized preview, or the launch release. Never expose an unreviewed candidate as if it were the site.
3. **Records from Vercel, not from memory.** Add `annus-mirabilis.com` and `www.annus-mirabilis.com` in the Vercel project, then read the exact records Vercel displays for this project (apex `A` value or values, and the `www` `CNAME` target). **Use the exact records supplied for the project, not addresses copied from a plan or a blog.**
4. **Cloudflare DNS records:**
   - Apex `A` (and `AAAA` only if Vercel instructs) with the Vercel-supplied values, **proxy status DNS only**.
   - `www` `CNAME` to the Vercel-supplied target, **DNS only**.
   - **CAA:** if the zone has any CAA records, add records permitting the certificate authority Vercel currently uses (confirm from Vercel's documentation at execution time). If the zone has none, adding none leaves every CA permitted.
   - **Email (the domain sends no mail):** null MX `MX 0 .` at the apex (RFC 7505); SPF `TXT "v=spf1 -all"` at the apex; DMARC `TXT "v=DMARC1; p=reject; sp=reject; adkim=s; aspf=s"` at `_dmarc`. Add aggregate-report addresses only if the user asks, because reports route mail about the domain to a third party. Optionally, if the user approves, an empty DKIM wildcard `*._domainkey TXT "v=DKIM1; p="` as additional parked-domain hardening.
   - **DNSSEC:** enable in Cloudflare once the records are stable and Vercel shows a valid configuration with issued certificates. With Cloudflare as registrar the DS record is published at the registry automatically; verify it.
5. **What the hostnames serve.** After DNS resolves, run `vercel inspect https://annus-mirabilis.com` and `vercel inspect https://www.annus-mirabilis.com` and confirm they serve the intended deployment (the holding page, the preview, or the release). If not, move them with the verified script under authorization; never with a hand-typed alias command.
6. **Canonical host.** In Vercel's domain settings, make the apex the primary domain and redirect `www` to it with a permanent redirect. The site's canonical links and `metadataBase` use `https://annus-mirabilis.com`. HTTP redirects to HTTPS. Record the `Strict-Transport-Security` header actually served; do not add `preload` or submit the domain to the HSTS preload list without the user's explicit authorization, because it is hard to reverse.
7. **Proxied mode stays off at launch.** Enabling the orange cloud later requires SSL mode Full (strict), a review of Vercel's documented caveats, and a new authorization.
8. **Documentation.** `docs/RELEASE.md` records every record (type, name, value, proxy status, TTL), the date and authorization, which deployment each hostname serves, and the verification output. No secrets or API tokens are recorded.

## Human Gate

- **Who qualifies:** the user authorizes each change; an agent may execute only afterward, or the user makes the changes and shares the evidence.
- **Evidence to record** (a `br comments add` on this bead plus `docs/RELEASE.md`): authorization quotes and timestamps; a Cloudflare record export or screenshot summary; the Vercel domain status ("Valid Configuration") for both hostnames; the `vercel inspect` output for both hostnames; the verification command outputs below.
- **Agents may prepare:** the record plan table with placeholders for Vercel-supplied values, the verification script, and the documentation skeleton.
- **Agents never close this bead on their own judgment.**

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Both hostnames are attached to the correct Vercel project under recorded authorization and serve the intended deployment.
- [ ] Apex and `www` records match Vercel's supplied values with DNS-only proxy status.
- [ ] CAA is correct for the zone's state; null MX, SPF `-all`, and DMARC `p=reject` are published.
- [ ] DNSSEC is enabled and validates.
- [ ] `https://annus-mirabilis.com` is canonical, `www` and HTTP redirect permanently, TLS certificates cover both names, and no HSTS preload was requested without authorization.
- [ ] `docs/RELEASE.md` records every record, the served deployments, and the verification output.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `scripts/verify-dns.test.ts`: parser tests for `dig` output fixtures (A, CNAME, CAA present and absent, MX `0 .`, SPF, DMARC, DS present or absent), for `curl -sI` redirect fixtures (301 and 308 accepted as permanent, 302 rejected), for HSTS header fixtures (a `preload` directive flagged), and for `vercel inspect` fixtures naming a deployment id.

### End-to-end tests
- `bun scripts/verify-dns.ts` runs and records: `dig +short A annus-mirabilis.com`; `dig +short CNAME www.annus-mirabilis.com`; `dig CAA annus-mirabilis.com`; `dig MX annus-mirabilis.com`; `dig TXT annus-mirabilis.com`; `dig TXT _dmarc.annus-mirabilis.com`; `dig DS annus-mirabilis.com +dnssec`; `delv annus-mirabilis.com` (validation); `curl -sI http://annus-mirabilis.com`; `curl -sI https://www.annus-mirabilis.com`; the HSTS header on `https://annus-mirabilis.com`; a TLS certificate subject check for both names; `vercel inspect` for both hostnames. Each result is compared with the recorded plan. Web requests use the user agent "OpenAI File Downloader, XaiImageApiFetch/1.0" per AGENTS.md.
- After attachment, the smoke test in `am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre` passes on both hostnames with the profile of the page they serve.

### Structured logging
- `artifacts/deploy-logs/dns-<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `logRunId`, `check`, `command`, `expected`, `actual`, `outcome`, `message`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- DNS propagation and certificate issuance take time; verification may need a wait. Never "fix" a pending certificate by switching to proxied mode.
- A stale CAA record pointing at a different CA silently blocks certificate issuance.
- Enabling DNSSEC with records that later change is safe with Cloudflare-managed DNS, but enabling it during registrar or nameserver moves is not; do it last.
- Never modify DNS for `classic-patents.com` as part of this work.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-rel-vercel-setup-ituk`: the domains attach to the project created there.

Unblocks:
- `am-launch-readiness-audit-sc9b`: DNS, certificates, redirects, and mail protection on the real hostnames must be verified before launch, because the launch promotion moves those hostnames.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: 2026-09-14, at the user's direct request for a temporary placeholder: annus-mirabilis.com and www.annus-mirabilis.com are attached to Vercel project annus-mirabilis and serve the placeholder deployment. Records Vercel supplied for the project: CNAME @ and CNAME www to 37f4f6b91ca01544.vercel-dns-016.com, DNS only (the CLI also suggested A @ 76.76.21.21). The user is adding the records in the Cloudflare dashboard. CAA, null MX, SPF, DMARC, DNSSEC, and docs/RELEASE.md remain to do; this bead stays open.

title: Run a bounded Cloudflare-hosting compatibility experiment only for a concrete reason
description:
# Run a bounded Cloudflare-hosting compatibility experiment only for a concrete reason

**Epic:** `am-ep-later-gap` · **Batch:** later · **Priority:** P4 · **Plan sections:** §18.1, §18.4 (traceability only)

## Background

The domain is registered at Cloudflare, but "registration at Cloudflare does not require hosting on Cloudflare." The plan chooses Vercel hosting through the verified prebuilt workflow and says a Cloudflare-hosted alternative is "worth testing only with a concrete cost, operational, or product reason, after a bounded compatibility experiment covering the framework version, static generation, source assets, workers, WASM, and preview releases. The release script, its lock, its prebuilt-artifact validation, and the smoke test are Vercel-shaped; re-validating them is not free, and editorial and instrument work never blocks on a hosting comparison."

**Why later:** it solves no reader problem by itself and would re-open a verified release path. **Start only when:** someone records a concrete reason (for example measured cost, an operational incident Vercel cannot address, or a product capability that needs it), the user approves the time box, and no editorial or instrument work is waiting on the outcome.

## Scope

In scope: a time-boxed compatibility experiment on a non-production Cloudflare preview hostname and a decision memo.
Out of scope: migrating production, changing DNS for `annus-mirabilis.com`, or altering the Vercel release path. Any migration needs a separate plan, beads, and authorization.

## Requirements

1. **Record the reason and the time box** in `docs/hosting/cloudflare-experiment.md` before starting.
2. **Isolation.** Use a Cloudflare preview hostname (for example a `pages.dev` or `workers.dev` subdomain) under the user's account with the user's authorization. Production DNS, the Vercel project, and the verified release script stay unchanged. No new git branches unless the user asks.
3. **Compatibility matrix,** each item pass, fail, or unsupported with evidence:
   - the framework version in use and the supported Cloudflare adapter for it;
   - static generation of every route, including readings rendered into HTML with the pre-paint detail script;
   - source assets (facsimile PDFs, figures) served with correct headers and the cache policy;
   - dedicated Web Workers and WASM streaming instantiation (`application/wasm`) under the site's Content-Security-Policy;
   - an unpromoted preview release equivalent, so candidate checks can run before promotion;
   - release manifest validation, candidate checks, smoke test, and a rollback drill adapted to the platform;
   - performance budgets on the agreed device profiles.
4. **Comparison.** Correctness, performance, cost, and operations (lock, artifact validation, rollback) against the current Vercel path, with numbers and measurement conditions.
5. **Decision memo.** Recommend keep, revisit later, or plan a migration, with reasons. The user decides.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The concrete reason, time box, and authorization are recorded before work starts.
- [ ] Every matrix item has evidence.
- [ ] Candidate checks and the smoke test ran against the Cloudflare preview, with logs.
- [ ] Production hosting, DNS, and the release script are unchanged.
- [ ] The decision memo exists and the user's decision is recorded.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- Any adapter-specific code gets unit tests in a clearly separated directory; no change to existing release tests.

### End-to-end tests
- `bun scripts/candidate-checks.ts --deployment <cloudflare-preview-url> --profile launch` (or the current profile), the smoke test, and the performance budget lane against the preview.

### Structured logging
- `artifacts/test-logs/hosting-experiment/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `platform`, `matrixItem`, `check`, `expected`, `actual`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `deviceProfile`, `message`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Adapter support for Next.js features changes often; pin versions in the memo.
- A green experiment is not a migration plan; release safety must be re-proven end to end before any switch.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre`: the experiment compares against a complete, proven Vercel release path.

Unblocks: none.

title: Define and ship the honest public preview with in-preparation states
description:
# Define and ship the honest public preview with in-preparation states

**Epic:** `am-ep-release-as1` · **Batch:** batch-d · **Priority:** P2 · **Plan sections:** §4.6, §19.3 (batches C and D), §19.6 (traceability only)

## Background

The Brownian motion paper (the reference slice and first full paper) and the mass–energy paper (the first complete paper, deliberately short) finish long before the light-quanta and relativity papers. The plan allows a public preview at that point: "A public preview may contain the complete Brownian and mass–energy papers while the others are clearly marked in preparation; it must not advertise four complete interactive editions before they exist. The launch is the complete four-paper site. A preview is a way to learn from a real reading experience, not permission to redefine the project as four landing pages and four famous equations." A preview is optional. If it happens, it must be honest in every surface a visitor or a search engine can reach.

A preview is also the first publication of the site's own English translation and explanatory prose, so it waits for the user's license and rider decision (`am-gov-decision-license-rights-tps`); the scaffold placeholder deploy was the only earlier publication, and it contained none of that material.

## Scope

In scope: the preview policy, the `preview` publication profile rules, in-preparation states for unpublished papers, sitewide copy and metadata rules, preview-specific candidate checks and the leak audit, and (only with authorization) the preview release itself.
Out of scope: the launch release (`am-launch-public-release-5nkq`); DNS (`am-rel-cloudflare-dns-e3tm`, needed only if the preview uses the custom domain); the home page, `/papers`, and `/about` themselves (`am-design-home-page-0s7s`, `am-design-papers-index-afnu`, `am-design-sources-about-zumd`), whose preview states this bead specifies and tests.

## Requirements

1. **Eligibility.** A paper is publishable in a preview only when its definition-of-done bead is closed: `am-dod-brownian-2k4y` and `am-dod-mass-energy-oxh2`. The release manifest's `publishedPapers` must equal the set of closed definitions of done (`am-rel-release-manifest-3gna`). The license decision must be recorded before any preview is deployed.
2. **In-preparation state** for each unpublished paper at `/papers/<slug>`: the printed German title, the working English title, the bibliographic identity (journal, volume, pages, received and published dates), a plain statement that the edition is in preparation, and links to the published papers. No draft German or English text, no unreviewed readings, no discovery journey, and no instruments presented as belonging to a finished paper. These pages carry `noindex` and are excluded from the sitemap.
3. **Every surface respects the profile:** home-page invitations for unpublished papers lead to their in-preparation pages; `/papers` shows the correct availability state for each paper and for the companion; the search index, machine-readable exports, notation page, timeline, connections, tours, and Open Graph images never expose unpublished draft content or imply completeness; `/lab/[experiment]` and `/embed/lab/[experiment]` routes for instruments of unpublished papers are either absent or clearly marked in preparation.
4. **Copy rules.** No page, metadata field, README section, or social card claims "four complete editions" during the preview. The About page states what the preview contains, that the launch is the complete four-paper site, and the license under which the published translation and prose may be reused. Visitor-facing text follows the editorial voice rules (no em dashes, no hype words).
5. **Feedback.** If `am-plat-clarity-signal-nlwr` exists, it may run on published papers. Otherwise the preview collects no analytics. No accounts, no third-party scripts.
6. **Candidate checks.** In the `preview` profile, `am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y` asserts the in-preparation states and the absence of unpublished draft text in HTML, the search index, and exports, runs the full checks on each published paper, and confirms same-origin loading.
7. **Shipping the preview is outward-facing.** The deploy runs through `bun scripts/verified-production-deploy.ts --profile preview --authorization <file>` only with the user's explicit written authorization in the current conversation, quoted in the authorization file. On the custom domain it also needs `am-rel-cloudflare-dns-e3tm` and `--include-custom-domains` with an authorization that names the domains; otherwise it lives on `annus-mirabilis-seven.vercel.app`.
8. **Exit.** The preview ends at the launch release or on the user's decision; `docs/RELEASE.md` records its start, contents, license statement, and end.

## Human Gate (shipping step only)

The policy, states, and checks are agent work. The public preview deploy requires recorded user authorization (quote and timestamp, in the authorization file and a bead comment). If the user declines a preview, close this bead with that decision recorded, keeping the implemented profile rules for future use.

**Added in review (one in-preparation wording).** The experiment registry renders "This experiment is in preparation" for catalogue ids that have no manifest. The preview's in-preparation states for papers, instruments, and routes use that same wording and component, so a reader never sees two phrasings for one state.

## Technical Approach

The in-preparation page is a component rendered from the paper's bibliographic record only, so it has no access to draft content by construction. `scripts/preview-leak-audit.ts` searches the static output, the search index, exports, and Open Graph images' text sources for sentence ids and distinctive German strings belonging to unpublished papers. Profile state comes from the release manifest at build time (`AM_RELEASE_PROFILE=preview`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/RELEASE.md` contains the preview policy.
- [ ] In-preparation pages exist for every unpublished paper and meet requirement 2.
- [ ] Profile rules are enforced in the manifest validator and candidate checks, with tests.
- [ ] The leak audit of the preview build output finds no unpublished draft text.
- [ ] The license decision is recorded before any preview deploy.
- [ ] Either the preview shipped under recorded authorization with passing candidate checks and smoke test, or the user's decision not to preview is recorded.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- Manifest profile tests: `preview` with an open definition of done fails; unpublished paper content in the search index fixture fails.
- Page tests for the in-preparation component: required identity fields, `noindex`, no instrument or journey links, and a type-level test that the component's props contain only bibliographic fields.
- `scripts/preview-leak-audit.test.ts`: in-memory fixture output containing an unpublished sentence id in the search index fails; containing a distinctive German string from an unpublished paper in an export fails; a clean fixture passes.

### End-to-end tests
- The browser harness in `preview` profile against a local production build: visit home, both published papers, each in-preparation page, `/papers`, and `/about`; search for a term that only appears in an unpublished paper (no result); open the sitemap (no in-preparation routes); confirm the About page's license statement matches `NOTICE.md`.

### Structured logging
- `artifacts/test-logs/preview/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `logRunId`, `profile`, `paper`, `route`, `check`, `expected`, `actual`, `outcome`, `message`; failures retain screenshots and DOM snapshots.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- The search index and JSON exports are the easiest places to leak drafts; audit them, not just the HTML.
- A preview must never become the project's new definition. Launch still requires all four papers.
- Do not publish a scan in an in-preparation page unless its redistribution rights are recorded.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-dod-brownian-2k4y`: only a paper that meets its definition of done may appear in a preview.
- `am-dod-mass-energy-oxh2`: the same rule for the second preview paper.
- `am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre`: a public release needs smoke testing and rollback.
- Proposed in review: `am-gov-decision-license-rights-tps` (a preview publishes the translation and prose), `am-design-home-page-0s7s`, `am-design-papers-index-afnu`, and `am-design-sources-about-zumd` (the surfaces whose preview states this bead requires and tests).

Unblocks: nothing structurally; it informs `am-launch-public-release-5nkq`.

title: Generate and validate the release manifest
description:
# Generate and validate the release manifest

**Epic:** `am-ep-release-as1` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §10.4, §11.3, §12.4, §18.3, §21 "The publication is maintainable" (traceability only)

## Background

A scientific edition is a bundle of separately versioned things: the site code, the content edition, pinned facsimile scans, reviewed translations, and WASM kernels built from a pinned FrankenSim revision. The plan requires a **release manifest** that binds "the site source revision, content edition version, source-asset hashes, WASM artifact hashes, generated schema version, and test results." Without it, a rollback can point old HTML at incompatible new WASM, a candidate check cannot prove it tested the bytes that went live, and nobody can reconstruct which reviewed translation a reader saw. The content model keeps `contentRevision`, `sourceAssetDigest`, `translationRevision`, `modelVersion`, and `artifactDigest` separate, and the manifest preserves that separation rather than collapsing it into one version number or one flattering completeness score.

The manifest also answers a launch question: is the deployment being promoted the same content that was audited? Test logs and timestamps legitimately differ between two builds of one commit, so the manifest carries a **determinism digest** over everything that describes content and artifacts, and excludes only the run-specific fields.

## Scope

In scope: the manifest schema, the generator run as part of the build, the determinism digest, its validator, the publication configuration it reads, the retained release record, and the rules each publication profile imposes.
Out of scope: running candidate checks (`am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y`); rollback and cache headers (`am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre`); building the WASM artifact itself (`am-fs-slim-artifact-0yh`); the content compiler (`am-cm-compiler-core-oa7`); the coverage computation (`am-cm-coverage-ledger-0ip`).

## Requirements

**Location.** The generator (`scripts/build-release-manifest.ts`, invoked by `bun run build` after the content compiler and before `next build`) writes `public/release-manifest.json`, which is listed in `.gitignore` in the same change, so it is served at `/release-manifest.json` with a short, revalidating cache and never dirties the tree. A retained copy goes to `artifacts/releases/<commit>-<log-run-id>.json`, which the release script later extends with candidate-check results and promotion events. The deployed file is immutable once built and never contains post-deploy results.

**Profile input.** The profile comes from the environment variable `AM_RELEASE_PROFILE` (`scaffold`, `preview`, or `launch`), set by the release script. When it is absent, the manifest records `profile: "development"`, which the validator refuses to deploy.

**Fields** (zod schema `src/content/releaseManifest.ts`, `schemaVersion` starting at 1):
- `releaseId`, `createdAt` (ISO), `profile`.
- `site`: `commit` (full hash), `branch` (`main`), `treeClean: true`, `toolchain` (Bun, Node.js, Next.js, TypeScript versions).
- `content`: `editionVersion`; per paper (`light-quanta`, `brownian-motion`, `special-relativity`, `mass-energy`, and the companion `molecular-dimensions` when admitted): `contentRevision`, `translationRevision`, the published faces, and completeness dimensions reported **separately** from the coverage ledger (source manifest coverage, translation review state, argument coverage, instrument availability, accessibility equivalence, numerical validation). `publishedPapers` lists the papers the profile publishes.
- `sourceAssets`: for every facsimile, ledger, figure crop, and dataset file the site serves or cites: `key`, `path` (or `null` when not redistributed), `sha256` (lowercase hex), `rightsStatus`, `redistributable` flag, and the provenance receipt path.
- `wasm`: for every content-addressed artifact listed in `public/wasm/manifest.json`: `path`, `sha256`, `capabilities`, `exports`, `modelVersion`, the FrankenSim commit, the Rust toolchain (for example `nightly-2026-07-06`), and the generated glue version.
- `schema`: generated content schema version and compiler version.
- `donors`: the classic-patents.com and FrankenSim commits pinned in `docs/DONOR_AUDIT.md` and `docs/FRANKENSIM_BINDING.md`.
- `tests`: for each pre-deploy suite (the gate steps the profile required): `stepId`, `command`, `result`, counts, `logRunId`, `logPath`, and the SHA-256 of the JSONL log.
- `determinismDigest`: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON (sorted keys, sorted arrays, no insignificant whitespace) of the whole manifest except `releaseId`, `createdAt`, `tests`, `site.toolchain`, and `determinismDigest` itself.

**Publication configuration.** `content/papers/publication.yaml` records the companion's status (`admitted` or `deferred`) with the decision id from `docs/DECISIONS.md` (`am-gov-decision-companion-at-launch-936`); the generator lists `molecular-dimensions` only when it is `admitted`.

**Validation** (`scripts/validate-release-manifest.ts`, called by `am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt` on the fresh artifact and by `--promote` on the deployed file):
- The schema validates; `profile` is not `development`; `commit` equals `HEAD`; the tree was clean.
- `determinismDigest` recomputes to the recorded value.
- Every `sourceAssets` and `wasm` entry with a path exists in the output and its hash matches the bytes on disk.
- Every WASM file the instrument registry or HTML references is listed, with matching digest; no listed artifact is unreferenced without a declared reason.
- Every test entry is `passed`; any other result refuses the release.
- Profile rules: `scaffold` lists no published papers; `preview` lists exactly the papers whose definition-of-done beads are closed (read through `br show <id> --json` in the release environment) and marks the others "in preparation" (`am-rel-preview-policy-cf6g`); `launch` requires all four papers with every completeness dimension satisfied. `molecular-dimensions` appears only when the publication configuration says `admitted` and the named decision id exists in `docs/DECISIONS.md`.
- A manifest may never state a completeness dimension that the source manifest or coverage ledger does not support, and never aggregates dimensions into a single percentage.

## Technical Approach

Hash files with streaming SHA-256; read source and translation revisions from compiled content records; read coverage dimensions from the coverage ledger's compiled output; read WASM identities from `public/wasm/manifest.json` and `docs/FRANKENSIM_BINDING.md`; read test results from JSONL logs written under AGENTS.md "Testing and Logging Standards". Keep generation deterministic: sorted keys and arrays, no wall-clock values except `createdAt`, so two builds of one commit and profile differ only in `releaseId`, `createdAt`, `tests`, and `site.toolchain`, and share one `determinismDigest`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The schema and generator exist and produce a manifest during `bun run build`, written to an ignored path.
- [ ] The validator rejects each tamper case in the Test Plan with a specific message.
- [ ] Profile rules, including the companion rule, are enforced by tests.
- [ ] The retained release record exists for every build the release script runs.
- [ ] Rebuilding the same commit and profile yields the same `determinismDigest`.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `scripts/build-release-manifest.test.ts` on a fixture output tree (in-memory file listing and bytes): correct hashes; sorted, deterministic output; separate completeness dimensions; `profile: "development"` when the environment variable is absent; two generations with different `createdAt`, `releaseId`, and test logs produce the same `determinismDigest`, while a one-byte change in a facsimile changes it.
- `scripts/validate-release-manifest.test.ts` tamper cases: one flipped byte in a facsimile, a missing WASM file, an HTML reference to an unlisted artifact, a failing test entry, a commit mismatch, a dirty tree flag, a `development` profile, an edited field that no longer matches `determinismDigest`, `preview` listing a paper whose definition of done is open (fixture `br` output), `launch` missing a paper, `molecular-dimensions` listed while the publication configuration says `deferred`, a completeness claim unsupported by the coverage ledger, and a single aggregated percentage field.

### End-to-end tests
- In CI, run `bun run build` on the current commit, then the validator against the Next.js output with `AM_RELEASE_PROFILE=scaffold`; assert pass and log the manifest digest and determinism digest.

### Structured logging
- The generator and validator append JSONL records (`timestamp`, `logRunId`, `commit`, `profile`, `check`, `path`, `expected`, `actual`, `outcome`, `message`) to `artifacts/test-logs/release-manifest/<log-run-id>.jsonl`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A checksum proves byte identity, not compatible meaning; compatibility between HTML and WASM comes from `modelVersion` and schema checks, which the rollback bead also relies on.
- Non-redistributable scans are listed with `path: null`; never publish a scan to satisfy the manifest.
- Keep the manifest small; do not inline logs.
- A `determinismDigest` that changes between two builds of the same commit is a bug in the generator (an unsorted list or a timestamp), not a reason to drop the check.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt`: the release script validates the manifest in the artifact.
- `am-fs-slim-artifact-0yh`: WASM artifacts and pinned digests must exist to be listed.
- `am-cm-compiler-core-oa7`: content revisions and route payloads come from the compiler.
- Proposed in review: `am-cm-coverage-ledger-0ip`: the separate completeness dimensions come from the coverage ledger.

Unblocks:
- `am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y`: candidate checks verify deployed bytes against this manifest.

title: Implement the post-promotion smoke test, coherent rollback, and cache policy
description:
# Implement the post-promotion smoke test, coherent rollback, and cache policy

**Epic:** `am-ep-release-as1` · **Batch:** batch-c · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §12.8, §16.3, §18.3, §21 "The publication is maintainable" (traceability only)

## Background

Even a fully checked candidate can fail after promotion: an alias can attach to the wrong deployment, the edge can serve something unexpected, or a hostname can resolve incorrectly. The plan asks for "a short live smoke test (the mass–energy paper, because it is quick, plus its German edition endpoint)" after promotion. It also requires that "a rollback restores a coherent site, content, and kernel set and never points old HTML at incompatible new WASM," that the previous verified deployment and its immutable assets stay available, that immutable content-addressed figures and WASM get long-lived caching, and that manifests and HTML "never reference a removed artifact." The donor's `smoke-test-deployment.ts` fetches core routes and checks HTTP 200 and minimum body sizes; this bead adapts that idea and adds profile awareness, automatic rollback, deployment retention, and the cache policy.

The runtime behavior that makes old HTML safe (the WASM loader refusing a module whose digest does not match with the `artifact-mismatch` execution outcome, and the laboratory pausing while the book stays usable) is owned by `am-fs-slim-artifact-0yh` and `am-rt-memory-lifecycle-5ws`. This bead proves the release-level guarantees around it and exercises that behavior in its drill; it does not reimplement it.

## Scope

In scope: `scripts/smoke-test-deployment.ts` (adapted, profile-aware), the rollback routine in the release script, the verified-deployment history and retention check, the cache and MIME header policy (in `vercel.json` headers or Next.js `headers()`), the build-output content-addressing test, and the `cache-headers` candidate check.
Out of scope: pre-promotion candidate checks (`am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y`); DNS (`am-rel-cloudflare-dns-e3tm`); service-worker caching (`am-plat-installable-offline-oit3`); the loader digest check and laboratory pause (`am-fs-slim-artifact-0yh`, `am-rt-memory-lifecycle-5ws`).

## Requirements

**Smoke test** (`bun scripts/smoke-test-deployment.ts --base https://<host> --profile <scaffold|preview|launch> --release-id <id>` for each promoted hostname):
- Every profile: `/`, `/robots.txt`, and `/sitemap.xml` return 200; `/release-manifest.json` carries the promoted `releaseId` (once `am-rel-release-manifest-3gna` has landed).
- `preview` and `launch`: `/papers/mass-energy` (reading face) returns 200 with the paper's German title *Ist die Trägheit eines Körpers von seinem Energieinhalt abhängig?* and a non-trivial body; the German edition endpoint (`/papers/mass-energy?view=german`, plus the machine-readable German edition export if `am-cm-machine-readable-exports-xgy` has shipped) returns the complete German text, including the date-line as edited ("Bern, September 1905", verified against the facsimile).
- Once DNS is attached: `http://annus-mirabilis.com` redirects to `https://annus-mirabilis.com`, and `https://www.annus-mirabilis.com` redirects permanently to the apex.
- Target runtime under one minute; no browser needed.

**Rollback:**
- Before promotion, `am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt` records the deployment currently serving each hostname as the rollback target, together with its `releaseId` and manifest digest from the retained release history.
- On smoke failure: re-alias every promoted hostname to its rollback target, confirm `vercel inspect` shows Ready and the target id, run the smoke test against the restored deployment, log both results, and exit non-zero. If rollback itself fails, print exact manual recovery commands and the recorded ids.
- Rollback always moves whole deployments. On Vercel each deployment serves its own HTML, content payloads, and WASM, so re-aliasing restores a coherent set. Never mix assets across deployments.
- Retention: the retained history keeps at least the last three verified deployments as rollback targets, plus any audited candidate awaiting `--promote`. Before promotion, the script reads the project's deployment retention settings (as recorded by `am-rel-vercel-setup-ituk` and re-checked through the Vercel CLI or API) and refuses if they would delete a recorded rollback target or audited candidate before its intended use. Deleting a Vercel deployment or changing retention settings requires the user's written permission (AGENTS.md Rule 1 applies to remote artifacts too).
- A manual rollback outside a release is an outward-facing action and requires the user's explicit authorization.

**Version coherence:**
- Every WASM URL referenced by HTML or route payloads is content-addressed (a digest in the path or filename). No `latest.wasm` style URL exists.
- The release-level drill confirms that a page served by an old deployment loads its own WASM and that a digest mismatch produces the runtime's `artifact-mismatch` outcome with the laboratory paused and the text readable.

**Cache and MIME policy:**
- Paths whose file name or directory contains a content digest (for example `/wasm/<bundle>/<sha256-prefix>/…` or `/figures/<name>.<hex>.<ext>`) and `/_next/static/*`: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. WASM also gets `Content-Type: application/wasm` for streaming instantiation.
- HTML, `release-manifest.json`, the search index, and route JSON fragments: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate`. Edge caching is allowed only where invalidated per deployment.
- Facsimile PDFs and any other asset whose URL does not contain a digest must not be marked `immutable`; use revalidation with ETag. Prefer moving immutable assets to content-addressed paths.
- The rule is applied by pattern, not by directory, so a non-content-addressed file placed under `/figures/` never receives an immutable header.
- Register a `cache-headers` check in the candidate-check catalogue (`am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y`) that asserts these headers on the deployed candidate.

## Technical Approach

Keep the smoke test dependency-free (`fetch` with timeouts) so it can run during an incident. Implement rollback as a small state machine in the release script with injectable command execution. Add a build-time test that walks the output and asserts every referenced WASM and figure path is content-addressed and present.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The smoke test runs after every promotion on every promoted hostname, with checks appropriate to the profile.
- [ ] A smoke failure triggers automatic rollback, proven by a state-machine test and a documented drill on the platform alias.
- [ ] The retained history lists at least three verified rollback targets with release ids and manifest digests, and the retention check refuses when settings would delete one.
- [ ] Header tests confirm the cache and MIME policy; no immutable header lands on a non-content-addressed URL.
- [ ] A build-output test proves HTML never references a missing or non-content-addressed WASM or figure.
- [ ] The drill shows an old deployment loading its own WASM, and a digest mismatch producing the `artifact-mismatch` outcome with a paused laboratory.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `scripts/smoke-test-deployment.test.ts` against an in-process fixture HTTP server: pass per profile; 404 on the paper; wrong `releaseId`; missing date-line; redirect loop; `scaffold` profile does not request paper routes.
- `scripts/rollback.test.ts`: smoke fails then rollback succeeds; rollback alias failure then manual recovery instructions; no recorded target then refusal before promotion; retention settings that would delete a target cause refusal.
- `scripts/cache-policy.test.ts`: parse the configured headers and assert per-path rules; a digest-free file under `/figures/` gets no `immutable`; walk a fixture build output (in-memory listing) for content addressing.
### End-to-end tests
- Rollback drill on the platform alias during an authorized release window: promote a candidate, force a smoke failure through a test-only flag, observe automatic rollback, and record evidence.
- In the browser harness, load an old deployment's HTML directly by deployment URL and confirm its WASM loads from the same deployment; serve a tampered WASM through request interception and confirm the `artifact-mismatch` outcome, a paused laboratory, and readable text.

### Structured logging
- `artifacts/deploy-logs/<log-run-id>.jsonl` records `stage` (`smoke`, `rollback`, `retention`), `profile`, `hostname`, `url`, `expected`, `actual`, `releaseId`, `rollbackTargetId`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `message`. The release history appends promotion, smoke, and rollback events.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Browser caches can hold old HTML for a long time; content addressing plus per-deployment assets is what keeps that HTML working.
- Do not "fix" a failing smoke test by loosening its assertions during an incident; roll back first.
- Keep the smoke test short, as the plan asks. The exhaustive checks already ran before promotion.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y`: promotion and smoke testing follow passing candidate checks.
- Proposed in review: `am-rt-memory-lifecycle-5ws`: the drill exercises the runtime's pause on artifact mismatch.

Unblocks:
- `am-rel-preview-policy-cf6g`: a public preview needs smoke testing and rollback.
- `am-launch-readiness-audit-sc9b`: "rollback restores a coherent version" is a launch criterion.
- `am-rel-cloudflare-hosting-experiment-n7re`: any hosting comparison re-validates this behavior.

title: Create the Vercel project and deploy the empty site to the Vercel alias with explicit authorization
description:
# Create the Vercel project and deploy the empty site to the Vercel alias with explicit authorization

**Epic:** `am-ep-release-as1` · **Batch:** batch-a · **Priority:** P1 · **Labels:** human-gate · **Plan sections:** §4.6, §18.1, §19.1 exit evidence (traceability only)

## Background

Batch A ends with three pieces of exit evidence, one of which is "the empty site deploys to the Vercel alias." Deploying early proves the release path before content exists, so the first paper does not also have to debug hosting. The site is hosted on Vercel through the verified prebuilt workflow built in `am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt`; `vercel.json` already disables git-triggered deployments (`{"git": {"deploymentEnabled": false}}`), so pushes to GitHub never deploy on their own. Creating a Vercel project, linking the repository, and deploying are outward-facing actions. The plan explicitly does not authorize them, so this is a human-gate bead.

This deploy is the one publication that does not wait for the license decision (`am-gov-decision-license-rights-tps`): it serves only an in-preparation placeholder page and code that is already public in the repository under the provisional LICENSE, with no translation or explanatory prose.

## Scope

In scope: creating or linking the Vercel project, pinning its identity in the release script, confirming project settings (framework, Node.js version, Deployment Protection, deployment retention), reserving the platform alias, and one authorized scaffold-profile deploy to `annus-mirabilis-seven.vercel.app`.
Out of scope: adding `annus-mirabilis.com` or `www` to the project and all DNS work (`am-rel-cloudflare-dns-e3tm`); preview or launch releases (`am-rel-preview-policy-cf6g`, `am-launch-public-release-5nkq`).

## Requirements

1. **Authorization first.** Obtain the user's explicit written authorization in the current conversation to (a) create or link the Vercel project and (b) run the scaffold deploy. Record the exact quote and timestamp. Authorization for one step does not cover the other or any later release. Write the scaffold deploy authorization, verbatim, to `artifacts/releases/authorizations/<ISO timestamp>-scaffold-full.md` with its scope (profile `scaffold`, full mode, hostname `annus-mirabilis-seven.vercel.app`, the commit), because the release script refuses without it.
2. **Account check.** `vercel whoami` must show the user's account (the donor project used `dicklesworthstone`). Stop if it does not.
3. **Project.** Create or link a project, proposed name `annus-mirabilis` (confirm with the user). Keep git deployments disabled. Confirm the framework preset and output settings are compatible with prebuilt deploys, and that the project's Node.js version matches `engines.node` in `package.json`. Record whether Deployment Protection is on for previews, because candidate checks depend on it, and whether a Protection Bypass for Automation secret exists (never record the secret itself). Record the project's deployment retention settings, because rollback targets and audited candidates must not be deleted automatically; any change to those settings requires the user's authorization.
4. **Pin identity.** Copy `projectId`, `projectName`, and `orgId` from `.vercel/project.json` into `CANONICAL_PRODUCTION_PROJECT` in `scripts/deployment-target.ts` and the matching constants in `deployment-verification.ts`, and commit them. `.vercel/` itself stays ignored by git.
5. **Platform alias.** The platform alias is `annus-mirabilis-seven.vercel.app`. The plain `annus-mirabilis.vercel.app` belongs to another Vercel account, so Vercel assigned this alias when the project was created on 2026-09-14. Use it in the script constants; AGENTS.md and the plan already do.
6. **Dry run, then deploy.** Run `bun scripts/verified-production-deploy.ts --profile scaffold --dry-run` and show the user its output; then run `bun scripts/verified-production-deploy.ts --profile scaffold --authorization <file>`. The scaffold profile promotes only the platform alias; custom domains are not attached.
7. **Verification.** `vercel inspect https://annus-mirabilis-seven.vercel.app` shows status Ready and the candidate id; `/`, `/robots.txt`, and `/sitemap.xml` return 200 with the expected placeholder content; an unknown path returns 404 with the not-found page; `/papers` is checked only if that route exists at the deployed commit; the served page contains no draft paper text and no claim that an edition is available.

## Human Gate

- **Who qualifies:** the user (repository owner) gives authorization; an agent may execute the commands only after that.
- **Evidence to record** (as a `br comments add` on this bead and in the deploy JSONL log): the authorization quotes and timestamps, the authorization file path, the Vercel account, project name and ids, Node.js version setting, Deployment Protection and bypass status, deployment retention settings, the deployment URL and id, `vercel inspect` output for the alias, and the log path.
- **Agents may prepare:** the checklist, the dry-run output of the script, and the constants patch with placeholders.
- **Agents never close this bead on their own judgment**, and never write an authorization file without the user's actual words.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Authorization quotes and timestamps are recorded for project creation and for the scaffold deploy, and the deploy authorization file matches the run's scope.
- [ ] Canonical project constants are committed and the identity check passes against `.vercel/project.json`.
- [ ] `annus-mirabilis-seven.vercel.app` serves the scaffold deployment with status Ready.
- [ ] The deploy was performed only through the verified script with the scaffold profile; no direct `vercel deploy --prod` was run.
- [ ] Protection, bypass availability, Node.js version, and retention settings are recorded.
- [ ] Custom domains remain unattached.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- After pinning, rerun `scripts/deployment-target.test.ts` and `scripts/deployment-verification.test.ts`; add `scripts/canonicalProject.test.ts` asserting the committed constants have the expected shapes (`prj_` and `team_` prefixes, lowercase hostnames) and that none equals a value on the forbidden donor identity list.

### End-to-end tests
- The verified script's dry run, then its candidate and promotion stages in scaffold profile.
- A post-deploy fetch loop against the alias for `/`, `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml`, and an unknown path, asserting status codes, minimum body sizes, and the absence of third-party origins in the HTML, logged to JSONL.

### Structured logging
- `artifacts/deploy-logs/<log-run-id>.jsonl` from the script, plus a `setup` record `{timestamp, logRunId, stage: "setup", account, projectName, projectIdPrefix, nodeVersion, deploymentProtection, bypassConfigured, retention, authorizationRef, aliasVerified, outcome, message}`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Linking the wrong project is the failure the identity check guards against; confirm the ids before committing them.
- If Deployment Protection is enabled, unauthenticated fetches of the candidate return 401. That is expected and is why candidate checks use the protected-preview adapter.
- Do not connect the custom domains here. Attaching them before DNS is ready produces certificate and verification noise and could expose an unfinished site.
- Never touch the classic-patents.com Vercel project.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt`: the only supported deploy path must exist and be tested first.

Unblocks:
- `am-rel-cloudflare-dns-e3tm`: custom domains are attached to the project this bead creates.

title: Adapt the verified candidate-then-promote release script for annus-mirabilis.com
description:
# Adapt the verified candidate-then-promote release script for annus-mirabilis.com

**Epic:** `am-ep-release-as1` · **Batch:** batch-a · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §2.3 (reuse table), §18.1, §18.3, §19.6, §21 (traceability only)

## Background

The plan reuses the donor's release workflow because it is fail-closed: it refuses stale or partial artifacts, validates a fresh prebuilt deployment under an unpromoted URL, and only then moves public hostnames. Classic Patents learned this after stale `.vercel/output` directories and concurrent builds put wrong content live. Annus Mirabilis inherits the workflow and extends it for a scientific edition whose releases must bind source texts, translations, and WASM kernels together. This bead writes the script and its tests. **It never performs a real deployment**; the first real deploy happens in `am-rel-vercel-setup-ituk` under the user's explicit authorization.

Two extensions matter for launch honesty. The launch audit and the final product test examine one specific deployment; if the public release then rebuilt and deployed a fresh candidate, the bytes readers get would be a different deployment from the one that was audited and tested. The script therefore has a `--candidate-only` mode (build, deploy unpromoted, check, record, stop) and a `--promote <deployment>` mode (re-verify a recorded candidate and promote it without rebuilding). And because deploying is an outward-facing action that only the user may authorize, every mode that deploys or moves an alias requires an authorization file containing the user's verbatim words, which the script checks for scope and copies into the release record. The script cannot prove the words are genuine; agents must never write such a file without the user's actual authorization in the current conversation.

Donor files to adapt (read-only source at the revision pinned in `docs/DONOR_AUDIT.md`): `scripts/verified-production-deploy.ts`, `scripts/deployment-target.ts` (+ `.test.ts`), `scripts/deployment-verification.ts` (+ `.test.ts`), `scripts/smoke-test-deployment.ts`. Extraction with license notices happens in `am-scaf-extract-scripts-7jm`; this bead turns the extracted copies into Annus Mirabilis code.

## Scope

In scope: `scripts/verified-production-deploy.ts`, `scripts/deployment-target.ts`, `scripts/deployment-verification.ts`, their tests, publication profiles, modes, authorization files, the release record, the `publication-contract` gate step, deploy logging, and documentation in AGENTS.md "Vercel Deployment Standards".
Out of scope (owned elsewhere): creating the Vercel project and first deploy (`am-rel-vercel-setup-ituk`); manifest generation (`am-rel-release-manifest-3gna`); the full candidate check suite (`am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y`); smoke test, rollback, retention, and caching (`am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre`); DNS (`am-rel-cloudflare-dns-e3tm`); the gate registry and runner (`am-scaf-quality-gates-ci-4xx`).

## Requirements

The script is the only supported production entry point:

`bun scripts/verified-production-deploy.ts --profile <scaffold|preview|launch> [--dry-run | --candidate-only | --promote <deployment-id-or-url>] [--authorization <path>] [--include-custom-domains]`

It must preserve every donor safety behavior, re-targeted:

1. **Exclusive local lock.** Bind `127.0.0.1` on a dedicated TCP port with `exclusive: true`; `EADDRINUSE` means another Annus Mirabilis release is running and the script refuses. Use a port distinct from the donor's (the donor port is on the forbidden identity list) so the two sites' releases stay independent. Release the lock in `finally`.
2. **Canonical project identity.** `.vercel/project.json` must match `CANONICAL_PRODUCTION_PROJECT` (`projectId`, `projectName`, `orgId`, custom domains `annus-mirabilis.com` and `www.annus-mirabilis.com`, platform domain `annus-mirabilis-seven.vercel.app`). The ids are unknown until `am-rel-vercel-setup-ituk`; until they are filled in, the script refuses with a message naming that bead. Never copy the donor's ids.
3. **No conflicting builds.** Scan `ps -Ao pid=,ppid=,etime=,command=` for `next build|dev`, `vercel build|deploy`, and `bun run build|dev` processes whose working directory (via `lsof -p <pid> -a -d cwd -Fn`) is inside this workspace; wait up to 120 s, then refuse. Check at preflight, after the application build, after the Vercel build, and before promotion.
4. **Clean tree and fixed commit.** `git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all` must be empty apart from a small documented allowlist (for example `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`, `next-env.d.ts`, `.beads/`). Record `HEAD` at preflight and refuse if it changes at any later stage. In `--promote` mode `HEAD` must equal the candidate's recorded commit.
5. **Quality gates before building.** Run `bun scripts/quality-gates.ts --profile <profile> --fail-fast`; exit code 2 (a required step is not available) and exit code 1 (a step failed) both refuse the release. The profiles' step lists live in the gate registry, not in this script: `scaffold` requires the architecture test, typecheck, lint, format check, unit tests, `ubs --diff`, `ubs --staged`, and build; `preview` and `launch` additionally require `publication-contract`, `verify-content`, `verify-wasm-artifacts`, `scenarios`, `license-inventory`, `voice-lint` (until folded into `verify-content`), `browser-acceptance`, and `perf-budgets`. This bead registers the `publication-contract` step (a fast `bun test` subset of the edition, dispatcher, architecture, and determinism tests, ordered first). A profile's list only grows.
6. **Fresh prebuilt artifact.** `vercel pull --yes`, then `vercel build --prod` with `AM_RELEASE_PROFILE=<profile>` set for the manifest generator, then validate: `.vercel/output/config.json` exists, parses, and has `version: 3`; `.vercel/output/static/` exists; the config was written after this attempt's build start (1 s tolerance); the file count is above a documented floor; for `preview` and `launch`, the release manifest is present and valid (`am-rel-release-manifest-3gna`), while `scaffold` records the manifest's absence explicitly in the deploy log until that bead lands; profile-specific content assertions pass (below).
7. **Build-output hygiene without silent deletion.** The donor deletes `.next` before building. AGENTS.md Rule 1 forbids agents deleting files without written permission. Either record the user's explicit approval for the script to clear its own build output directories (quote and date in the script header and AGENTS.md), or build into a fresh per-release output location and rely on the timestamp freshness check. Do not add a deletion silently.
8. **Unpromoted candidate.** `vercel deploy --prebuilt --prod --skip-domain --json`; extract the last `https://*.vercel.app` URL from stdout and stderr. Validate protected previews through one adapter: `vercel curl --deployment <url> <path> -- --silent --show-error --write-out "\n<MARKER>%{http_code}"` when the locked CLI provides it, otherwise `curl` with the `x-vercel-protection-bypass` header whose secret is read from an environment variable and never logged; parse the status marker. Invoke `am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y` here, before any alias moves. The donor ran its full sweep after promotion; that ordering is not inherited.
9. **Release record.** After candidate checks pass, write `artifacts/releases/<commit>-<log-run-id>.json` with profile, mode, commit, candidate deployment id and URL, manifest digest and determinism digest, candidate-check summary and log path, and the authorization reference. `--candidate-only` stops here and prints the candidate id.
10. **Promotion with atomic intent.** Before moving anything, record the deployment currently serving each hostname (`vercel inspect https://<host>`) as the rollback target, with its `releaseId` and manifest digest when it serves `/release-manifest.json`. For each hostname: `vercel alias set <candidate> <host>`, then `vercel inspect https://<host>` must parse to status Ready and the candidate's id. Then assert the composite alias set (`assertDeploymentReadyAndAliased`, `assertDeploymentHasRequiredAliases`). If any step fails after the first alias moved, re-point the moved aliases to the recorded previous deployment, verify them, and exit non-zero with both failures reported.
11. **`--promote <deployment>`.** No rebuild. Take the lock; check identity, conflicts, clean tree, and `HEAD`; load the candidate's release record, which must exist, name the same profile, and show passing candidate checks; fetch the candidate's deployed `/release-manifest.json` and require its digest to equal the recorded digest; rerun `am-rel-candidate-checks-kc7y` against the candidate for fresh evidence; then promote as in Requirement 10 and hand off to the smoke test.
12. **Post-promotion.** Hand off to the smoke test in `am-rel-smoke-rollback-cache-phre`; a smoke failure triggers that bead's rollback.
13. **Publication profiles.** `scaffold` promotes only `annus-mirabilis-seven.vercel.app`, and, with `--include-custom-domains` and an authorization that names the custom domains, also the apex and `www` to serve the in-preparation placeholder as an honest holding page; it requires the architecture, build, and placeholder route checks. `preview` requires the release manifest's `publishedPapers` to be exactly the papers whose definition-of-done beads are closed, and "in preparation" states for the rest (`am-rel-preview-policy-cf6g`); it promotes the platform alias, and the custom domains only when the authorization names them. `launch` requires all four papers complete and promotes all three hostnames. A profile can never weaken a gate that applies to a paper it publishes.
14. **Authorization files.** Every mode except `--dry-run` requires `--authorization <path>` pointing to a Markdown file under `artifacts/releases/authorizations/` containing the user's verbatim authorization text, its timestamp, and the scope it grants (profile, mode, hostnames, and commit or `releaseId`). The script refuses when the file is missing, when its scope does not cover this profile, mode, commit or candidate, or when it names fewer hostnames than the run would move. The reference is copied into the release record and the deploy log.
15. **Help and refusal messages.** `--help` prints usage. Every refusal names the stage, the failed assertion, and the next action. Exit code 1 on any refusal or failure.

## Technical Approach

Keep `deployment-target.ts` as pure parsing and assertion functions (`parseDeploymentInspect`, `assertDeploymentReadyAndAliased`, project-identity validation) so they are unit-testable with fixtures. `deployment-verification.ts` holds constants, alias assertions, and the reader sweep adapted to paper routes (`/papers/<slug>?view=german|english|reading`), checking a `data-source-delivery` style marker and forbidding draft or hold strings on published faces (for example unreviewed-draft banners). `authorization.ts` parses and scope-checks authorization files. The main script composes them as a stage machine whose command runner is injected. All child processes go through one `run()` wrapper that logs and throws on non-zero exit, with a 64 MB output buffer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] No donor identity (project id, org id, hostnames, Wright or patent routes, lock port) remains in the adapted code.
- [ ] Every safety behavior in Requirements 1–15 is implemented and covered by a test.
- [ ] Running the script without a linked canonical project refuses before any build or network call.
- [ ] Partial-promotion failure restores previously serving deployments (proven with fixture-driven tests of the promotion state machine).
- [ ] `--candidate-only` never moves an alias, and `--promote` never builds (proven by recorded command lists in tests).
- [ ] AGENTS.md "Vercel Deployment Standards" matches the implemented behavior, including the lock port, profiles, modes, and authorization files.
- [ ] No real deployment was run by this bead.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `scripts/deployment-target.test.ts`: inspect-output fixtures (Ready, Error, Building, missing aliases, extra aliases, trailing slashes, `╶` bullets, an unknown format that must fail closed); project.json fixtures (missing file message, invalid JSON, wrong name, wrong id, wrong org).
- `scripts/deployment-verification.test.ts`: alias normalization; required-alias refusal text; reader-sweep route manifest for the four papers and their faces; forbidden-string detection on fixture HTML.
- `scripts/authorization.test.ts`: a missing file refuses; a file for `preview` used with `launch` refuses; a file naming only `annus-mirabilis-seven.vercel.app` refuses a run that would move the apex; a file naming a different commit refuses; a complete file passes and its reference appears in the record.
- `scripts/verified-production-deploy.test.ts`: `ps` and `lsof` fixture parsing for conflicting builds; porcelain filtering with the allowlist; deployment URL extraction from mixed JSON and text; protected-preview status-marker parsing (2xx pass, 401, 404, missing marker); artifact validation on fixture trees (missing config, version 2, stale mtime, too few files); gate runner exit code 2 and exit code 1 each refuse; profile rules (scaffold cannot promote custom domains without `--include-custom-domains` and a matching authorization; preview lists only closed papers; launch requires all four); promotion state machine with injected command results, including failure on the second hostname; `--candidate-only` records a candidate and issues no `vercel alias set`; `--promote` refuses on a missing record, a record with failed checks, a manifest digest mismatch, and a `HEAD` mismatch, and issues no `vercel build` or `vercel deploy`.
- Tests use fixed fixture files and injected command runners. They never create or delete temporary files in the repository and never call Vercel or git for real.

### End-to-end tests
- A dry-run mode (`--dry-run`) executes every local stage (lock, identity, conflicts, tree, gates, build, artifact validation, manifest validation) and prints the deploy and promotion commands it would run without executing them. CI runs the dry run against the scaffold profile once `am-scaf-quality-gates-ci-4xx` exists.

### Structured logging
- Each run writes `artifacts/deploy-logs/<log-run-id>.jsonl` with `timestamp`, `logRunId`, `profile`, `mode`, `stage`, `command`, `exitCode`, `durationMs`, `commit`, `candidateUrl`, `deploymentId`, `hostname`, `check`, `expected`, `actual`, `authorizationRef`, `outcome`, and `message`. On refusal it retains the failing response body excerpt, HTTP status, and inspect output. Secrets and bypass tokens are never logged.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- `vercel inspect` output formats change; parsing must fail closed on unknown formats, never assume Ready.
- A stale `.vercel/output` from another checkout is the failure this whole script exists to prevent; freshness checks are mandatory even in dry run.
- Deployment Protection on previews means plain `fetch` of the candidate returns 401; use the protected-preview adapter for candidate checks.
- A recorded candidate can disappear if the project's deployment retention settings delete it; `--promote` must refuse with that explanation rather than rebuild silently.
- The script must never touch `~/projects/classic-patents.com` or its Vercel project.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-scaf-extract-scripts-7jm`: the donor scripts must be extracted with license notices before they are adapted.
- `am-scaf-quality-gates-ci-4xx`: the gate registry and profile runner the script calls.

Unblocks:
- `am-rel-vercel-setup-ituk`: the first authorized deploy uses this script.
- `am-rel-release-manifest-3gna`: the script validates the manifest inside the artifact.

Implement the six command classes so a change of description never changes the world
description:
# Implement the six command classes so a change of description never changes the world

**Epic:** `am-ep-runtime-iml` · **Batch:** A · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §12.6, §12.10 (stream allocation for measurement noise), §13.5 (observer adversarial row), §14.3 (hold-something-fixed), §17.4, §19.4 "Experiment controller" (traceability only)

## Background

The most serious conceptual bug an interactive physics site can ship is letting a re-description change the world: changing the frame speed in a relativity explanation that generates new events or restarts clocks, a camera setting that silently draws a new Brownian path, or a new estimator that quietly swaps the data it is estimating from. Each of those turns a teaching point ("the same events, described from another frame") into its opposite.

The plan makes the control classification **executable**: every command that can reach a laboratory instance belongs to exactly one of six classes, and the runtime enforces what must stay stable for each. The same machinery enables one of the site's strongest interactions: hold the world fixed and compare two descriptions or two measurements side by side (`am-reason-hold-fixed-comparison-xgxw`).

## Scope

In scope: the typed command envelope and union; per-class revision effects and invariants enforced by the instance controller; canonical scientific digests used to prove invariants; the manifest rule that every parameter and action declares its class; replay-grid rules for observation cadence; baseline and variant comparison; runtime fixture experiments and tests.

Out of scope (owned elsewhere): the store, identity set, and publication ordering `am-rt-snapshot-store-aft`; request refusals and the refusal-code registry `am-rt-typed-results-mqb`; the production stream allocation registry `am-rt-u64-identities-7ce`; worker transport `am-rt-worker-scheduler-7tl`; tape recording and the `blake3:` digest switch `am-rt-control-tapes-0gc`; control widgets `am-inst-parameter-controls-cmj9`; nonvisual equivalents `am-a11y-action-contracts-k75g`; browser lanes ``am-rt-browser-conformance-09i5``.

## Requirements

1. **The classes and their invariants.**

| Command class | What changes | What must remain stable |
|---|---|---|
| `setup-change` | Initial physical conditions or governing model | The old run stays identifiable; the new accepted run is explicit |
| `physical-intervention` | Conditions after a specified model time | Earlier accepted history |
| `observer-change` | Coordinate frame, origin, orientation, observer description | Physical worldlines, events, trial identity |
| `measurement-change` | Sampling, projection, exposure, calibration under an admitted observation model | The identified latent trajectory; the measurement result gets a new revision |
| `estimator-change` | Statistic, fitted model, inference assumptions | Selected observation data and their provenance |
| `presentation-change` | Camera, labels, layout, colors, explanation selection | Every scientific state and data identity |

2. **Command envelope.** `{ commandId, instanceId, actionIndex, class, payload }`, where the controller assigns `actionIndex` (the per-instance logical order the store uses for publication ordering) at dispatch. `physical-intervention` also carries `atSimulatedTime`. Payloads use canonical SI values keyed by parameter and quantity ids; unit formatting belongs to views.
3. **Revision effects.**
   - `setup-change`: increments `inputRevision`; creates a new `runId` with `parentRunId` set to the previous run; the new run starts at `stepIndex` 0 and its initial `simulatedTime`. The previous run remains retrievable by id in the instance history and on the tape, and the new accepted run is announced explicitly.
   - `physical-intervention`: increments `inputRevision`; keeps the `runId` when `atSimulatedTime` is not earlier than the latest accepted `simulatedTime`. A backdated intervention forks an explicitly identified new run (`parentRunId`, `forkedAtSimulatedTime`) and never rewrites accepted history.
   - `observer-change`: increments `observerRevision`; keeps `runId`, event identities, worldline identities, `stepIndex`, and trial identity; consumes zero random draws; never restarts clocks or generates events. The owner recomputes only derived coordinate descriptions into a new snapshot.
   - `measurement-change`: increments `measurementRevision`; keeps the latent trajectory identity and leaves latent streams untouched. Measurement-error draws come from their own logical stream, so changing a camera setting re-observes the same identified path.
   - `estimator-change`: increments `estimatorRevision`; keeps the selected observation data and their provenance; the estimate is recomputed.
   - `presentation-change`: changes no revision, no scientific state, and no data identity; never reaches a worker; is excluded from scientific digests; may be recorded on tapes for interface replay.
4. **Scientific digests.** `src/experiments/digest/scientificDigest.ts` defines the canonical byte encoding used to prove invariants and later reused by tapes: fields sorted by id; canonical SI values as IEEE-754 binary64 bit patterns, little-endian; integers as fixed-width little-endian; seeds as their canonical decimal strings in UTF-8; typed arrays with their layout id and shape; presentation state excluded. The digest is SHA-256 over those bytes (Web Crypto, available in browsers, workers, and Bun), written `host:sha256:<hex>`. Named digests: `latentPathDigest`, `eventSetDigest`, `worldlineDigest`, `observationDataDigest`, `estimateDigest`.
5. **Ordinary-language clarifications, named in the interface and tested.** A camera's physical exposure time is a measurement change. Moving the viewpoint of the rendered microscope is presentation. A moving detector is a physical component (setup or intervention), not a frame choice. "Describe this detector in another frame" never changes the experiment; "a detector moves differently" does.
6. **Declaration rule.** Every parameter and action in an experiment manifest (`commandClass` in `am-cm-schemas-experiment-fuu`) declares exactly one class. Registration fails for a parameter or action without a class. A control that would need two classes is split into two controls.
7. **Observation cadence and the replay grid.** Observation cadence subsamples an existing fixed logical path and never consumes a different random stream because the plot interval changed. Each stochastic experiment declares a replay grid (base spacing and stored horizon); supported observation intervals are positive integer multiples of the base spacing within the horizon. A requested interval off the grid is a request refusal with code `off-replay-grid` (domain kind `numerical`), ranked repairs naming the nearest supported intervals below and above, and the last accepted snapshot kept, using the shared refusal shape from `am-rt-typed-results-mqb`. It is never a silently resampled path. A later hierarchical Brownian-bridge refinement may permit path-consistent refinement only with its own tests and a stream-semantics version bump (not part of this bead). Equal seeds alone do not guarantee a pathwise-consistent comparison between arbitrary discretizations; the runtime never implies they do.
8. **Invariant enforcement.** The controller computes the relevant digests and draw counters before and after every command. In development and test builds a violated invariant throws with the class, the field, and both values. In production the controller keeps the last accepted snapshot and reports the execution outcome `invariant-violation`.
9. **Comparison support.** The controller can pin a baseline snapshot and apply exactly one command of a declared class to a variant. A variant from a description class (observer, measurement, estimator, presentation) shares the baseline's `runId` and latent data. A variant from a physical class is a new identified run with `baselineRunId`; when it reuses the baseline seed it is labeled "same random numbers, different setup" (common random numbers), never "independent trials". The comparison reports what remained fixed, what changed physically, and what was merely re-described.

## Technical Approach
