- Planned files: `src/experiments/commands/types.ts` (envelope and discriminated union keyed by `class`), `src/experiments/commands/apply.ts` (controller entry that assigns `actionIndex`, routes by class, updates revision counters, and enforces invariants before and after owner evaluation), `src/experiments/commands/invariants.ts`, `src/experiments/commands/replayGrid.ts`, `src/experiments/commands/comparison.ts`, `src/experiments/digest/scientificDigest.ts`.
- Runtime fixtures in `src/testing/runtime-fixtures/`, never shown to readers and excluded from production bundles:
  - `eventLedgerFixture.ts`: a handful of identified events and two worldlines, described in a frame selected by a signed speed $v/c \in (-1, 1)$ with the exact aligned boost $x' = \gamma(x - vt)$, $t' = \gamma(t - vx/c^2)$;
  - `seededWalkFixture.ts`: a small ensemble on a replay grid with a latent stream and a separate localization-noise stream, reading numbers from `drawTable.json`, a committed table of uniform and standard-normal values keyed by `(streamPurpose, tile, index)` whose header records the generation command and the SHA-256 of its contents. A draw accessor counts draws per stream. The table is fixture data, not a production generator; production streams come from the Philox port and the registry in `am-rt-u64-identities-7ce`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every command maps to exactly one class, and manifest registration refuses a parameter or action with no class or two classes.
- [ ] After an `observer-change`, `eventSetDigest`, `worldlineDigest`, `runId`, `stepIndex`, and every draw counter are unchanged, and `observerRevision` increments.
- [ ] After a `measurement-change`, `latentPathDigest` and the latent draw counter are unchanged, `measurementRevision` increments, and only the measurement-noise draw counter advances.
- [ ] After an `estimator-change`, `observationDataDigest` and provenance are unchanged.
- [ ] After a `presentation-change`, every scientific digest and revision counter is unchanged and no worker message is produced.
- [ ] A `setup-change` yields a new `runId` with `parentRunId`, while the old run remains retrievable by id.
- [ ] A backdated `physical-intervention` forks an explicitly identified run and leaves the parent's accepted history untouched.
- [ ] An off-grid observation interval is refused with `off-replay-grid`, ranked repairs, and the last accepted snapshot kept.
- [ ] A late response to an older observer change is refused by the store as `stale-action` (integration with `am-rt-snapshot-store-aft`).
- [ ] A physical-class variant that reuses the baseline seed is labeled as common random numbers, never as independent trials.
- [ ] The §13.5 adversarial row "changing observer means starting a new experiment" fails for its intended reason: a deliberately wrong test-only implementation of the frame slider as `setup-change` fails the invariant check on `runId` and `eventSetDigest`.
- [ ] `bun scripts/e2e-runtime-contracts.ts --suite commands` passes and writes JSONL evidence.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `commands.invariants.test.ts`: table-driven over all six classes with both fixtures; asserts the stable set, the changed set, and the revision counter effects.
- `observerChange.test.ts`: boost the event-ledger fixture through $v/c = 0.6, -0.6, 0.95, 0$ and back; identical event and worldline digests, zero draws; the round-trip description equals the original within an absolute tolerance of $10^{-12}$ in natural units, recorded as `tolerance`.
- `measurementChange.test.ts`: change exposure and localization error on the seeded walk; `latentPathDigest` identical; only the noise stream counter advances by the declared number of draws.
- `interventions.test.ts`: forward intervention keeps `runId`; backdated intervention forks with `parentRunId` and `forkedAtSimulatedTime`.
- `replayGrid.test.ts`: supported multiples subsample with zero draws; an off-grid interval is refused with the two nearest supported repairs; an interval beyond the stored horizon is refused.
- `scientificDigest.test.ts`: field order independence, `-0.0` versus `+0.0` distinguished, seeds above $2^{53}$ hashed from their decimal strings, presentation fields excluded.
- `comparison.test.ts`: description-class variants share run and data; physical-class variants create identified runs and the common-random-numbers label.
- `manifestClassDeclaration.test.ts`: registration refuses undeclared or double-class parameters.
- `adversarialObserver.test.ts`: the test-only wrong implementation fails on the named assertions; it is not importable from production code.

### End-to-end tests
- `bun scripts/e2e-runtime-contracts.ts --suite commands`: a scripted session applies all six classes, a backdated intervention, and an off-grid request to both fixtures inside a real Bun `Worker`, logging every command with digests before and after.
- Browser lanes (implemented by ``am-rt-browser-conformance-09i5`` on the fixture page): frame speed changed back and forth keeps `data-run-id` and the event digest; a measurement change keeps the latent digest; a presentation change produces zero worker messages.
- Obligations re-asserted on real instruments: BM-01 observation interval change keeps `data-run-id` and the latent-path digest shown in the test-only model note (`am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu`); BM-08 exposure and localization changes re-observe the same path (`am-bm-08-measurement-bias-h1ye`); SR-03 frame speed changes keep event and run identities (`am-sr-03-rod-simultaneity-0l5i` and row 9 of `am-ver-adversarial-audit-1ef`).

### Structured logging
Through the shared logger, suite `runtime-commands`, file `artifacts/test-logs/runtime-commands/<log-run-id>.jsonl`: `timestamp`, `suite`, `testId`, `beadId` (`am-rt-command-classes-dzp`), `instanceId`, `logRunId`, `runId`, `inputRevision`, `acceptedInputRevision`, `snapshotVersion`, `seed`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `comparisonKind`, `outcome`, `message`, and in `extra`: `commandClass`, `actionIndex`, `runIdBefore`, `runIdAfter`, `stepIndexBefore`, `stepIndexAfter`, `revisionsBefore`, `revisionsAfter`, `latentPathDigest`, `eventSetDigest`, `observationDataDigest`, `drawCounterDeltaByStream`, `refusalCode`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- The bug to prevent is not hypothetical: a frame-speed slider implemented as a setup change restarts clocks and looks plausible.
- Do not implement observation cadence by re-simulating at the new cadence; that consumes a different stream and breaks comparisons.
- Presentation changes must not trigger worker requests.
- A digest over formatted strings hides real differences; digest canonical bits.
- Common random numbers can isolate an effect, but they are not independent trials; the label says which.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-rt-snapshot-store-aft`: commands act on store instances, and publication ordering uses `actionIndex`.
- `am-rt-typed-results-mqb`: command refusals such as `off-replay-grid` use the shared request-refusal shape, and `invariant-violation` is an execution outcome.

Unblocks:
- `am-rt-worker-scheduler-7tl`: the scheduler routes commands by class and never sends presentation changes to workers.
- `am-rt-control-tapes-0gc`: tape events are classified by command class, ordered by `actionIndex`, and digested with `scientificDigest.ts`.
- `am-ver-adversarial-audit-1ef`: the observer-change adversarial row.
- `am-reason-hold-fixed-comparison-xgxw`: baseline and variant comparisons.
- `am-bm-08-measurement-bias-h1ye`: measurement changes that re-observe one latent path.
- `am-a11y-action-contracts-k75g`: equivalent actions are typed commands.
- `am-me-01-two-ledgers-g1re`: frame changes on the two-ledger instrument preserve the emission events.

title: Adapt control tapes with model identity, command classes, prediction events, checkpoints, and teaching tapes
description:
# Adapt control tapes with model identity, command classes, prediction events, checkpoints, and teaching tapes

**Epic:** `am-ep-runtime-iml` · **Batch:** B · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §12.11, §12.5, §12.6, §12.10, §7.7 (prediction events), §10.7 (permalinks), §13.3 (Einstein's displacement fixture) (traceability only)

## Background

Control history is a tape. A reader can scrub "Einstein's 0.8 micron" or "the boost to 0.6c" and see exactly the same states every time; a shared permalink restores what someone else saw, including what they predicted before seeing the result.

The donor museum's `src/physics/controlTape.ts` already implements a bounded versioned tape: `ControlTape` with `modelIdentity`, `initialConditions`, `seed`, `tickS`, `events` of `{tick, paramId, value, previousValue}`, checkpoints with `digestKind: "host" | "blake3"`, `MAX_TAPE_EVENTS = 3600` (60 seconds at 60 ticks per second), `quantizeFloat` with 6 decimal places, `validateTapeCompatibility`, a recorder that checkpoints every 60 ticks, a replayer that seeks the last valid checkpoint, and authored teaching tapes. Annus Mirabilis reuses its structure with new identities, and four donor choices must change:

- its `tick` is a UI concept, so events are reordered by the logical `actionIndex`;
- its `seed` is a JavaScript number, and its host digest starts from `(2166136261 ^ seed ^ tick) >>> 0`, which coerces the seed to 32 bits, so seeds that differ only above bit 32 (for example `1` and `4294967297`) produce identical digests; digests now come from canonical bytes;
- its events are unclassified, so every event now carries a command class;
- its blanket 6-decimal quantization destroys SI values below $10^{-6}$ (a Brownian radius of $5\times10^{-7}$ m, a diffusivity of $4.3\times10^{-13}$ m²/s) and truncates small viscosities to a few significant figures, so quantization now follows each parameter's declared policy.

A tape carries one experiment's model identity, so each named teaching tape is authored by the instrument whose model it replays.

## Scope

In scope: the version-2 tape schema; recorder and replayer adapted to command classes and `actionIndex`; prediction events; digest rules; compatibility refusals; bounds; the teaching-tape content format, validator, and replay engine; one runtime-fixture tape; the audit that the five named teaching tapes exist once their instruments register.

Out of scope (owned elsewhere):
- permalink compaction and size limits (`am-inst-permalink-tape-s677`);
- predict-mode UI (`am-inst-predict-mode-ti7m`);
- the canonical scientific digest function (`am-rt-command-classes-dzp`, reused here);
- conversion of stream positions to the `fs-rand` canonical checkpoint frame (`am-rt-memory-lifecycle-5ws`);
- the named teaching tapes' scientific content, authored in `am-bm-01-tracer-ensemble-hdly`, `am-bm-07-infer-molecular-number-frf9`, `am-sr-03-rod-simultaneity-0l5i`, `am-me-01-two-ledgers-g1re`, and `am-lq-05-independent-configurations-jtvo`;
- other instruments' own tapes (for example SR-04's "construct the map at 0.6c", authored in `am-sr-04-lorentz-map-px1k`);
- browser lanes (`am-rt-browser-conformance-09i5`).

## Requirements

1. **Tape schema version 2** carries: `tapeVersion: 2`; `tapeId`; `experimentId` and mode; model identity (`modelId`, `modelVersion`, and `artifactDigest` or the evaluator source hash); `constantSetId` (ids from `am-ref-constants-xik`, for example `einstein-1905-brownian-printed` or `modern-si-2019`); `seed` as a canonical decimal string (`am-rt-u64-identities-7ce`); `streamVersion`; `allocationId`; the replay grid identity (base spacing and horizon) for stochastic experiments; canonical SI `initialConditions`; events; checkpoints; `title`, `description`, `isTeachingSequence`.
2. **Events** are ordered by `actionIndex` (never a UI tick or wall-clock time) and carry `commandClass`, `commandId`, the canonical parameter or action id, the quantized canonical SI `value`, `previousValue`, and `atSimulatedTime` for `physical-intervention`.
3. **Prediction events** (`kind: "prediction"`) record the prompt id and either the chosen candidate id or a bounded sketch polyline (at most 64 points, coordinates quantized to $10^{-3}$ of each axis range). They carry no free text and no wall-clock timestamps.
4. **Quantization.** Quantize each parameter by the policy declared in its parameter schema, in canonical SI: integer multiples of a declared step, or a declared number of significant figures. A test proves that $1.35\times10^{-3}$ Pa·s, $5\times10^{-7}$ m, and $4.2944\times10^{-13}$ m²/s survive at their declared precision.
5. **Checkpoints** carry `actionIndex`, `stepIndex`, `simulatedTime`, the scientific-state digest from `scientificDigest.ts`, `digestKind`, stream positions per allocation as structured fields (`checkpointVersion`, `streamSemanticsVersion`, `seed`, `kernel`, `tile`, `index`, with 64-bit values as canonical decimal strings), and optional `label` and `teachingNote`. Presentation state is excluded from digests.
6. **Digest honesty.** Digests are written `host:sha256:<hex>` until `fs-blake3` is bound in the browser, then `blake3:<hex>`. Host code never produces a digest labeled `blake3` (the donor's test for this is ported).
7. **Compatibility refusals.** Replay refuses, with a typed refusal registered in the shared refusal-code registry (domain kind `input`) and without inventing state, when any of these differ from the recording:
   - tape version (`tape-version-unsupported`);
   - model identity (`tape-model-mismatch`);
   - artifact digest or evaluator hash (`tape-artifact-mismatch`);
   - constant set (`tape-constant-set-mismatch`);
   - stream-semantics version (`tape-stream-version-mismatch`);
   - allocation id (`tape-allocation-mismatch`);
   - replay grid (`tape-grid-mismatch`).

   The refusal offers a new run with the current model. `am-inst-permalink-tape-s677` reuses these codes for shared links.
8. **Bounds.** In-memory recordings stop at a maximum event count (donor default 3600) with a visible notice, never a silent drop. Compact URL serialization belongs to `am-inst-permalink-tape-s677`.
9. **Time and randomness.** Playback uses host-fed time through the tick scheduler, but the scientific state depends only on events and executed steps: replaying at any playback speed yields identical digests. No `Math.random` in any frame loop or scientific path. A refusal is a museum label and the last legal state is kept.
10. **Teaching tapes** are content files `content/experiments/tapes/<id>.yaml` validated by schema. The plan names five, each authored by the instrument whose model identity it replays:
    - "Einstein's 0.8 micron" (BM-01);
    - "Perrin's count" (BM-07);
    - "the boost to 0.6c" (SR-03: select the simultaneous pair of events 10 light-seconds apart, reveal $\Delta t' = -7.5$ s, see the 12.5 light-second separation refused as a length, then see 8 light-seconds credited as the length measured with frame-simultaneous endpoints);
    - "the two pulses" (ME-01);
    - "the locked positions" (LQ-05).

    This bead ships the format, validator, and replay engine plus one runtime-fixture tape. The audit enumerates the five names with their authoring instruments and fails once any of those instruments is registered without its tape. A named tape whose model identity belongs to a different experiment is rejected.
11. **Einstein's 0.8 micron, scientific expectations** (authored in BM-01, checked by this bead's audit when present). The tape runs on the historical constant set `einstein-1905-brownian-printed`:
    - as printed in paper 2 §5: $N = 6\times10^{23}$, the viscosity of water at 17 °C $k = 1.35\times10^{-2}$ poise ($1.35\times10^{-3}$ Pa·s), and the particle diameter 0.001 mm (radius $a = 0.5\,\mu$m);
    - $R = 8.31\times10^{7}$ erg/(mol·K), the value Einstein prints in the light-quanta paper, because paper 2 §5 appears not to print $R$ (confirm on the facsimile; the constant-set record states the provenance);
    - $T = 290.15$ K, the site's conversion of the printed 17 °C.

    Then $\lambda_x = \sqrt{2Dt}$ is $0.795\,\mu$m at 1 s and $6.16\,\mu$m at 60 s (full precision 0.7947833 and 6.156365 μm; 0.7946 and 6.155 μm if 17 °C is taken as 290 K). Einstein printed "$\lambda_x = 8\times10^{-5}$ cm = 0,8 Mikron" and "ca. 6 Mikron". With the modern exact $k_B$ and the printed viscosity (`modern-si-2019` with the printed $k$, $a$, and $T$), the values are 0.794 and 6.15 μm (full precision 0.7935339 and 6.146687 μm). Every displayed number names its constant set: at two significant figures the historical set shows 0.79 and 6.2 μm, and "6.1 μm" appears only as the modern-$k_B$ value with that set named.

## Technical Approach

- Planned files: `src/experiments/tapes/schema.ts`, `src/experiments/tapes/recorder.ts`, `src/experiments/tapes/replayer.ts`, `src/experiments/tapes/digest.ts` (prefix rules over `scientificDigest.ts`), `src/experiments/tapes/quantize.ts`, `src/experiments/tapes/teachingTapes.test.ts`, `src/testing/runtime-fixtures/fixture-walk.tape.yaml`.
- Start from the extracted donor `controlTape.ts` (`am-scaf-extract-runtime-utilities-99y`); keep its structure and still-valid tests, migrate identities, and replace its host digest.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Recording and replaying the same actions with the same model, seed, stream version, allocation, and constant set reproduces identical scientific digests at two different playback speeds.
- [ ] Every event carries a command class and an `actionIndex`; presentation events never change digests.
- [ ] Prediction events (candidate and bounded sketch) survive serialization and replay; free text is rejected by the schema.
- [ ] Replay refuses each mismatch type with its registered code and offers a new run.
- [ ] Seeds `9007199254740993` and `18446744073709551615` round-trip through tapes unchanged, and seeds `1` and `4294967297` produce different digests (the donor collision regression).
- [ ] Quantization preserves the three SI examples in requirement 4 at their declared precision.
- [ ] No digest labeled `blake3` is produced by host code.
- [ ] Exceeding the event bound shows a notice and never drops events silently.
- [ ] The teaching-tape audit lists the five named tapes with their authoring instruments (BM-01, BM-07, SR-03, ME-01, LQ-05), rejects a named tape carrying another experiment's model identity, and passes once the instruments supply them.
- [ ] A teaching tape whose expected displayed values omit their constant-set id fails validation.
- [ ] `bun scripts/e2e-runtime-contracts.ts --suite tapes` passes and writes JSONL evidence.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `tapes.replay.test.ts`: record a runtime-fixture session with observer, measurement, intervention, and presentation commands plus a prediction; replay at two playback speeds; compare digests at every checkpoint.
- `tapes.compatibility.test.ts`: each mismatch type is refused with its code.
- `tapes.quantize.test.ts`: SI parameters at extreme magnitudes under step and significant-figure policies; the donor's 6-decimal behavior is shown to destroy the small values (documentation assertion).
- `tapes.digest.test.ts`: prefix rules; the `1` versus `4294967297` seed regression.
- `tapes.u64.test.ts`: seed boundary values from `src/testing/fixtures/u64-boundaries.json`.
- `tapes.bounds.test.ts`: the event bound and its notice.
- `teachingTapes.test.ts`: schema validation of every tape file; the five-name audit with authoring instruments; rejection of a named tape with a foreign model identity; rejection of an expected displayed value without a `constantSetId`.

### End-to-end tests
- `bun scripts/e2e-runtime-contracts.ts --suite tapes`: record the fixture session in one Bun `Worker`, serialize, replay in a fresh `Worker`, compare digests and the restored prediction, and run every compatibility refusal, logging each step.
- Browser lanes (implemented by `am-rt-browser-conformance-09i5`): scrubbing the fixture tape back and forth reproduces identical digests; a tape URL opened in a fresh context restores identical digests and the recorded prediction.
- Obligations re-asserted on real instruments:
  - BM-01 plays "Einstein's 0.8 micron" and displays 0.795 μm at 1 s and 6.16 μm at 60 s (0.79 and 6.2 μm at two figures) labeled with `einstein-1905-brownian-printed`, with identical digests on repeated scrubbing (`am-bm-01-tracer-ensemble-hdly`, `am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu`);
  - SR-03 plays "the boost to 0.6c" with identical event digests on scrubbing (`am-sr-03-rod-simultaneity-0l5i`);
  - a permalink with a prediction opens in a fresh context with identical state (`am-inst-permalink-tape-s677`).

### Structured logging
Through the shared logger, suite `runtime-tapes`, file `artifacts/test-logs/runtime-tapes/<log-run-id>.jsonl`: `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId` (this execution of the suite), `testId`, `beadId` (`am-rt-control-tapes-0gc`), `instanceId`, `runId` (the experiment realization being recorded or replayed), `modelVersion`, `artifactDigest`, `seed`, `streamVersion`, `expected`, `actual`, `comparisonKind` (`bitwise` for digests), `outcome`, `durationMs`, `message`, and in `extra`: `tapeId`, `experimentId`, `constantSetId`, `actionIndex`, `commandClass`, `digest`, `digestKind`, `refusalCode`, `playbackSpeed`, `allocationId`, `authoringInstrument`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Tapes are replay artifacts: never upgrade an old tape silently when stream semantics change; refuse it and offer a new run.
- Keep teaching tapes authored against the constant sets they claim (Einstein's printed viscosity and $N$ for "Einstein's 0.8 micron"), never modern constants presented as his.
- Tapes must not store private notebook text; predictions are structured choices or bounded sketches only.
- A digest over quantized floats hides differences below the quantum; digest canonical bits of the accepted state, and quantize only the recorded control values.
- A tape recorded against one instrument's model cannot be replayed by another instrument; that is a model-identity refusal, not a convenience to work around.
- The same displacement differs in its third figure between constant sets (6.16 versus 6.15 μm at 60 s); an unlabeled two-figure "6.1 μm" invites exactly the mix-up the constant-set id prevents.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-rt-command-classes-dzp`: events are classified by command class, ordered by `actionIndex`, and digested with `scientificDigest.ts`.
- `am-rt-u64-identities-7ce`: seeds, stream positions, and allocation ids are canonical 64-bit identities.
- `am-scaf-extract-runtime-utilities-99y`: the donor tape implementation to adapt.

Unblocks:
- `am-inst-predict-mode-ti7m`: prediction events.
- `am-inst-permalink-tape-s677`: compact tape permalinks and the reused compatibility codes.
- `am-inst-real-rate-mode-gtez`: real-rate playback uses the replay clock.
- `am-reason-explanation-replay-35ds`: the notebook references tapes and accepted identities.
- `am-bm-01-tracer-ensemble-hdly`, `am-bm-07-infer-molecular-number-frf9`, `am-sr-03-rod-simultaneity-0l5i`, `am-me-01-two-ledgers-g1re`, `am-lq-05-independent-configurations-jtvo`: they author the five named teaching tapes.
- `am-sr-04-lorentz-map-px1k`: authors its own "construct the map at 0.6c" tape.
- `am-rt-browser-conformance-09i5`: tape replay and restoration lanes.

title: Implement the reproducibility contract, execution labels, and truthful fallbacks
description:
# Implement the reproducibility contract, execution labels, and truthful fallbacks

**Epic:** `am-ep-runtime-iml` · **Batch:** B · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §10.1 (kernel-source labels), §12.9, §2.2 (provenance tied to ownership), §17.3 (fallback label never `wasm`) (traceability only)

## Background

"Deterministic" is easy to overclaim. The same Rust source does not guarantee bitwise-identical floating-point results across architectures, compilers, browsers, and fast-math modes. And "powered by WASM" is easy to fake: a loaded module that never produced the displayed number earns nothing. The donor museum already separates packaged surfaces, loaded artifacts, typed refusal boundaries, and accepted steps (`HONEST_PLACEHOLDER`, `TS_FALLBACK`, `WASM` in `coverageManifest.ts`; `"wasm" | "ts-fallback" | "unloaded"` in `genericWasm.ts`). Its `genericWasm.ts` also shows the trap: a module-global `source` flips to `"wasm"` once a module loads. This bead keeps the underlying truth, derives execution state only from accepted provenance, and gives readers plain wording.

Precision about comparisons matters as much as the labels. Some cross-engine comparisons can honestly be bitwise and others cannot, and the difference follows from the arithmetic, not from preference:

- Philox4x32-10 counter output is pure integer arithmetic: bitwise everywhere.
- Uniform draws use the exact 53-bit ladder: bitwise.
- Coin and uniform walk steps use only IEEE-754 multiplication, addition, and correctly rounded `sqrt` (FrankenSim's `fs_math::det::sqrt` is the hardware square root): bitwise when both engines evaluate the same operations in the same order.
- Gaussian steps and `philox_normals` use Box–Muller with `ln` and `cos`; upstream uses `fs_math::det` strict functions and JavaScript uses `Math.log` and `Math.cos`: tolerance-based.
- The FTCS stepper: FrankenSim's `Csr::spmv` accumulates each row in ascending column order with fused multiply-add, but every stencil coefficient is $\pm1$ or $-2$, so fused and unfused products are exact and agree. The fields are therefore bitwise when the TypeScript stepper uses the same summation order and the same unfused update $u + r\,y$ with $r$ computed in the same order. Any other arrangement is tolerance-based and must say so.

## Scope

In scope: the written reproducibility contract; per-run engine selection; derivation of the execution state and model-note data from accepted snapshots; the fallback registry; replay metadata recording bitwise versus tolerance comparisons; the no-`SharedArrayBuffer` requirement; the "fallback label is never FrankenSim" check in `scripts/verify-wasm-artifacts.ts`.

Out of scope (owned elsewhere): the public wording, label component, placement, and accessibility of labels and the model note `am-inst-execution-labels-5ywv` (it maps this bead's derived states to the four exact labels); the WASM artifact and its digests `am-fs-slim-artifact-0yh`; the Philox vector cross-check `am-fs-philox-ts-port-7kp`; the full equivalence of the TypeScript walk and FTCS fallbacks with WASM `am-ref-diffusion-lr3`; quantity-specific verification records `am-ver-quantity-records-fby2`; browser lanes ``am-rt-browser-conformance-09i5``.

## Requirements

1. **The contract, stated precisely** in `docs/DETERMINISM.md`. Reproducibility holds for the same admitted model, executable, parameters, constant set, seed, stream semantics, and logical actions. Rendering cadence and worker scheduling never change the scientific state. The site does not promise bitwise identity across all architectures, compilers, browsers, and fast-math modes. The document lists the comparison kind for each case in the background above, records each export's FrankenSim determinism class from its `CONTRACT.md` (`Deterministic`, `DeterministicPerIsa`, or `Fast`) without upgrading it downstream, and states that fixed random goldens test stream semantics, distribution tests test statistical properties, and neither alone proves the physical model.
2. **Public execution labels** (exact wording, rendered by `am-inst-execution-labels-5ywv`):
   - "Ideal model, computed with FrankenSim": an accepted call to the registered FrankenSim owner produced this snapshot.
   - "Ideal model, host calculation": the audited TypeScript reference evaluator produced it. Closed-form physics is not a deficiency; the papers are closed-form.
   - "Static worked example": no live computation; an authored worked case.
   - "This experiment is unavailable on this device."
3. **Derived execution state.** `deriveExecutionState(view)` is a pure function of the store's `ExperimentView`: `frankensim-accepted` only when the accepted snapshot's `provenance.ownerKind` is `frankensim` and its capability id and artifact digest are registered; `host-accepted` when `ownerKind` is `host-reference`; `static-example` when no live snapshot exists and the authored example is shown; `unavailable` when the view state is unavailable (`environment-unsupported`, restart bound exceeded, or `artifact-mismatch` with no admissible fallback). Loader state is not an input to the function (enforced by its type). While a newer request is pending, the state describes the last accepted snapshot.
4. **Model-note data.** `modelNoteData(view, registry)` returns model id and version, owner (capability id and export, or evaluator id and function), `artifactDigest` or evaluator source hash, determinism class, `streamVersion`, seed, constant set, accepted revisions and `snapshotVersion`, the comparison records that validate this owner (kind and tolerance), the fallback reason when a fallback runs (`artifact-unavailable`, `capability-not-registered`, `artifact-mismatch`, `environment-unsupported`, `engine-refused`), and a link target for the quantity's verification record.
5. **Engine selection per run.** At run creation choose, in order: an admitted and instantiated FrankenSim capability whose `modelVersion` and `streamVersion` match the run's recorded identity; the registered host reference evaluator; the static worked example; unavailable. A checksum match alone is not compatibility. A running stochastic experiment never switches engines without a new identified run and compatible replay semantics. Deterministic closed-form evaluations may change owner between evaluations, and each accepted snapshot carries its own provenance.
6. **Fallback registry.** Each experiment with a live owner declares its admitted fallbacks and, per output, the expected comparison kind: the TypeScript reference evaluator for selected algebraic cases, the random walk, and the 1D FTCS stepper (the same scheme with the same `ftcs-unstable` refusal as the WASM export). An experiment with no fallback declares that explicitly.
7. **Always available.** The static reader and worked examples render with JavaScript disabled, with WASM blocked, and without workers.
8. **No isolation requirement.** Never require `SharedArrayBuffer` or cross-origin isolation (COOP and COEP). Everything works in a non-isolated tab.
9. **Artifact script check.** Add to `scripts/verify-wasm-artifacts.ts`: with the bundle instantiated, a host-produced snapshot derives `host-accepted`; a WASM-produced accepted snapshot with the manifest digest derives `frankensim-accepted`; a WASM response whose digest is absent from the manifest never reaches the store.

## Technical Approach

- Planned files: `docs/DETERMINISM.md`, `src/experiments/provenance/executionState.ts`, `src/experiments/provenance/modelNoteData.ts`, `src/experiments/provenance/engineSelection.ts`, `src/experiments/provenance/fallbackRegistry.ts`, `src/experiments/provenance/replayMetadata.ts`.
- Use the extracted donor `genericWasm.ts` only as a loading pattern; never read its `source` state for labels.
- Runtime fixture `src/testing/runtime-fixtures/fixtureNormals.ts`: an experiment with a host owner built on `src/physics/reference/philox.ts` and a FrankenSim owner calling `philox_normals` and `brownian_frames` (kernels 0 and 3) from the pinned artifact, used to exercise selection, derivation, and comparison records without depending on paper evaluators.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/DETERMINISM.md` states the contract and the per-case comparison kinds, and a phrase scan finds no claim of cross-platform bitwise identity.
- [ ] A snapshot produced by the host evaluator derives `host-accepted` even when the WASM module has loaded.
- [ ] A snapshot produced by an accepted FrankenSim call with a registered digest derives `frankensim-accepted`, and its model-note data carry the digest and determinism class.
- [ ] An attempted engine switch during a stochastic run is refused unless a new identified run is created; a version mismatch refuses selection even when the checksum matches.
- [ ] Replay records name `bitwise` or `tolerance` for every comparison, with tolerance values.
- [ ] The site functions fully in a non-isolated context with `SharedArrayBuffer` unavailable.
- [ ] With JavaScript disabled, worked examples and readings render; with WASM blocked, instruments derive host or unavailable states.
- [ ] The artifact script check in requirement 9 passes.
- [ ] `bun scripts/e2e-runtime-contracts.ts --suite provenance` passes and writes JSONL evidence.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `executionState.test.ts`: every combination of provenance, view state, pending requests, and loader state, including "loaded but no accepted result" and "WASM result with an unregistered digest" (rejected upstream, never derived as FrankenSim).
- `engineSelection.test.ts`: selection order; refusal of mid-run stochastic engine switches; closed-form owner changes per evaluation; version mismatch refusal.
- `replayMetadata.test.ts`: comparison kinds and tolerance values required.
- `fallbackRegistry.test.ts`: every compiled experiment with a live owner declares fallbacks or an explicit none, with per-output comparison kinds.
- `determinismDoc.test.ts`: required statements present; forbidden overclaims absent.

### End-to-end tests
- `bun scripts/e2e-runtime-contracts.ts --suite provenance`: `fixtureNormals` runs twice with the same seed as two identified runs, once in the host worker and once in the WASM worker with the pinned artifact; the runner compares integer-derived uniform draws and kernel 0 walk positions bitwise and normals and kernel 3 positions within the recorded tolerance, derives both execution states, and logs every comparison record.
- Browser lanes (implemented by ``am-rt-browser-conformance-09i5``): WASM blocked by request interception derives the host state with the fallback reason; with WASM allowed the FrankenSim state appears only after the first accepted result, not at module load; a non-isolated lane asserts `crossOriginIsolated === false` and passes; a JavaScript-disabled lane shows the worked example and readings.
- Obligations re-asserted on real instruments: BM-01 labels and model notes (`am-inst-execution-labels-5ywv`, `am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu`).

### Structured logging
Through the shared logger, suite `runtime-provenance`, file `artifacts/test-logs/runtime-provenance/<log-run-id>.jsonl`: `timestamp`, `suite`, `testId`, `beadId` (`am-rt-determinism-fallbacks-8i4`), `instanceId`, `logRunId`, `runId`, `executionLabel`, `artifactDigest`, `streamVersion`, `seed`, `comparisonKind`, `tolerance`, `expected`, `actual`, `outcome`, `message`, and in `extra`: `executionState`, `ownerKind`, `capabilityId`, `determinismClass`, `fallbackReason`, `maxDeviation`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Never write "WASM Core" or similar badges from load state; the donor learned this the hard way.
- Tolerance comparisons need a stated tolerance chosen per quantity and regime with the helpers of `am-ver-precision-display-5e5`; record it, never hide it.
- A checksum proves byte identity, not compatible meaning; engine selection must also match model and stream versions.
- A bitwise expectation that fails is a finding to investigate (a changed operation order, a fused operation, a different sqrt), not a reason to switch silently to a tolerance.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-rt-snapshot-store-aft`: states derive from accepted snapshot provenance and view state.
- `am-rt-typed-results-mqb`: unavailable, refused, and outcome states are typed.
- `am-fs-slim-artifact-0yh`: the pinned artifact, its manifest, and `scripts/verify-wasm-artifacts.ts`, which this bead extends.

Unblocks:
- `am-inst-execution-labels-5ywv`: instrument chrome renders the derived states and model-note data.
- `am-rt-worker-scheduler-7tl`: engine selection decides which worker a run uses.

title: Enforce buffer ownership, WASM memory-growth safety, disposal, visibility pausing, and crash recovery
description:
# Enforce buffer ownership, WASM memory-growth safety, disposal, visibility pausing, and crash recovery

**Epic:** `am-ep-runtime-iml` · **Batch:** B · **Priority:** P0 · **Labels:** runtime, performance · **Plan sections:** §12.7 (memory), §12.8 (resource ownership and recovery), §16.2 (reduced motion), §16.4 (resource lifecycle budget), §17.4 (context loss, restart) (traceability only)

## Background

Brownian ensembles of up to 10 000 particles, diffusion frames, and Three.js studios move large buffers between WASM linear memory, workers, and renderers. Four classes of silent corruption follow if ownership is loose:

- **Memory growth.** When a `WebAssembly.Memory` grows, its old `ArrayBuffer` is detached. A typed-array view retained over the old buffer becomes zero-length, so reads return `undefined` and arithmetic quietly produces `NaN`; hand-written views that cache an offset into a re-fetched buffer read the wrong bytes.
- **Detached snapshot data.** A transferred buffer is detached on the sending side while a published "immutable" snapshot still exposes it.
- **Mutable reuse.** A pooled buffer is reused behind an immutable snapshot. The donor's `BoundedBufferPool` (in `transport.ts`) makes this easy: under pressure `acquire` evicts the oldest active lease and hands its buffer to a new caller, and it can allocate on `SharedArrayBuffer` when `useSharedMemory` is set.
- **Leaks.** Repeated route changes leak workers, GPU contexts, listeners, and animation frames until a phone gives up.

Recovery after a crash, context loss, or artifact mismatch must never resume from a checkpoint whose meaning has changed. A checksum is evidence of byte identity, not of compatible meaning.

## Scope

In scope: buffer lifetime rules; WASM memory-growth handling; pooling rules; disposal helpers; visibility, background-tab, and reduced-motion pausing; concurrency limits for heavy laboratories; the degradation policy under load; checkpoint-validated recovery after crashes, context loss, or artifact mismatch; the lifecycle diagnostics counters used by stress and conformance lanes.

Out of scope (owned elsewhere): the scheduler's restart bound `am-rt-worker-scheduler-7tl`; the repeated-route stress run with heap sampling in CI `am-plat-resource-stress-9zgu` (it consumes this bead's counters); Three.js studio construction and scene rebuild `am-inst-three-studio-y0y0`; device profile decisions `am-gov-decision-device-profiles-1zm`; browser lanes ``am-rt-browser-conformance-09i5``.

## Requirements

1. **Buffers stay out of React state.** Large particle and field buffers live in the instance owner and snapshots; React state holds ids and small summaries only.
2. **WASM memory growth.** Never retain a JavaScript view into WASM linear memory across any call into the module. The default is copy-out: `wasm-bindgen` returns `Vec<f64>` as a fresh `Float64Array` copy, which a test verifies against the pinned generated glue (the returned array's `buffer` is not the module's `memory.buffer`). Any zero-copy view must go through `wasmViews.ts`, which tracks a memory generation (incremented whenever `memory.buffer` identity changes) and checks it on every access; a mismatch throws in development and test builds and yields the execution outcome `invariant-violation` in production.
3. **Ownership.** Transferring a buffer changes ownership. Never transfer or detach a buffer that a published snapshot still exposes (refused, with the snapshot version named). Never reuse a mutable buffer behind an immutable snapshot. Pools recycle only buffers whose reference count (snapshots plus views) is zero. The donor pool's eviction of active leases is never used for snapshot-exposed buffers; it may serve display-only scratch buffers that no snapshot references. `SharedArrayBuffer` allocation is never enabled.
4. **Rendering efficiency.** Reuse geometry and buffers, use instancing where appropriate, and publish UI summaries (tables, accessible text) at a bounded rate. Scientific stepping and display interpolation keep separate schedules.
5. **Disposal.** When an owner ends, dispose of Three.js geometries, materials, textures, render targets, controls, subscriptions, event listeners, animation frames, observers, and workers. `src/visuals/three/dispose.ts` provides one traversal helper used by every studio, testable without a WebGL context.
6. **Pausing.** Pause laboratories that are not visible (`IntersectionObserver`, `document.visibilityState`, and `pagehide`). Pausing issues no new step requests, lets an in-flight chunk finish and be accepted, and preserves `simulatedTime`, stream positions, and the tape; resuming continues the same run. With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, autoplaying stepping and animation pause, the current state stays visible, and manual stepping remains available.
7. **Concurrency limit.** Limit concurrent heavy laboratories. Provisional defaults: two on desktop-class devices and one on constrained mobile devices, chosen locally from `navigator.hardwareConcurrency` and the viewport (never transmitted anywhere), stored in `src/experiments/lifecycle/limits.ts` with their rationale; the final values are adopted from `am-gov-decision-device-profiles-1zm` when it is recorded. Exceeding the limit suspends the least recently used heavy laboratory with replayable state (seed, stream positions, tape, checkpoint) so it resumes exactly.
8. **Degradation policy.** A depleted performance budget reduces visual detail (displayed particle count, resolution, rendering frequency) or pauses with an explanation. It never changes a model's diffusivity, enlarges an integration step, changes the model, reduces the statistical sample behind an inference, or skips scientific time. Rendering a subset of particles never changes the ensemble used for results.
9. **Recovery.** A worker crash, WebGL context loss, or artifact mismatch pauses the laboratory while the book remains usable, and numbers are never relabeled during the pause. Recovery validates the checkpoint's model id and version, protocol, layout, and tape schema versions, parameter digest, seed, and stream semantics before continuing. For `fs-rand` streams the stream position is the canonical little-endian `StreamCheckpoint` frame of 83 bytes: magic `FSRCKPT\0` (8), domain `org.frankensim.fs-rand.stream-checkpoint.v1` (43), checkpoint version (u32), stream-semantics version (u32), seed (u64), kernel (u32), tile (u32), and next index (u64), decoded fail-closed with trailing bytes refused, using the codec from `am-fs-philox-ts-port-7kp`. If anything differs, the laboratory begins a visibly new run (`parentRunId` set, the reason stated). On `webglcontextrestored` the studio rebuilds from the current snapshot without restarting the run or consuming randomness.
10. **Diagnostics counters.** Extending the test-build diagnostics registry started by `am-rt-snapshot-store-aft`: live workers, WebGL contexts created, lost, and disposed, tracked listeners, animation-frame handles, observers, live and pooled buffer bytes, and suspended laboratories. Counters exist only in test builds; a bundle check proves their absence from production.

## Technical Approach

- Planned files: `src/experiments/memory/buffers.ts` (owned typed arrays, reference counts, pool), `src/experiments/memory/wasmViews.ts` (copy-out helpers and generation checks), `src/experiments/lifecycle/visibility.ts`, `src/experiments/lifecycle/limits.ts`, `src/experiments/lifecycle/concurrency.ts`, `src/experiments/lifecycle/recovery.ts` (checkpoint validation and new-run decisions), `src/experiments/lifecycle/diagnostics.ts`, `src/visuals/three/dispose.ts`.
- Runtime fixture `src/testing/runtime-fixtures/heavyFixture.ts`: a buffer-heavy stepping experiment backed by the pinned artifact's `brownian_frames` export, used for growth, ownership, pausing, concurrency, and recovery tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Forcing memory growth between calls (for example `memory.grow(1)` from JavaScript after a call) never lets a stale view be read: copy-out results are correct and a retained raw view is caught by the generation check.
- [ ] The pinned glue returns `Vec<f64>` as copies (tested).
- [ ] Transferring a buffer referenced by a live snapshot is refused; pooled buffers are recycled only at zero references; no code path enables shared memory.
- [ ] Mounting and unmounting a runtime fixture laboratory 100 times leaves worker, context, listener, animation-frame, observer, and buffer counts at baseline.
- [ ] A hidden laboratory stops stepping and resumes the same run with the same `simulatedTime` and stream positions; reduced motion pauses autoplay while showing the current state.
- [ ] Exceeding the heavy-laboratory limit suspends the least recently used laboratory, and its resumed scientific digest equals the digest it would have had without suspension.
- [ ] Under a simulated low budget, displayed particles decrease while moments and inference use the full ensemble (digests unchanged).
- [ ] Forced context loss and forced worker crash pause the laboratory with an explanation; recovery continues only when checkpoint validation passes, otherwise a new run id with its reason appears.
- [ ] `bun scripts/e2e-runtime-contracts.ts --suite memory` passes and writes JSONL evidence.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `buffers.ownership.test.ts`: reference counting across snapshots and views; refused transfer of referenced buffers; pool recycling only at zero references; eviction never touches snapshot-exposed buffers.
- `wasmViews.growth.test.ts`: with the pinned slim artifact loaded in Bun, grow memory between calls; verify copy-out values against a second copy; verify the generation check throws on a retained raw view.
- `glue.copy.test.ts`: generated glue returns arrays not backed by `memory.buffer`.
- `recovery.checkpoint.test.ts`: a valid checkpoint continues; each single-field mutation (model version, protocol version, tape schema version, parameter digest, seed, stream-semantics version, kernel, tile, index, magic, domain, a trailing byte) forces a new run with the named reason.
- `pause.test.ts`: visibility, `pagehide`, and reduced-motion pausing with continuation of the same run.
- `concurrency.test.ts`: least-recently-used suspension and exact resumption digests.
- `degradation.test.ts`: reduced displayed detail leaves scientific digests unchanged.
- `dispose.test.ts`: the traversal helper disposes every geometry, material, and texture in a constructed scene graph without a WebGL context.

### End-to-end tests
- `bun scripts/e2e-runtime-contracts.ts --suite memory`: growth, ownership, checkpoint recovery, and concurrency scenarios with real workers and the pinned artifact, logging counters at every step.
- Browser lanes (implemented by ``am-rt-browser-conformance-09i5``): 50 navigations between a reading page and the fixture page return all counters to baseline; `WEBGL_lose_context` on a minimal WebGL fixture view pauses with the static fallback and restores the same run; scrolling a running fixture out of view pauses stepping and scrolling back continues it; a mobile lane opens three heavy fixtures and observes suspension and exact resumption.
- Obligations elsewhere: the full stress run with heap sampling (`am-plat-resource-stress-9zgu`); studio context-loss rebuild (`am-inst-three-studio-y0y0`); BM-01 visibility pausing in the slice (`am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu`).

### Structured logging
Through the shared logger, suite `runtime-memory`, file `artifacts/test-logs/runtime-memory/<log-run-id>.jsonl`: `timestamp`, `suite`, `testId`, `beadId` (`am-rt-memory-lifecycle-5ws`), `instanceId`, `logRunId`, `runId`, `snapshotVersion`, `seed`, `streamVersion`, `expected`, `actual`, `outcome`, `message`, and in `extra`: `liveWorkers`, `webglContexts`, `listeners`, `animationFrames`, `liveBufferBytes`, `pooledBufferBytes`, `memoryGeneration`, `checkpointValid`, `checkpointMismatchField`, `newRunCreated`, `displayedParticles`, `ensembleSize`, `suspendedLaboratories`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- `wasm-bindgen` returns copies for `Vec<f64>`, but hand-written zero-copy views do not; audit every view and keep them in `wasmViews.ts`.
- Browsers cap WebGL contexts per page; leaking one per remount fails silently on mobile.
- Pausing must not reset tapes or seeds; a resumed run is the same run.
- The donor pool's detached-buffer check (`byteLength === 0` then reallocate) hides a bug instead of reporting it; a detached snapshot buffer is an invariant violation here.
- A "lighter" mode that samples fewer particles for statistics is a physics change, not a performance setting.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-rt-worker-scheduler-7tl`: recovery and pausing coordinate with the scheduler's queues and restart bound; through it, the pinned slim artifact and the Philox checkpoint codec are available.

Unblocks:
- `am-inst-three-studio-y0y0`: studios use the disposal helper and context-loss recovery rules.
- `am-plat-resource-stress-9zgu`: the CI stress run asserts these lifecycle guarantees using these counters.
- ``am-rt-browser-conformance-09i5``: browser lanes for lifecycle, visibility, context loss, and concurrency.

title: Build the instance-scoped accepted-snapshot store with full identity fields
description:
# Build the instance-scoped accepted-snapshot store with full identity fields

**Epic:** `am-ep-runtime-iml` · **Batch:** A · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §12.5, §12.6 (revisions by command class), §12.8, §2.2 (usePatentPhysics finding), §17.4, §19.4 "Experiment controller" (traceability only)

## Background

The donor's `usePatentPhysics.ts` keeps module-global parameter maps keyed by patent id and increments a control-change tick. That design cannot host two independent instances of one experiment, cannot keep a stochastic run alive across re-renders, and confuses a UI event count with physical time. Annus Mirabilis replaces it with one owner per laboratory instance that publishes **immutable accepted snapshots**. Every view of that instance (plots, equations, scene geometry, tables, accessibility summaries, the result weave) reads the same snapshot, so numerical truth has exactly one owner and a reader never sees two slightly different numbers for the same quantity.

Two failure modes shape this store beyond the donor's. First, a reader who switches `?view=` faces may cause the React subtree holding an instrument to unmount and mount again; if a remount creates a fresh owner, the experiment silently restarts. The store therefore keys instances by a stable **placement** and reattaches a remount to the running owner. Second, stale results are not only about physical inputs. A late response computed for an older observer, measurement, or estimator setting carries the same `runId` and `inputRevision` as the newer one. Ordering publication by a per-instance logical `actionIndex` closes that gap for every command class.

This store is the foundation of every instrument, of live equation values, and of the "identical accepted snapshot ids across views" browser acceptance rule.

## Scope

In scope: snapshot types and the identity set; publication ordering; the `ExperimentView` read model with requested, accepted, pending, refused, paused, and unavailable states; the placement-keyed instance registry and owner lifecycle; the React hooks; the per-view frame record for `renderTime`; verification data attributes and test-build diagnostics; the import-boundary test that keeps physics out of components; a small runtime fixture experiment and the `scripts/e2e-runtime-contracts.ts` runner that later runtime beads extend.

Out of scope (owned elsewhere): command semantics and revision effects `am-rt-command-classes-dzp`; output statuses, request refusals, and execution outcomes `am-rt-typed-results-mqb`; worker transport `am-rt-worker-protocol-gaq` and `am-rt-worker-scheduler-7tl`; buffer lifetimes and recovery `am-rt-memory-lifecycle-5ws`; execution labels `am-rt-determinism-fallbacks-8i4`; tapes `am-rt-control-tapes-0gc`; browser lanes ``am-rt-browser-conformance-09i5``.

## Requirements

1. **Instances and placements.** Every mounted laboratory belongs to exactly one instance with a unique `instanceId` (format `<experimentId>:<page-scoped monotone counter>`, assigned by the registry; never random, never persisted in permalinks). Instances are registered under a stable placement key `<route path>#<anchor>/<experimentId>/<slot>`. Two placements of the same experiment on one page (different slots) are independent instances whose controls, runs, seeds, and snapshots never leak. A remount of the same placement while its route segment stays mounted reattaches to the existing instance.
2. **Identity set.** Fields and where they live:

| Field | Meaning | Lives in |
|---|---|---|
| `instanceId` | This laboratory instance, independent of other copies | snapshot and view |
| `runId`, `parentRunId` | This experiment realization; the run it forked from, if any | snapshot |
| `actionIndex` / `acceptedActionIndex` | Newest command issued / newest command reflected in the accepted snapshot (logical order, never wall-clock or UI ticks) | requested state / snapshot |
| `inputRevision` / `acceptedInputRevision` | Latest requested physical input set (setup and intervention commands) / the set that produced the displayed result | requested state / snapshot |
| `observerRevision`, `measurementRevision`, `estimatorRevision` | Requested and accepted counters for descriptions, observations, and estimators | requested state / snapshot |
| `stepIndex` | Accepted logical solver or sample step, never a UI event count (0 for closed-form evaluations) | snapshot |
| `simulatedTime` | Canonical SI time of the accepted state, or the tagged `{ kind: "not-time-evolving" }` marker for closed-form evaluations, never a stand-in 0 | snapshot |
| `snapshotVersion` | Monotone publication identity per instance; never reset when a new run starts | snapshot |
| `renderTime` | Display or interpolation time; never a hidden physical input | per-view frame record |
| `modelVersion` / `artifactDigest` | Mathematical implementation and exact executable identity (WASM digest or evaluator source hash) | snapshot |
| `seed` / `streamVersion` | Stochastic realization as a canonical unsigned 64-bit decimal string (grammar owned by `am-rt-u64-identities-7ce`; the store never parses or rounds it) and random-stream semantics version | snapshot |
| `constantSetId`, `provenance` | Constant set used; owner kind and capability or evaluator id | snapshot |

3. **Immutability.** A published snapshot never changes. In development and test builds the envelope is deep-frozen and mutation throws. Typed arrays cannot be frozen, so large arrays are exposed through read-only accessor objects (no index assignment, no access to the underlying `ArrayBuffer`) whose lifetime rules come from `am-rt-memory-lifecycle-5ws`. Production builds skip freezing for speed; the test suites always run with freezing enabled.
4. **Publication ordering.** Within the instance's current run, the publication key `(acceptedActionIndex, stepIndex)` must be strictly greater, lexicographically, than the key of the currently published snapshot, and `snapshotVersion` must be strictly greater. A snapshot whose `runId` is not the instance's current run is refused. Refusals carry a reason (`stale-action`, `superseded-run`, `non-monotone-step`, `mixed-revisions`) and are logged; they never throw into React. Progress snapshots of one long run keep `acceptedActionIndex` and advance `stepIndex`.
5. **No mixed revisions.** A publication is built from one decoded response. Merging outputs from an earlier snapshot is allowed only when the experiment manifest declares partial results and every merged output carries the same accepted revision tuple; otherwise it is refused as `mixed-revisions`.
6. **Read model.** `ExperimentView = { snapshot, requested, state, refusal?, outcome? }` where `requested` holds `actionIndex` and the four requested revision counters, and `state` is `current`, `pending` (a newer request exists), `refused` (the newest request was refused; the snapshot is the last legal state), `paused`, or `unavailable`. Views can say "these settings have not produced a result yet" or "this request was refused; the display still shows the last accepted state." Old numbers are never shown beneath new labels as if freshly computed. The view object is cached and replaced only when one of its parts changes.
7. **React integration.** `useExperimentView(instance, selector?)` and `useExperimentSnapshot(instance)` wrap `useSyncExternalStore`. `getSnapshot` returns the identical cached reference until a publication or requested-state change; manufacturing a new object from the same state on every call is a bug (render loops and tearing). Selectors are memoized by `snapshotVersion` and requested counters. `getServerSnapshot` returns the state that renders the same markup as the static HTML (the authored static worked example or a not-started state), so hydration never mismatches and the no-JavaScript page stays complete.
8. **Owner lifecycle.** React StrictMode double effects, repeated subscriptions, and remounts are normal. They never create duplicate stepping owners, leak workers, or advance randomness. Mounting a second view subscribes to the existing instance through an `ExperimentInstanceProvider`. Release is reference-counted with a deferred release scheduled through an injected scheduler (deterministic in tests), and a placement is released when its route segment unmounts.
9. **No physics in components.** No `.tsx` module anywhere, and no module under `src/visuals/`, `src/reader/`, `src/equations/`, or `src/app/`, may import `src/physics/reference/**`, `src/workers/wasm/**`, or generated WASM glue under `public/wasm/**`. Components read views and dispatch typed commands only. An import-graph test enforces this with a planted violation fixture.
10. **Render time.** Each view keeps a frame record `{ snapshotVersion, renderTime }`. Interpolation uses `renderTime`; it never feeds the physical state, and rendering cadence never changes `stepIndex`, `simulatedTime`, or draws.
11. **Verification hooks.** Every view root exposes `data-instance-id`, `data-run-id`, `data-snapshot-version`, `data-accepted-action-index`, `data-accepted-input-revision`, `data-input-revision`, and `data-view-state`. Test builds (never production, verified by a bundle check) expose diagnostics counters: owners per instance, subscriptions per instance, and per-stream draw counters supplied by owners.

## Technical Approach

- Planned files: `src/experiments/store/snapshot.ts` (types, identity set, freeze helpers, read-only array accessors), `src/experiments/store/instanceStore.ts` (`createExperimentStore`: publish with ordering checks, requested state, subscribe, `getSnapshot`, `getServerSnapshot`), `src/experiments/store/registry.ts` (placement-keyed registry, reference counts, deferred release), `src/experiments/store/useExperimentSnapshot.ts` (both hooks and the provider), `src/experiments/store/frame.ts`, `src/experiments/store/noPhysicsInComponents.test.ts`.
- The snapshot payload type is generic over the experiment's typed outputs; `am-rt-typed-results-mqb` supplies the status union that payloads use.
- Runtime fixtures: `src/testing/runtime-fixtures/fixtureAnalytic.ts`, a small closed-form experiment (a linear response $y = kx$ on a declared grid with one control and two outputs) with a real evaluator, never shown to readers and excluded from production bundles. Later runtime beads add more fixtures in the same directory.
- `scripts/e2e-runtime-contracts.ts`: a Bun runner that executes registered runtime contract suites against real Bun `Worker` instances and writes JSONL; this bead registers the `store` suite.
- Reuse the extracted donor `tickScheduler.ts` only for host-fed frame time. Do not port the module-global maps.
- Use the DOM test environment chosen by `am-gov-decision-stack-versions-6ax` (for example happy-dom registered in Bun's test preload) with the real store, never a mock of it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Two placements of the same experiment on one page run, change, and publish independently.
- [ ] A remount of the same placement (face switch simulation) reattaches: same `instanceId`, same `runId`, continuing `stepIndex`, zero extra draws.
- [ ] `getSnapshot` returns the same reference across repeated calls between changes (asserted by reference equality and render counts).
- [ ] Server-rendered HTML and hydrated output match with no hydration warning.
- [ ] Under StrictMode double mounting, exactly one owner exists and zero extra random draws occur.
- [ ] `snapshotVersion` is strictly monotone per instance and is not reset by a new run; publications with a stale action, a superseded run, a non-monotone step, or mixed revisions are refused with their reason and logged.
- [ ] An out-of-order observer-change response (older `actionIndex`, same `runId` and `inputRevision`) is refused as `stale-action`.
- [ ] Requested, accepted, pending, refused, paused, and unavailable states are distinguishable in the API and in a rendered status line.
- [ ] Mutating a published snapshot or writing through an array accessor throws in development and fails tests.
- [ ] The import-graph test fails on the planted violation and passes on the real tree.
- [ ] `bun scripts/e2e-runtime-contracts.ts --suite store` passes and writes JSONL evidence.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `instanceStore.test.ts`: publication ordering over a table of `(runId, acceptedActionIndex, stepIndex, snapshotVersion)` cases including equal keys, a progress snapshot, a new run with continuing `snapshotVersion`, a superseded run, and `mixed-revisions`; requested-versus-accepted separation; freeze enforcement on envelopes and array accessors.
- `staleDescriptions.test.ts`: issue observer changes with `actionIndex` 5 (v = 0.6c) and 6 (v = 0.8c) against the fixture; publish the response for 6 first; the response for 5 is refused and the view still shows 0.8c values under the 0.8c request.
- `registry.test.ts`: remount reattachment within a route; distinct slots yield distinct instances; route-segment unmount releases the placement after the injected deferred release; no timers from the real clock.
- `useExperimentSnapshot.test.tsx` (StrictMode, real store): reference stability, render counts, two independent placements, second view reuses one owner, no additional draws (the fixture owner counts draws; no mock of the store).
- `hydration.test.tsx`: server snapshot markup equals the client's first render.
- `noPhysicsInComponents.test.ts`: import graph over all `.tsx` files and the listed directories, with a planted violation in a test fixture directory.

### End-to-end tests
- `bun scripts/e2e-runtime-contracts.ts --suite store`: a real Bun `Worker` evaluates `fixtureAnalytic` and returns responses in a scripted out-of-order sequence; the runner asserts accepted and refused publications, view states, and identity fields at every step.
- Browser lanes (implemented by ``am-rt-browser-conformance-09i5`` against the fixture page, using this bead's data attributes): two placements on one page are independent; a `?view=` face switch during a running fixture keeps `data-run-id` and continues stepping with one owner; identical `data-snapshot-version` on the plot, equation, and table of one instance.
- Obligations re-asserted on real instruments by `am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu`: two BM-01 instances, face switch during a running ensemble, identical snapshot versions across BM-01 views.

### Structured logging
Through the logger from `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`, suite `runtime-store`, file `artifacts/test-logs/runtime-store/<log-run-id>.jsonl`: `timestamp`, `suite`, `testId`, `beadId` (`am-rt-snapshot-store-aft`), `instanceId`, `logRunId`, `runId`, `inputRevision`, `acceptedInputRevision`, `snapshotVersion`, `seed`, `streamVersion`, `expected`, `actual`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `message`, and in `extra`: `placementKey`, `actionIndex`, `acceptedActionIndex`, `stepIndex`, `viewState`, `publicationRefusal`, `ownersForInstance`, `drawCounterDelta`. Browser failures in the conformance lanes retain a screenshot, trace, DOM snapshot, and console log.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Returning a fresh object from `getSnapshot` causes infinite loops under React's concurrent rendering; cache per change.
- Deep-freezing typed arrays is impossible; freeze the envelope and expose arrays through accessors with lifetime rules from `am-rt-memory-lifecycle-5ws`.
- A server snapshot that renders different markup from the client breaks the static-first, no-JavaScript reading guarantee.
- Do not let a requested value leak into views as if accepted; that is exactly the donor failure mode this bead removes.
- A placement registry keyed by placement is allowed; a registry keyed only by experiment id is the donor bug in a new file.
- Never order publications by wall-clock time or `Date.now()`; worker scheduling must not change which result is shown.
- Keep the API minimal until `am-bm-slice-retrospective-pp09`; it must still implement every identity field now.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-scaf-nextjs-app-bu2`: the application, strict TypeScript, and Bun test runner.
- `am-scaf-extract-runtime-utilities-99y`: extracted donor transport, tick scheduler, and tape utilities that the store integrates with.
- `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`: the JSONL logger every suite here uses.

Unblocks:
- `am-rt-typed-results-mqb`, `am-rt-command-classes-dzp`, `am-rt-determinism-fallbacks-8i4`: they define statuses, commands, and labels over this store.
- `am-inst-registry-dispatcher-66l0`: instruments are instantiated as store instances.
- `am-eq-live-bindings-2se` and `am-read-result-weave-jex`: live equation values and sentence highlighting read accepted snapshots.
- `am-a11y-graph-descriptions-vxe1`: accessible summaries describe the same snapshot the graph shows.
- ``am-rt-browser-conformance-09i5`` (through the scheduler chain): browser lanes use this bead's data attributes and diagnostics.

title: Implement typed result statuses, execution outcomes, and reader-facing explanations
description:
# Implement typed result statuses, execution outcomes, and reader-facing explanations

**Epic:** `am-ep-runtime-iml` · **Batch:** A · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §10.6, §11.4 "Typed results beyond numbers", §12.7, §13.4 (uncertainty kinds), §8.1–8.4 examples (traceability only)

## Background

A scientific result is not always a number. A diffusion measurement cannot separately identify particle radius and molecular number. The mass–energy ledger knows a change in body energy without knowing an absolute zero. A Wien-only entropy comparison has no meaning in dense radiation. At $t = 0$ a localized particle has a point distribution, not an infinitely tall bar. Below threshold there is no stopping potential because no electron is emitted.

Rendering those states as `NaN`, infinity, zero, a clamped slider, or a red error toast would teach false physics. The plan requires every output to carry a status and keeps model refusals separate from software failures: a model refusal is not a numerical zero, and a budget refusal is not a physical impossibility.

Three different things are easy to blur, and this bead keeps them apart:

- an **output status** inside an accepted snapshot (the request was evaluated; one output is a limit, undefined, underdetermined, or outside its domain while others may be values);
- a **request refusal** (the requested settings cannot be evaluated at all; the display keeps the last legal state and names the refused request, "a refusal is a museum label");
- an **execution outcome** (software, budget, or environment events such as a crashed worker or a missing artifact; never a statement about physics).

Refusals also differ in kind. $|v| \ge c$ has no inertial observer (physical); a Wien-only formula in dense radiation is an approximation outside its validity (model); an explicit FTCS step with $D\,dt/dx^2 > 1/2$ is unstable (numerical, a property of the scheme and not of diffusion); a seed with a leading zero is malformed (input). Reader explanations must never turn a numerical or input refusal into a claim about nature.

## Scope

In scope: the output status union and payloads; the request refusal shape, domain kinds, and the refusal-code registry; execution outcomes; partial-result rules; uncertainty kinds; encoding and strict decoding; the explanation registry; small presentational components that render statuses in ordinary language; typed example fixtures later beads import.

Out of scope (owned elsewhere): protocol framing `am-rt-worker-protocol-gaq`; precision and interval formatting `am-ver-precision-display-5e5`; per-instrument authored explanation text (each instrument bead); compiler checks that explanations exist (`am-cm-checks-epistemic-o7n`); the live-region policy (`am-a11y-graph-descriptions-vxe1`).

## Requirements

1. **Output statuses.**

| Status | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | A finite result with units, semantic kind, owner, and uncertainty metadata where applicable | An admitted diffusion coefficient |
| `symbolic` | A relation whose unspecified symbols remain explicit | An absolute internal energy in the historical ledger |
| `analytic-limit` | A defined limit with its own representation | The point distribution at $t = 0$; the mass coefficient at $v = 0$ |
| `underdetermined` | The admitted information does not select a unique value | Radius and molecular number from diffusivity alone |
| `not-applicable` | The quantity is not defined for this model and question | A stopping potential when no electron is emitted |
| `outside-domain` | The model does not support the requested conditions for this output | A Wien-only entropy comparison in a dense state |

2. **Output payloads.**
   - `value`: finite number or typed array; canonical quantity id; canonical SI unit; semantic kind (density or total, angular or cyclic, coordinate or proper, laboratory or comoving, measured or latent); owner id (reference evaluator function or FrankenSim capability); optional uncertainty metadata whose kind is always named (requirement 6).
   - `symbolic`: an expression-tree reference plus the list of unspecified symbols (for example $E_0$, $E_1$, $H_0$, $H_1$).
   - `analytic-limit`: a description of the limit and its own representation (a point mass at $x_0$ with interval probability 1 when the closed interval contains $x_0$ and 0 otherwise; the coefficient $L/c^2$ at $v = 0$).
   - `underdetermined`: the family of compatible values (for example the one-parameter family with $a\,N_A = RT/(6\pi\eta D)$ fixed at constant $R$, $T$, $\eta$) and the additional information that would select a value.
   - `not-applicable`: why the quantity is undefined for this question.
   - `outside-domain`: the violated condition, `domainKind` (`physical`, `model`, `numerical`, or `input`), a readable reason, and the nearest admissible boundary or an alternative model.
3. **Request refusals.** `RequestRefusal = { code, domainKind, affected: { parameterIds?, capabilityId? }, message, rankedRepairs: [{ label, action? }], details? }`, where an `action` names a parameter and an admissible value. The store keeps the last accepted snapshot and records the refusal against the requested settings. Choose between a refusal and an output status by one rule: if the request cannot be evaluated at all it is refused; if it is evaluated and some outputs are not values, those outputs carry statuses. Each experiment manifest declares which applies to each condition.
4. **Refusal-code registry** (`src/experiments/results/refusalCodes.ts`, the single source that the protocol, WASM mapping, and TypeScript evaluators import). Initial codes, each with a domain kind, generic reader text, and a repair template: `ftcs-unstable` (numerical; `details: { ratio, limit: 0.5, dtMax }`), `off-replay-grid` (numerical), `superluminal-observer` (physical), `outside-wien-domain` (model), `stokes-gas-medium` (model; Stokes drag without the Cunningham slip correction is invalid when the mean free path is comparable to the radius), `invalid-seed` (input), `nonfinite-input` (input), `unsupported-kernel` (input). Codes are stable: they become explanation keys and fixture ids. A new code requires reader text before registration succeeds.
5. **Execution outcomes** are a separate type, never mapped to a physical status: `transport-error`, `protocol-mismatch`, `malformed-response`, `budget-exhausted` (with requested and allowed work units), `cancelled`, `superseded`, `missing-artifact`, `artifact-mismatch`, `environment-unsupported` (no `Worker` or no `WebAssembly`), `worker-crashed`, `context-lost`, `invariant-violation`. Each carries retry guidance (`retry-same-request`, `new-run`, `reload`, or `none`) and reader text in software language.
6. **Uncertainty kinds** (the shared enum that `am-ver-precision-display-5e5` renders): `statistical-interval` (coverage, sample size, method), `enclosure` (interval-arithmetic method), `numerical-error-estimate` (method; bound or estimate), `input-precision` (source), `measurement-uncertainty` (dataset id and uncertainty type). A confidence interval is never an enclosure, and a numerical error bar is never a measurement uncertainty.
7. **Partial results.** A snapshot may contain valid outputs beside honestly unknown ones only if the experiment manifest declares that its model permits partial results. Each output is individually statused. All outputs in one snapshot share its accepted revision tuple; mixing quantities from different requests to fill gaps is refused.
8. **Encoding.** Results are tagged JSON objects (`{"status": "value", ...}`) with typed-array bodies referencing protocol buffer layouts. Decoding refuses nonfinite numbers in value fields, unlabeled uncertainty, unknown statuses, and a zero-length array without a status. There is no status for "error"; errors are execution outcomes.
9. **Reader-facing language.** Status, refusal, and outcome identifiers never appear in the reader's view. An explanation registry maps each status (generic text), each refusal code, each outcome, and each experiment output (authored text supplied by instrument beads) to an ordinary-language sentence and a next action ("choose a radius to see a narrow interval," "move toward lower density," "raise the frequency above threshold," "use a time step of at most 0.0116 s"). Missing authored text falls back to generic text and is reported by the content audit. Numerical and input refusals and every execution outcome are worded without physical claims (no "impossible," "nature," or "forbidden").
10. **Accessibility.** Status notes are announced when a committed comparison changes, never on every animation frame, following the live-region policy of `am-a11y-graph-descriptions-vxe1`.

## Technical Approach

- Planned files: `src/experiments/results/types.ts` (statuses, payloads, uncertainty kinds), `src/experiments/results/refusals.ts` (request refusal shape) and `refusalCodes.ts` (registry), `src/experiments/results/outcomes.ts`, `src/experiments/results/codec.ts` (encode and strict decode), `src/experiments/results/explanations.ts` (registry and lookup), `src/experiments/results/ResultStatusNote.tsx` and `ResultValue.tsx` (presentational only; formatting delegated to `am-ver-precision-display-5e5`), `src/experiments/results/__fixtures__/planExamples.ts`.
- Status payload schemas are shared with `am-cm-schemas-experiment-fuu` so manifests declare which statuses each output may take and which conditions are refusals.
- `planExamples.ts` exports typed payloads for every plan example; evaluator beads (`am-ref-diffusion-lr3`, `am-ref-inference-2w9`, `am-ref-mass-energy-ht0`, `am-ref-radiation-15c`, `am-ref-photoelectric-q6r`) import them in their own tests to prove their outputs conform.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All six statuses, the request refusal shape, the refusal-code registry, all execution outcomes, and the uncertainty kinds exist as typed unions with the payloads above.
- [ ] Each plan example is representable and round-trips through the codec: BM-07 underdetermined radius and $N_A$; ME-01 symbolic absolute energy; LQ-04 outside-domain dense radiation; BM-06 analytic-limit at $t = 0$ with interval probabilities; LQ-08 not-applicable stopping potential below threshold; ME-02 analytic-limit coefficient at $v = 0$.
- [ ] Refusal fixtures round-trip: `ftcs-unstable` at ratio 0.5000001 with its `dtMax` repair; `superluminal-observer` at $v/c = 1$; `invalid-seed` for the input `01`.
- [ ] Decoding refuses `NaN`, `Infinity`, and `-Infinity` in value fields, unlabeled uncertainty, zero-length arrays without status, and a snapshot whose outputs carry mixed revisions.
- [ ] A partial result is accepted only when the manifest permits it.
- [ ] No rendered string contains a raw status, refusal code, or outcome identifier (component test over every member).
- [ ] Every status, refusal code, and outcome has generic reader text and a next action; numerical and input refusals and outcomes contain no physical-impossibility wording (asserted by a word list).
- [ ] `bun scripts/e2e-runtime-contracts.ts --suite results` passes and writes JSONL evidence.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
- `results.codec.test.ts`: round trips for every status, refusal, and outcome; rejection corpus (nonfinite values, missing quantity id, unlabeled uncertainty, mixed revisions, unknown status, zero-length array without status).
- `results.partial.test.ts`: manifest-permitted versus forbidden partial results.
- `results.refusalCodes.test.ts`: codes unique and stable; every code has domain kind, text, and repair template; registering a code without text fails.
- `results.explanations.test.tsx`: every member renders ordinary language with a next action and no identifier leakage; the no-physical-wording check for numerical, input, and outcome texts.
- `results.examples.test.ts`: the plan examples and refusal fixtures from `planExamples.ts` validate against the schemas.
- `results.uncertainty.test.ts`: each uncertainty kind requires its fields; an interval declared as `statistical-interval` cannot carry an enclosure method.

### End-to-end tests
- `bun scripts/e2e-runtime-contracts.ts --suite results`: every fixture crosses a real Bun `Worker` boundary by structured clone, is decoded strictly, and is rendered to static HTML with React server rendering; the runner asserts identity-free text and logs each case.
- Browser lanes (implemented by ``am-rt-browser-conformance-09i5``): a forced missing artifact shows an execution-outcome note distinct from any physical status; a refused request keeps the last accepted state with the refusal named against the requested settings.
- Obligations re-asserted on real instruments: BM-06 at $t = 0$ shows the point-distribution explanation, and an FTCS ratio above 0.5 shows the typed refusal while keeping the last legal state (`am-bm-06-gaussian-spread-982y`, `am-bm-slice-e2e-sbqu`).

### Structured logging
Through the shared logger, suite `runtime-results`, file `artifacts/test-logs/runtime-results/<log-run-id>.jsonl`: `timestamp`, `suite`, `testId`, `beadId` (`am-rt-typed-results-mqb`), `resultStatus`, `acceptedInputRevision`, `expected`, `actual`, `outcome`, `message`, and in `extra`: `refusalCode`, `domainKind`, `executionOutcome`, `quantityId`, `uncertaintyKind`, `renderedText`.

## Considerations and Pitfalls
