- `src/equations/colorPalette.test.ts`: every palette color used for text meets WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1 for body text) against the three planned theme backgrounds (values from `am-design-themes-typography-288q` when available; donor backgrounds until then).
- `src/equations/valueFormatting.test.ts`: donor cases ported.
- `src/testing/legacyImportBoundary.test.ts`: scans import graphs under `src/app` and `src/reader` for `equations/legacy`.
- `src/search/CommandPalette.test.tsx` (pure keyboard handler tests): ⌘K and Ctrl+K open; the shortcut inside a focused text input does nothing; Escape closes and returns the recorded focus target.
- `src/testing/thirdPartyRequests.test.ts`: scans `src/` and `public/` source text for request-initiating references to other origins (`<script src>`, `<link rel="stylesheet" href>`, `@import url(`, `fetch(` with an absolute URL, remote font loaders, analytics package imports) and for every forbidden donor identity; plain anchor `href` values are allowed. A fixture string with an analytics script tag fails; a fixture with a plain repository hyperlink passes.
### End-to-end tests
Through `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh` against the production build of the empty site, in Chromium and WebKit: the theme toggle switches and persists across reload; ⌘K or Ctrl+K opens the palette and Escape closes it with focus restored; a nonexistent route shows the not-found page with status 404; the Open Graph image route returns an image with the expected content type; the network log of the home page contains no request to another origin.
### Structured logging
Adopt the JSONL library from `am-test-logging-standard-l3cp`: `suite` (`ui-extraction`), `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId`, `outcome`, and for scans the offending `path`, `line`, and `origin`; browser checks add `browser`, `viewport`, `jsEnabled`, and evidence paths on failure.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Do not "fix" the legacy equation's lookup seams here; the refactor has its own bead and tests.
- The facsimile viewer must only ever load assets admitted for redistribution; the rights check lives in the source beads.
- Keep the chrome restrained; visual identity comes from `am-design-themes-typography-288q`.
- Open Graph routes in many projects fetch fonts from a CDN at render time; that is a third-party request and fails the scan.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-scaf-nextjs-app-bu2` (layout, build, and the initial-route graph check), `am-gov-donor-audit-0wa` (pinned revision, verified paths, header template, identity list, third-party request findings); proposed in review: `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh` (the browser checks run through the harness instead of a throwaway script).

Unblocks: `am-eq-static-katex-7da` (adapts the renderer), `am-read-facsimile-face-er0` (uses the facsimile viewer), `am-inst-three-studio-y0y0` (adapts the studio scene), `am-plat-search-index-snx1` (fills the palette's index).

title: Wire the local and CI quality gate chain
description:
# Wire the local and CI quality gate chain

**Epic:** `am-ep-scaffold-5wh` · **Batch:** A · **Priority:** P0 · **Plan sections:** §17.1, §17.3, §17.7 item 9, §18.3 (traceability only)

## Background

The per-paper definition of done requires `verify-content`, typecheck, lint, format, build, `ubs --diff`, the WASM artifact test, and the Playwright vertical slice to be green (§17.7 item 9), and the release workflow runs the quality gates before deploying anything (§18.3). Those gates must exist as one ordered, reproducible chain that every agent runs the same way locally, that GitHub Actions runs on every push and pull request, and that the release script runs for each publication profile. If the release script kept its own list of gate commands, the two lists would drift; so this bead builds **one typed gate registry**, and every consumer (local runs, CI, the release profiles) selects steps from it.

Two principles from AGENTS.md shape the chain. First, **never weaken a gate** to get green: no skipped lanes, loosened tolerances, deleted evidence, or reruns of flaky statistical tests. Second, **a command that does not exist yet is never reported as passing**; the chain shows it as `not-available` until the bead that creates it registers it, and a release profile that requires it refuses. And CI never deploys: releases go only through the verified prebuilt workflow (`am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt`).

## Scope

In scope: the gate registry, the runner script, the `gates` package script, release-profile selection and refusal, the GitHub Actions workflow for the fast chain, log retention, and tests.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere: the individual gates' implementations (architecture `am-scaf-architecture-gate-l1p`, content `am-cm-audit-scripts-d34`, WASM `am-fs-slim-artifact-0yh`, voice `am-edit-voice-lint-trmf`, license inventory ``am-gov-license-inventory-w6yz``, scenarios `am-ver-scenario-registry-om3`, browser `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`, performance `am-plat-perf-budgets-s3ww`); the browser-acceptance workflow file (`.github/workflows/browser-acceptance.yml`, owned by `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`); deployment (`am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt`).

## Requirements

1. **Registry** `scripts/quality-gates/registry.ts`: a typed list of `GateStep` entries with `id`, `title`, `command` (argument array), `family` (`fast`, `browser`, or `perf`), `requiredInCi` (boolean), `requiredInProfiles` (a subset of `scaffold`, `preview`, `launch`), `availability` (a script path that must exist or a tool that must be on `PATH`), and `owner` (the bead id that registered the step). Registry validation rejects duplicate ids, unknown profiles, and steps without an owner.
2. **Initial steps, in order:** `architecture` (`bun scripts/app-router-architecture.ts`), `typecheck`, `lint` (`biome check`), `format-check`, `unit-tests` (`bun run test`), `ubs-diff` (`ubs --diff`), `ubs-staged` (`ubs --staged`), `build` (last among the fast steps). All are required in the `scaffold`, `preview`, and `launch` profiles; all except the two `ubs` steps are required in CI.
3. **Later registrations** (each by its owning bead, in the same change that creates the command): `verify-content` (`am-cm-audit-scripts-d34`), `verify-wasm-artifacts` (`am-fs-slim-artifact-0yh`), `voice-lint` (`am-edit-voice-lint-trmf`, until `verify-content` absorbs it), `license-inventory` (``am-gov-license-inventory-w6yz``), `scenarios` (`am-ver-scenario-registry-om3`), `publication-contract` (a fast `bun test` subset of the edition, dispatcher, architecture, and determinism tests, registered by `am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt` and ordered first so release refusals come early), `browser-acceptance` (`am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh`, family `browser`), and `perf-budgets` (`am-plat-perf-budgets-s3ww`, family `perf`). Each later step is required in CI and in the `preview` and `launch` profiles unless its owner records a reason otherwise.
4. **Runner** `scripts/quality-gates.ts`, with modes:
   - `--fail-fast` (local default): run available steps of the selected families in registry order, stopping at the first failure;
   - `--all` (CI): run every step of the selected families and summarize;
   - `--profile <scaffold|preview|launch>` (used by the release script): run exactly the steps required in that profile, fail-fast; any required step whose availability check fails is `refused`, and the run exits with code 2 before running anything;
   - `--family <fast|browser|perf>` and `--only <ids>` filters.
5. **Outcomes:** `passed`, `failed`, `not-available` (the step's script is absent), `skipped` with a reason (`tool-unavailable` for an absent tool in a mode where the step is not required, or `not-required-in-ci`), and `refused` (profile mode only). `not-available` and `skipped` are never counted as passing. Exit codes: 0 when every required step passed, 1 on any failure, 2 on refusal.
6. **Package script:** `bun run gates` runs `bun scripts/quality-gates.ts --fail-fast --family fast`.
7. **GitHub Actions** (`.github/workflows/quality-gates.yml`): triggers on push and pull request to `main` (never `pull_request_target`); `permissions: contents: read`; checkout pinned by commit SHA with `persist-credentials: false`; the Bun version read from `package.json` `packageManager` and the Node.js version from `engines.node`; `bun install --frozen-lockfile`; `bun scripts/quality-gates.ts --all --family fast`; uploads `artifacts/test-logs/` as a workflow artifact on failure; all third-party actions pinned by commit SHA; a concurrency group cancels superseded runs on the same ref; no secrets; **no deployment, alias, or DNS step of any kind**.

## Technical Approach

The runner spawns each command, streams output, measures duration, records an outcome per step, and exits with the codes above. It writes a summary table to stdout and JSON lines to the logs directory. Registry entries are plain data plus an availability probe, so the runner's tests can pass fixture registries whose commands are real processes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `bun run gates` passes locally on the empty-corpus scaffold.
- [ ] `bun scripts/quality-gates.ts --profile scaffold` passes locally when `ubs` is installed, and exits with code 2 naming the missing tool when it is not.
- [ ] The workflow passes on `main` and fails the job when any required step fails, with logs uploaded.
- [ ] Not-yet-available steps are reported as such and never counted as passing.
- [ ] The workflow contains no deploy, alias, or DNS command and requests only read permission.
- [ ] README.md and AGENTS.md reference `bun run gates` and the profile flag consistently.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests
`scripts/quality-gates.test.ts` runs the real runner with small fixture registries whose commands are real processes:
- a step running `bun -e "process.exit(0)"` passes; a step running `bun -e "process.exit(3)"` fails and stops the chain in fail-fast mode;
- in `--all` mode later steps still run and the exit code is 1;
- a step whose script path does not exist reports `not-available` in `--all` mode and is not counted as passing;
- in `--profile preview` mode, a required step whose script is absent produces `refused`, exit code 2, and no step runs;
- a required tool absent from `PATH` is `skipped: tool-unavailable` in `--all` mode when not required in CI, and `refused` in profile mode;
- registry validation rejects a duplicate id, an unknown profile name, and a step without an owner;
- the JSONL output contains one line per step with the fields below plus a summary line.
`scripts/quality-gates/workflowScan.test.ts`: reads every file in `.github/workflows/` and fails on `vercel`, `deploy`, `alias`, `wrangler`, `cloudflare`, `pull_request_target`, or a `permissions` block granting write access; a fixture workflow containing `vercel deploy` fails.
### End-to-end tests
The CI workflow itself on a pull request; a deliberately failing fixture step in the test suite (never in the real registry) proves failure propagation.
### Structured logging
One JSON line per step `{timestamp, suite: "quality-gates", logRunId, mode, profile, stepId, owner, command, outcome, reason, exitCode, durationMs, message}` to `artifacts/test-logs/quality-gates/<log-run-id>.jsonl`, plus a summary line with counts per outcome.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Browser and performance families are slow; they run in separate workflow jobs owned by their beads, but they are never dropped from the definition of done or from the `preview` and `launch` profiles.
- Keep the build step last among the fast gates so earlier failures surface quickly.
- CI minutes must not become a reason to skip gates; if the chain is slow, profile it.
- A release profile's step list only grows; removing a step from a profile requires a recorded decision.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `am-scaf-architecture-gate-l1p` (the first step of the chain).

Unblocks: `am-rel-verified-deploy-qndt` (the release script runs this registry in profile mode before building a candidate), `am-edit-voice-lint-trmf` and `am-cm-audit-scripts-d34` (register their steps); proposed in review: `am-test-e2e-harness-bqmh` and ``am-gov-license-inventory-w6yz`` (register their steps).

title: Build SR-01 clock synchronization with the event ledger
description:
# Build SR-01 clock synchronization with the event ledger

**Epic:** `am-ep-relativity-kinematics-q2g` · **Batch:** batch-e · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §3.5 §1, §7.2, §8.3, §9.4, §10.1-10.7, §12.6, §13.2 (traceability only)

## Background

The relativity paper opens its kinematics with a question a careful person can actually answer: how will you assign a time to an event that happens elsewhere? SR-01 makes the procedure concrete. Its primary view is an **event ledger** of emissions, reflections, and receptions at named clocks; a spatial scene supports it without implying that what a distant camera sees equals a simultaneous coordinate measurement. The instrument applies Einstein's criterion $t_B - t_A = t'_A - t_B$ explicitly, keeps an event distinct from its reception in every view, runs the same procedure on the ends of a moving rod (§2's chase), and then shows that a pair of clocks synchronized in its own frame and moving at $v$ is judged out of step by $vL/c^2$ (for proper separation $L$) in the platform frame. It is also the destination of the no-algebra first encounter, the "make a measurement procedure" stage of Journey III, and the fifteen-minute tour, so its named presets are part of its contract.

## Scope

In scope: the SR-01 manifest, controls, typed outputs, views, caption readings, named preset scenarios, weave predicate records, action contract, predict mode, show-the-code, tape identity, permalink, embeddable flag, and tests.

Out of scope: the evaluator (`am-ref-events-yvl`); rod measurements (`am-sr-03-rod-simultaneity-0l5i`); the no-algebra entrance (`am-srk-first-encounter-471z`); Journey III narration (`am-disc-journey-iii-chain-hpr7`); the `/embed/lab/[experiment]` route itself (`am-inst-embed-route-rnyg`, Batch H).

## Requirements

**Explanatory question.** How can distant clocks acquire an operational common time, and do moving clocks share it?

**Linked source and argument ids.** §1 (definition of simultaneity, the criterion, $2\overline{AB}/(t'_A - t_A) = V$); §2 (clocks at the ends of a moving rod and the chase); Journey III stage "make a measurement procedure."

### Controls

| Control | Dimension | Display unit | Model domain | Numerical domain | Default | Mapping | Class |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Clock separation (stations A, B) | length | light-seconds (km toggle) | $> 0$ | $10^{-6}$ to $10^{6}$ ls | 10 ls | logarithmic | setup-change |
| Initial clock offsets | time | s | any finite | $\pm10^{6}$ s | 0 | linear, typed entry | setup-change |
| Signal emission time at A | time | s | finite, after run start | $0$ to $10^{6}$ s | 0 | typed | physical-intervention |
| Station motion (§2 mode: A and B as rod ends moving in the stationary frame) | velocity | fraction of $c$ | $\lvert u\rvert < c$ | $\lvert u\rvert \le 0.95c$ | 0 | linear | setup-change |
| Moving clock pair velocity | velocity | fraction of $c$ | $\lvert u\rvert < c$ | $\lvert u\rvert \le 0.95c$ | $0.6c$ | linear | setup-change |
| Moving pair proper separation $L$ | length | ls | $> 0$ | as above | 10 ls | logarithmic | setup-change |
| Frame of description | velocity | fraction of $c$ | $\lvert v\rvert < c$ | $\lvert v\rvert \le 0.95c$ | 0 | linear | observer-change |

Typed entry sits beside every slider; out-of-domain entries explain the problem and offer the admissible boundary; nothing is silently clamped.

### Derived outputs (all from one accepted snapshot)

- Ledger rows: event id, kind (emission, reflection, reception), clock, the clock's own reading at the event (invariant under a change of description), coordinates in the chosen frame, and the reception event linked to each remote event. Receptions are separate rows.
- Criterion check per clock pair: `value` offset $t_B - t_A - (t'_A - t_B)$, or "synchronized by definition" when zero within the declared absolute tolerance.
- Assigned remote time by the equal-travel-time rule, labeled "stated procedure."
- Round-trip speed $2\overline{AB}/(t'_A - t_A)$: `value` equal to $c$ in the frame where the procedure is applied.
- §2 chase legs for moving rod ends: $t_B - t_A = r_{AB}/(c - u)$ and $t'_A - t_B = r_{AB}/(c + u)$ in the stationary frame (from `movingRodLegs`), with the criterion's failure for observers moving with the rod stated.
- Desynchronization of the moving pair as judged in the platform frame: `value` $vL/c^2$ with the trailing clock ahead.
- One-way light speed: `not-applicable` with the explanation that the model defines it by convention.
- $\lvert v\rvert \ge c$ or $\lvert u\rvert \ge c$: `outside-domain` ("no inertial observer moves at or above light speed"); nonfinite or nonpositive separation: input refusal with the reason and the admissible boundary.

### Model assumptions and admitted domain

Inertial frames; aligned axes; point events; ideal clocks; light speed $c$ in every inertial frame (postulate); separations and speeds within the numerical domain.

### `notModeled`

Signal delays in cables or electronics; gravitational effects; accelerated or rotating clocks; clock mechanisms; optical appearance of distant clocks; detector response times; any measurement of one-way light speed.

### Owner and execution label

`src/physics/reference/events.ts` (`synchronizationRound`, `synchronizationTransitivity`, `movingRodLegs`, `receptionTime`, `classifySimultaneity`, `desynchronizationObserved`, `redescribe`), with transforms from `kinematics.ts`. Public label "Ideal model, host calculation" until `am-fs-owner-relativity-feh` is adopted and an accepted FrankenSim result produced the snapshot.

### Views and caption readings

Primary: the ledger table. Secondary: an SVG track scene with stations and signal paths, where a received flash is visibly a later event than its emission. Optional: an event diagram labeled "later geometric aid (Minkowski 1908)" with light lines at 45 degrees and coherent axis scaling. Canvas and WebGL are not needed. Every view caption carries authored R0-R3 texts in the manifest's caption records (audited by `audit-readings.ts`), consistent with the §1 readings.

### Named preset scenarios (`content/scenarios/`, referenced by the first encounter, results cards, Journey III, and the tour)

- `sr-01-sync-0-10`: emission at 0, reception at 10, reflection assigned 5.
- `sr-01-second-flash-20-30`: emission at 20, reception at 30, reflection assigned 25.
- `sr-01-round-trip-10ls`: a round trip over 10 ls gives speed $c$.
- `sr-01-rod-chase-0.6c`: rod ends 10 ls apart moving at $0.6c$; legs 25 s and 6.25 s.
- `sr-01-moving-pair-0.6c`: $L = 10$ ls at $0.6c$; 6 s desynchronization, trailing clock ahead.
- `sr-01-three-stations`: transitivity of synchronization across A, B, C.

### Action contract (clock and event geometry family)

Choose named events from the ledger with the shared `EventSelector` (from `am-inst-interaction-families-m2ps`: events addressed by ledger ids; selecting two events and a frame issues the `estimator-change` query "Which frame regards these as simultaneous?"; changing the frame issues an `observer-change` that keeps event and run identities; near-equal times are classified through `classifyWithTolerance` and may return an indeterminate boundary result); set separations, offsets, and speeds by typed entry validated against the owner's domain without clamping; emit a signal with a button at a typed model time. Screen readers receive committed comparisons ("In the platform frame the trailing clock of the moving pair reads 6 s ahead"), never per-frame streams. The visual and equivalent paths produce identical runtime commands (`am-a11y-action-contracts-k75g`).

### Predict mode, code, tape, permalink, embed

- Predict (on by default for first visits): before revealing the moving pair, choose among "they agree with us," "the leading clock is ahead," "the trailing clock is ahead." The prediction is a tape `prediction` event; the explanation is available regardless.
- Show the code: the pinned source of `synchronizationRound` and `desynchronizationObserved`, identifiers colored like their equation terms, with identifier bindings for every live term.
- Tape model identity `sr-01@<modelVersion>`; commands classified as listed above; permalink `?tape=` with bounded size.
- Manifest sets `embeddable: true`; the rendered embed at `/embed/lab/sr-01` is exercised by `am-inst-embed-route-rnyg` and recorded at `am-dod-relativity-105y`.

### Result weave (predicate records owned here, targets from the §1-2 readings)

`threshold` and `agreement` predicates with hysteresis light the §1 criterion sentence when a pair satisfies it, the §1 constant sentence when the round-trip speed is shown, and the §2 sentence about observers moving with the rod when the chase legs or the moving pair's desynchronization are shown. Targets are sentence ids from the frozen inventory.

### Misconceptions addressed

"Time dilation is symmetric, so it cannot be real" (groundwork: simultaneity is procedure-relative); the network-latency confusion (the analogy stops because the effect is not a delay artifact).

## Technical Approach

- Manifest `content/experiments/sr-01.yaml` per `am-cm-schemas-experiment-fuu`; explicit dispatcher case; owner binding in `src/experiments/owners.ts`; instance-scoped owner from the runtime; views (planned `src/visuals/relativity/sr-01/`, location as frozen by the retrospective) consume only the accepted snapshot.
- The ledger is the canonical scientific state; the scene and diagram are projections. A change of the frame of description calls `redescribe` and never creates events.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The ledger implements the stated procedure; reception and remote-event times are distinct in every view; each clock's own reading at an event is unchanged by an observer change.
- [ ] Fixtures pass: emission 0 and reception 10 assign 5; emission 20 and reception 30 assign 25; a round trip over 10 ls gives speed $c$; §2 rod ends with $r_{AB} = 10$ ls and $u = 0.6c$ give legs of 25 s and 6.25 s; a pair with $L = 10$ ls at $0.6c$ is desynchronized by 6 s in the platform frame, trailing clock ahead; at $v = 0$ there is no desynchronization.
- [ ] An observer change leaves event ids, clock histories, and run identity unchanged.
- [ ] $\lvert v\rvert \ge c$ returns `outside-domain`; one-way speed returns `not-applicable`; malformed separations are refused with a reason.
- [ ] Every view caption has R0-R3; every named preset exists and reproduces its stated values.
- [ ] Contract items present: `notModeled`, predict mode, show-the-code with bindings, tape identity, permalink, `embeddable: true`, action contract, 320 px, keyboard, reduced motion, honest label (`audit-instruments.ts` shows every column satisfied).

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `sr-01.test.ts` (beside the instrument binding) against the real `events.ts`, never a mock, with `expectClose` (relative $10^{-12}$, absolute $10^{-12}$ s for zero offsets): every fixture above; offsets; transitivity of synchronization for three stations through `synchronizationTransitivity`, including its `not-applicable` result for stations in relative motion; sign of the desynchronization for $\pm v$; the chase legs from `movingRodLegs`; observer-change invariance of event ids, clock readings at events, and run id; each typed refusal and its reader-facing explanation.
- `EventSelector` parity (the primitive from `am-inst-interaction-families-m2ps` with the real `events.ts`): selecting the same two events on the diagram and in the ledger table issues the same `estimator-change` action with the same classification and accepted snapshot id; a frame change issues `observer-change` and keeps event ids and `runId`; near-equal reception times return the indeterminate boundary result.
- Property test over a fixed seeded list of 200 admissible configurations: the midpoint rule assigns $(t_A + t'_A)/2$; the criterion offset is zero after synchronization; the round-trip speed equals $c$ in the procedure's frame; redescribing to $v$ and back to 0 returns coordinates within tolerance.
- Adversarial: "changing observer starts a new experiment" must fail (identities compared before and after); "a camera image of the distant clock shows its coordinate time" must fail (reception time differs from the event time by the light travel time).
- Preset tests: each named preset scenario loads through the scenario runner and reproduces its values.
- Weave predicate tests on scripted snapshots: enter and exit with hysteresis; targets resolve to sentence ids.
- Caption audit: `audit-readings.ts` finds R0-R3 for every caption; manifest validation through `audit-instruments.ts`.

### End-to-end tests

- Keyboard-only: set separation, emit a signal, select the reflection and reception rows, ask the simultaneity question in two frames; screen-reader announcements occur once per committed comparison.
- JavaScript disabled: the static worked ledger for the 0-5-10 case renders with its caption.
- 320 px (no page overflow), WebKit, reduced motion; permalink restore reproduces the accepted snapshot id; two SR-01 instances on one page keep independent run ids; rapid typed changes never show an older result under newer labels.

### Structured logging

- Unit suite `instrument-sr-01` to `artifacts/test-logs/instrument-sr-01/<log-run-id>.jsonl` through the logging library: `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId` (`am-sr-01-clock-sync-jbfn`), `paper`, `anchor`, `instrumentId`, `instanceId`, `runId` (the experiment run), `inputRevision`, `acceptedInputRevision`, `snapshotVersion`, `modelVersion`, `artifactDigest` (or the host evaluator's pinned source hash), `executionLabel`, `resultStatus`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `comparisonKind`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `message`, and `extra: {commandClass, scenarioId, eventIds, frameSpeed}`. `seed` and `streamVersion` are omitted (closed-form, no random stream).
- Browser steps (through the harness) add `browser`, `viewport`, `reducedMotion`, `jsEnabled`, and `evidence`; a failing step retains screenshot, Playwright trace, DOM snapshot, console log, network log, and the accepted snapshot JSON.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- A camera image of a distant clock shows an earlier reading than the coordinate time; never present the picture as the measurement.
- Moving the pair (physical) and changing the frame of description (observer) are different command classes and different labels.
- Near-equal times in a criterion check use an absolute tolerance, never a relative one.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-ref-events-yvl`: ledger, synchronization, chase, and desynchronization functions.
- `am-bm-slice-retrospective-pp09`: frozen instrument platform and runtime contracts.
- `am-inst-show-the-code-4brv`: the instrument contract requires a show-the-code disclosure pinned to the kernel source.
- `am-inst-predict-mode-ti7m`: the instrument contract requires predict mode or a recorded exemption.
- `am-inst-permalink-tape-s677`: the instrument contract requires bounded `?tape=` permalinks.
- `am-inst-interaction-families-m2ps`: the `EventSelector` primitive for choosing events and asking the simultaneity query.

Unblocks: `am-srk-e2e-4qkd`; `am-srk-first-encounter-471z` (round-2 proposal: the entrance opens SR-01 presets); `am-sr-results-cards-k9ck` (round-2 proposal: card probes); `am-disc-journey-iii-chain-hpr7` (the measurement-procedure stage); `am-disc-essays-measurement-fixed-cb1i` (the essay anchors here).

title: Build SR-02 magnet and conductor descriptions
description:
# Build SR-02 magnet and conductor descriptions

**Epic:** `am-ep-relativity-electrodynamics-afj` · **Batch:** batch-g · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §3.5 (introduction, §6), §8.3, §9.4 (nagging fact, Fork B), §10.2, §12.6, §13.2 (traceability only)

## Background

The paper opens with an asymmetry: move the magnet and the conductor sits in an electric field that carries energy; move the conductor and it experiences an "electromotive force" with no corresponding energy, yet equal relative motion gives the same current. Nature does not care which body moves; the theory did. Section 6 dissolves the asymmetry: the force that the magnet-frame description calls an electromotive force ($q\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{B}$ on the moving conductor's charges, with $\mathbf{E} = 0$) is, in the conductor's own rest frame, an ordinary electric field $\mathbf{E}' = \gamma(\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{B})_\perp$ obtained by transforming the magnet's field. SR-02 shows both descriptions of the same situation. It keeps two things apart: a **qualitative apparatus reconstruction** (no numbers claimed) and a **narrow analytic model** (a prescribed uniform field or ideal dipole with a test charge or straight segment) that establishes frame consistency quantitatively. The two descriptions agree only to first order in $v/c$; at finite speed they are related by the transformation law.

SR-02 also serves Journey III's nagging fact (`am-disc-journey-iii-chain-hpr7`), where the apparatus must present the two classical descriptions without yet revealing the 1905 resolution, while keeping that explanation one request away.

## Scope

In scope: SR-02 manifest with the analytic model (default) and the `sr-02:apparatus` mode, controls, typed outputs, views, caption readings, named preset scenarios (including the nagging-fact preset), weave predicate records, action contract, predict mode, show-the-code, tape identity, permalink, embeddable flag, tests.

Out of scope: `fields.ts` (`am-ref-fields-6l9`); the component-by-component derivation (`am-sr-07-field-equations-xxes`); general field transformation play (`am-sr-08-field-frame-change-5ibt`); any circuit or conductor-response model; Journey III's stage text (`am-disc-journey-iii-chain-hpr7`); the embed route.

## Requirements

**Explanatory question.** Why does moving the magnet instead of the conductor create an explanatory asymmetry, and how does the transformation remove it?

### Modes

1. **Narrow analytic model (default, quantitative):** a prescribed field region and a test charge or straight segment moving perpendicular to the field (controls and outputs below).
2. **`sr-02:apparatus` (qualitative, labeled "qualitative reconstruction"; an `ExperimentMode` with `notModeledAdditions` "no field or circuit is computed in this mode"):**
   - Magnet, coil, and galvanometer; a toggle "magnet moves" or "coil moves" at equal relative speed.
   - Classical captions, following the introduction's own descriptions (verify wording against the translation): with the magnet moving and the conductor at rest, an electric field with a definite energy arises near the magnet and produces a current in the conductor; with the conductor moving and the magnet at rest, no electric field arises, but the conductor experiences an electromotive force with no corresponding energy that produces currents of the same size and course, assuming equal relative motion.
   - Observation caption: the observable current depends only on the relative motion, to the precision of the observations (the two classical accounts agree to first order in $v/c$).
   - Resolution caption (1905, §6): in the paper's new manner of expression, the force on the conductor's charges is, in the conductor's rest frame, an electric field obtained by transforming the magnet's field; electric and magnetic forces do not exist independently of the state of motion of the coordinate system.
   - Option `resolution: withheld | shown` (a presentation setting). With `withheld`, the resolution caption sits collapsed behind a native disclosure labeled "How the 1905 paper removes this asymmetry (§6)"; it is not visible and not exposed in the accessibility tree until the reader opens it, and opening it is always allowed (guided discovery never makes an explanation conditional). With `shown`, all captions are visible.
   - Outputs are `symbolic` statements; no current, field, or EMF values are displayed in this mode.

### Controls (analytic mode)

| Control | Dimension | Unit | Model domain | Numerical domain | Default | Class |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Description frame | choice | magnet rest or conductor rest | either | either | magnet rest | observer-change |
| Relative speed $v$ | velocity | m/s (fraction of $c$ toggle) | $\lvert v\rvert < c$ | $\lvert v\rvert \le 0.95c$ | 10 m/s | setup-change |
| Field model | choice | uniform $B$ or ideal dipole | these | these | uniform | setup-change |
| Uniform field magnitude $B$ | magnetic field | T | finite | $10^{-9}$ to $10^{2}$ T | 1 T | setup-change |
| Dipole moment $m$ (dipole model) | magnetic moment | A·m² | finite | $10^{-6}$ to $10^{3}$ A·m² | 1 A·m² | setup-change |
| Test point distance and position (dipole) | length | m | $> 0$ | $10^{-3}$ to 10 m | 0.05 m, equatorial plane | setup-change |
| Segment length $\ell$ | length | m | $> 0$ | $10^{-6}$ to 10 m | 0.1 m | setup-change |
| Test charge $q$ | charge | C | finite | $\pm10^{-6}$ C | $e$ | setup-change |

### Outputs and statuses (analytic mode)

- Magnet frame: $\mathbf{E} = 0$, $\mathbf{B}$ at the test point, force on the moving charge $q\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{B}$, motional electromotive force for the segment ($vB\ell$ in the uniform model; in the dipole model the line integral $\int(\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{B})\cdot d\mathbf{l}$ along the segment, evaluated by the owner in closed form or by a declared quadrature with an error estimate).
- Conductor frame (same event): $\mathbf{E}'_\perp = \gamma(\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{B})_\perp$ for $\mathbf{E} = 0$ (for $\mathbf{B} = B\hat{z}$ and $\mathbf{v} = v\hat{x}$, $E'_y = -\gamma vB$), $\mathbf{B}'_\perp = \gamma\mathbf{B}_\perp$, force on the charge at rest $q\mathbf{E}'$, electromotive force $\gamma vB\ell$ along the segment in the uniform model.
- Covariant comparison: the transverse force transformation $F_\perp = F'_\perp/\gamma$ holds within tolerance; the invariants $\mathbf{E}\cdot\mathbf{B} = 0$ and $E^2 - c^2B^2 = -c^2B^2$ agree in both frames.
- First-order statement: the ratio of electromotive forces is $\gamma = 1 + \tfrac12\beta^2 + \dots$. The **excess** $\gamma - 1$ is computed and displayed directly with `gammaMinusOne` ($\gamma^2\beta^2/(\gamma + 1)$), never as "ratio minus 1": at 10 m/s it is $5.563\times10^{-16}$ (the naive float64 $\gamma - 1$ gives $6.66\times10^{-16}$, and the ratio $1 + 5.563\times10^{-16}$ is not representable), which is the source's "neglecting second and higher powers of $v/V$"; at $0.6c$ the ratio 1.25 is shown with the explanation that these quantities are frame-dependent and the correct comparison is the transformation law.
- Current in a real circuit: `not-applicable` (no circuit model). $\lvert v\rvert \ge c$: `outside-domain`.

### Model, `notModeled`, owner

- Model: prescribed static field in the magnet frame, pointwise field transformation at a single event, test charge without back-reaction.
- `notModeled`: conductor resistance and induced currents; self-inductance; magnetization dynamics and extended-magnet fields beyond the ideal dipole; time-varying flux of extended circuits; edge fields; radiation; unipolar machines.
- Owner: `fields.ts` (`emfBothDescriptions`, `dipoleField`, `transformSI`, `fieldInvariants`, `lorentzForce`, `forceConsistency`) with `gammaMinusOne` from `kinematics.ts` for the excess; nothing is computed in a view. Label "Ideal model, host calculation" until `am-fs-owner-electrodynamics-mxr` is adopted with accepted results; the apparatus mode carries the "Static worked example" label because it computes nothing.

### Views and caption readings

SVG apparatus schematic labeled "qualitative reconstruction"; side-by-side field and force arrows at the test point for both frames with numeric tables; the first-order excess shown as "exceeds 1 by ..." in scientific notation. No WebGL. Every caption, in both modes, carries authored R0-R3 texts in the manifest, consistent with the introduction and §6 readings; the qualitative schematic is visually distinct from the quantitative panel.

### Named preset scenarios

- `sr-02-apparatus-nagging-fact`: mode `sr-02:apparatus`, `resolution: withheld`; used by Journey III's nagging fact.
- `sr-02-apparatus`: mode `sr-02:apparatus`, `resolution: shown`; used by the §6 readings and `/lab/sr-02`.
- `sr-02-uniform-10ms`: $B = 1$ T, $v = 10$ m/s, $\ell = 0.1$ m; 1 V in the magnet frame; excess $5.563\times10^{-16}$.
- `sr-02-uniform-0.6c`: the same field at $0.6c$; ratio 1.25.
- `sr-02-dipole-equatorial`: $m = 1$ A·m², test point 0.05 m in the equatorial plane, $\lvert B\rvert = 8.000\times10^{-4}$ T (on the axis at the same distance it would be $1.600\times10^{-3}$ T), $v = 10$ m/s, force on $e$ of magnitude $1.2817\times10^{-21}$ N.

### Action contract (fields and boosts family)

Analytic mode: select the frame and a component, then inspect transformed components at the same event; typed entry for every quantity. Apparatus mode: choose "magnet moves" or "coil moves" from a radio group and read the captions; open the resolution disclosure by keyboard. Committed changes are announced once; visual and equivalent paths produce identical commands.

### Predict, code, tape identity, permalink, embed

- Predict: "The magnet moves past the wire at 10 m/s instead of the wire moving past the magnet at 10 m/s. Is the electromotive force along the wire larger, the same, or zero?" The reveal: the same to first order (they differ by $5.563\times10^{-16}$ in ratio); at $0.6c$ the descriptions differ by the factor 1.25 and are related by the transformation law. The apparatus mode states the observed equality of currents for equal relative motion symbolically.
- Show the code: pinned transform, invariant, dipole, and electromotive-force functions, with identifier bindings.
- Tape model identity `sr-02@<modelVersion>` with the mode recorded; permalink `?tape=`; manifest `embeddable: true`.

### Weave (predicate records owned here), fork, countermodel

Predicates light the introduction's asymmetry sentence in apparatus mode and the §6 sentence that the asymmetry disappears when both frames' analytic descriptions are displayed (never while the resolution is withheld). Journey III Fork B: Maxwell's equations true only in the ether frame versus form-invariant with mixing fields. The pre-1905 two-mechanism explanation reproduces the same first-order current and is presented as empirically equivalent at that order, not refuted.

## Technical Approach

- Manifest `content/experiments/sr-02.yaml` with `modes: [sr-02:apparatus]`; dispatcher case resolving the mode id; instance owner; the field configuration and event are the scientific state; the frame toggle is an observer-change command; the apparatus toggle and the resolution option are presentation-changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Fixtures: $B = 1$ T, $v = 10$ m/s, $\ell = 0.1$ m gives 1 V in the magnet frame and a conductor-frame excess of $5.563\times10^{-16}$ from the cancellation-free form; at $0.6c$ the ratio is 1.25; $F_\perp = F'_\perp/\gamma$ within $10^{-12}$ relative; invariants agree; the dipole preset gives $8.000\times10^{-4}$ T with the modern constant set's $\mu_0$.
- [ ] `sr-02:apparatus` never displays computed values; with `resolution: withheld` the resolution caption is collapsed, absent from the visible text and accessibility tree until opened, and openable by keyboard and without JavaScript; with `shown` all captions are visible.
- [ ] Analytic mode never claims to solve a circuit; frame changes preserve the event, the field configuration, and run identity.
- [ ] Every caption has R0-R3; presets reproduce their states and values; contract items present including `embeddable: true`.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `sr-02.test.ts` against the real `fields.ts` and `kinematics.ts` with `expectClose`: the fixtures above; the excess against a 40-digit reference within $10^{-12}$ relative, and a test showing the naive `gamma(beta) - 1` misses that tolerance by about 20 percent; dipole transform at a test point compared with an independent evaluation of the closed-form dipole field; the dipole segment EMF converging to $v\lvert B\rvert\ell$ at the midpoint as $\ell \to 0$ within the declared quadrature error; invariants over a fixed seeded list of 100 configurations.
- `sr-02.apparatus.test.tsx` with the real dispatcher: rendering by the mode id `sr-02:apparatus`; no numeric value in the markup for either motion state; with `resolution: withheld` the resolution text is inside a closed native disclosure and absent from the accessibility tree snapshot until the disclosure is opened; with `shown` it is present; the no-JavaScript HTML contains the disclosure; the introduction's asymmetry weave predicate fires and the §6 predicate does not fire while withheld.
- Adversarial: asserting exactly equal electromotive-force numbers in both frames at $0.6c$ must fail; an observer change must not create a new run (identities compared).
- Weave predicate tests; caption audit; preset tests; `audit-instruments.ts` columns satisfied.

### End-to-end tests

- Analytic mode: toggle frames by keyboard and read both tables; the excess displays in scientific notation; permalink round trip.
- Apparatus mode: a harness fixture host embeds `sr-02-apparatus-nagging-fact` through the dispatcher, as Journey III does; switch motion states by keyboard; confirm no numbers and the collapsed resolution; open it and confirm the §6 caption and return focus.
- JavaScript disabled shows the static worked comparison and the apparatus captions with the native disclosure; 320 px, WebKit, reduced motion.

### Structured logging

- Unit suite `instrument-sr-02` to `artifacts/test-logs/instrument-sr-02/<log-run-id>.jsonl`: `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId` (`am-sr-02-magnet-conductor-x1gc`), `paper`, `anchor`, `instrumentId`, `instanceId`, `runId`, `inputRevision`, `acceptedInputRevision`, `snapshotVersion`, `modelVersion`, `artifactDigest` (or pinned source hash), `executionLabel`, `resultStatus`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `comparisonKind`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `message`, and `extra: {mode, resolution, frame, fieldModel, commandClass, excess, scenarioId, constantSet, weaveFlags}`.
- Browser steps add `browser`, `viewport`, `reducedMotion`, `jsEnabled`, `evidence`; failures retain screenshot, trace, DOM snapshot, console and network logs, and the accepted snapshot JSON.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- The introduction's claim is about equal observable currents at the speeds of real apparatus; keep the first-order qualification visible.
- Keep the qualitative schematic visually distinct from the quantitative panel.
- A value like $1 + 5.563\times10^{-16}$ cannot be stored as a float64 ratio; the excess is its own computed output.
- Say which frame each force belongs to: in the magnet's frame the charges feel $q\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{B}$; in the conductor's frame they feel $q\mathbf{E}'$. Reversing these is a common slip.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-ref-fields-6l9`: field transforms, invariants, dipole field, electromotive force in either frame.
- `am-bm-slice-retrospective-pp09`: frozen platform contracts.
- `am-inst-show-the-code-4brv`, `am-inst-predict-mode-ti7m`, `am-inst-permalink-tape-s677`: instrument contract items.

Unblocks: `am-sre-e2e-xmj6`; `am-disc-journey-iii-chain-hpr7` (the nagging fact embeds `sr-02-apparatus-nagging-fact`; edge proposed by the discovery reviewer); `am-sr-results-cards-k9ck` (round-2 proposal: card 8's probe).

title: Build SR-03 rod measurement and simultaneity
description:
# Build SR-03 rod measurement and simultaneity

**Epic:** `am-ep-relativity-kinematics-q2g` · **Batch:** batch-e · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §3.5 §§2, 4, §5.3, §7.6, §8.3, §10.2, §10.9, §12.6, §12.11, §13.3, §13.5 (traceability only)

## Background

"The moving rod is shorter" is only meaningful once the measurement is specified: the positions of both ends taken **at one time in the measuring frame**. SR-03 makes that procedure the instrument. The reader selects endpoint events, the instrument transforms them, and only frame-simultaneous endpoint pairs are credited as length measurements. The signature fixture exposes the most common error: at $v = 0.6c$ two events 10 light-seconds apart and simultaneous in the unprimed frame map to $\Delta t' = -7.5$ s and $\Delta x' = 12.5$ ls. That larger separation is **not** a longer rod, because the events are not simultaneous in the primed frame. SR-03 authors the named teaching tape "the boost to 0.6c," which the misconception ledger, the kinematics browser journey, and Journey III replay.

## Scope

In scope: the SR-03 manifest, controls, typed outputs, 2D views, caption readings, named preset scenarios, the "the boost to 0.6c" teaching tape, weave predicate records, action contract, predict mode, show-the-code, permalink, embeddable flag, and tests.

Out of scope: the evaluators (`am-ref-events-yvl`, `am-ref-kinematics-tjq`); the Three.js sphere-and-clock studio and its tests (`am-srk-sphere-clock-studio-lpxr`); clocks (`am-sr-05-moving-clocks-2zka`); optical appearance (`am-later-deep-optical-appearance-f6ni`); the `/embed/lab/[experiment]` route (`am-inst-embed-route-rnyg`).

## Requirements

**Explanatory question.** What do measurements of a moving rod actually compare?

**Linked source.** §2 (operations (a) and (b); the relativity of simultaneity), §4 (the sphere measured as an ellipsoid with axes $R\sqrt{1 - v^2/V^2}, R, R$).

### Controls

| Control | Dimension | Unit | Model domain | Numerical domain | Default | Class |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rod rest frame | choice | K or k | either | either | k | setup-change |
| Relative speed $v$ of k with respect to K | velocity | fraction of $c$ | $\lvert v\rvert < c$ | $\lvert v\rvert \le 0.95c$ | $0.6c$ | setup-change (changes how the rod moves relative to the other frame) |
| Rod proper length $L_0$ | length | ls | $> 0$ | $10^{-6}$ to $10^{6}$ | 10 ls | setup-change |
| Measuring frame | choice | K or k | either | either | K | observer-change (re-describes the same worldlines) |
| Endpoint event selection | event ids | n/a | events on the rod-end worldlines or free events | two events | the platform-simultaneous pair | measurement-change |
| Sphere radius $R$ (studio link) | length | ls | $> 0$ | $10^{-6}$ to $10^{6}$ | 1 ls | setup-change |

Typed entry beside every slider; out-of-domain entries are explained with the admissible boundary; nothing is silently clamped.

### Derived outputs

- For the selected pair: $\Delta t$, $\Delta x$ in K and $\Delta t'$, $\Delta x'$ in k from $x' = \gamma(x - vt)$, $t' = \gamma(t - vx/c^2)$.
- Simultaneity classification in each frame (`simultaneous`, `ordered` with sign, or `indeterminate` near cancellation under an absolute-plus-relative tolerance).
- Length credit: `value` $L = L_0/\gamma$ (or $L_0$ in the rest frame) only when the endpoints are simultaneous in the measuring frame; otherwise `not-applicable` with the reason "these endpoint events are not simultaneous in the measuring frame; choose endpoints at one time of that frame" and a repair button that selects a valid pair through `selectSimultaneousEndpoints`.
- Reciprocal measurement: a rod at rest in K measured from k is shortened by the same factor.
- Sphere: measured axes $R/\gamma, R, R$ (the studio renders them from this snapshot).
- $\lvert v\rvert \ge c$: `outside-domain`.

### Model, `notModeled`, owner

- Model: inertial frames, aligned boosts, ideal rods and clocks, point endpoint events.
- `notModeled`: optical appearance and light-travel-time imaging; rigid-body dynamics, stresses, and acceleration history; material properties; non-inertial motion; measurement noise.
- Owner: `events.ts` (`measureRodLength`, `selectSimultaneousEndpoints`, `classifySimultaneity`, `redescribe`) with transforms from `kinematics.ts` (`transformEvent`, `ellipsoidAxes`). Label "Ideal model, host calculation" until `am-fs-owner-relativity-feh` is adopted with accepted results.

### Views and caption readings

2D only (plan §10.9 reserves Three.js for the studio): a strip view showing rod positions at one chosen time of each frame with endpoint markers; the event table; an optional event diagram labeled "later geometric aid (Minkowski 1908)" with coherent axis scaling and light lines at 45 degrees. A caption states "coordinate measurement, not what a camera sees." Every caption carries authored R0-R3 texts in the manifest (audited by `audit-readings.ts`), consistent with the §2 and §4 readings.

### Named preset scenarios and the teaching tape

- Teaching tape "the boost to 0.6c" (`content/experiments/tapes/the-boost-to-0.6c.yaml`, model identity `sr-03@<modelVersion>`): select the 10-ls platform-simultaneous pair, apply the boost description, reveal $-7.5$ s and 12.5 ls with the refusal as a length, then select a frame-simultaneous pair and reveal 8 ls. It is one of the five named teaching tapes audited by `am-rt-control-tapes-0gc`.
- `sr-03-boost-0.6c`: the tape's starting state.
- `sr-03-valid-pair-0.6c`: a frame-simultaneous pair on a 10-ls rod, credited 8 ls.
- `sr-03-reciprocal-0.6c`: rod at rest in K measured from k, credited 8 ls.
- `sr-03-sphere-0.6c`: sphere of radius 1 ls, measured axes 0.8, 1, 1.

### Action contract (clock and event geometry family)

Choose named endpoint events from the table with the shared `EventSelector` (from `am-inst-interaction-families-m2ps`: events addressed by ledger ids; the simultaneity query is an `estimator-change`; picking the measuring frame is an `observer-change` that keeps event and run identities; near-equal endpoint times may return the indeterminate boundary result, which is never credited as a length), pick the measuring frame, and ask "Which frame regards these as simultaneous?" and "Is this a length measurement?"; typed entry for speeds and lengths; committed answers are announced once. Visual and equivalent paths produce identical commands.

### Predict, code, tape identity, permalink, embed

- Predict: "Two events 10 ls apart happen at the same platform time. In the moving frame, are they still simultaneous, and is their separation the rod's length?" Candidates cover the common answers (still simultaneous and 10 ls; still simultaneous and 8 ls; not simultaneous, and the separation is not a length); explanation always available.
- Show the code: pinned source of `transformEvent`, `classifySimultaneity`, and `measureRodLength`, with identifier bindings for every live term.
- Tape model identity `sr-03@<modelVersion>`; permalink `?tape=`; manifest `embeddable: true` (the rendered embed is exercised by `am-inst-embed-route-rnyg`).

### Weave (predicate records owned here) and misconceptions

Predicates light the §2 relativity-of-simultaneity sentence when the classification differs between frames, and the §4 ellipsoid sentence when the sphere axes are shown. Addresses "length contraction is an optical illusion," "the rod is physically squashed," and "a larger spatial separation of two transformed events is a longer rod."

## Technical Approach

- Manifest `content/experiments/sr-03.yaml`; dispatcher case; owner binding in `src/experiments/owners.ts`; instance-scoped owner; views project the snapshot.
- The endpoint selector is a measurement-change command: the rod's worldlines and the run identity never change when the reader picks different endpoints or a different measuring frame.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Only frame-simultaneous endpoint pairs are credited; others return `not-applicable` with a repair action.
- [ ] Fixtures: at $0.6c$, $\gamma = 1.25$; the 10-ls platform-simultaneous pair maps to $\Delta t' = -7.5$ s, $\Delta x' = 12.5$ ls and is refused as a length; a rod of proper length 10 ls measured with valid endpoints is 8 ls; the reciprocal case is also 8 ls; a sphere of radius 1 ls has measured axes 0.8, 1, 1.
- [ ] Observer and measurement changes leave worldlines, event ids, and run id unchanged.
- [ ] The teaching tape and the four presets exist, replay deterministically, and reproduce their values; the control-tape audit lists "the boost to 0.6c" as present.
- [ ] Every caption has R0-R3; contract items present, including the "coordinate measurement, not what a camera sees" caption and `embeddable: true`.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `sr-03.test.ts` against the real `events.ts` and `kinematics.ts` with `expectClose` (relative $10^{-12}$; absolute $10^{-12}$ s near equal times): all fixtures; identity at $v = 0$; the inverse transform recovers the original separations; classification near equal times uses an absolute tolerance and can return `indeterminate`.
- Property test over a fixed seeded list of 200 admissible speeds and rods: every pair returned by `selectSimultaneousEndpoints` is credited with $L_0/\gamma$; every non-simultaneous pair is refused; the refusal message names the measuring frame.
- Adversarial: crediting the 12.5-ls separation as a length must fail; changing the measuring frame must not create new events (event id sets compared before and after).
- `EventSelector` parity (the primitive from `am-inst-interaction-families-m2ps` with the real `events.ts`): selecting the same endpoint pair on the diagram and in the table issues the same action, classification, and accepted snapshot id; an indeterminate pair is never credited as a length.
- Tape test: replaying "the boost to 0.6c" twice produces identical scientific digests and the stated reveals; a tape with a mismatched model identity is refused with its typed reason.
- Weave predicate tests on scripted snapshots with hysteresis; caption audit; `audit-instruments.ts` columns satisfied.

### End-to-end tests

- Run the teaching tape and assert displayed values; select endpoints by keyboard through `EventSelector`; verify the refusal message and repair button; JavaScript disabled shows the static worked fixture with its caption; 320 px, WebKit, reduced motion (no animated compression); permalink round trip preserves the accepted snapshot id; two instances on one page stay independent.

### Structured logging

- Unit suite `instrument-sr-03` to `artifacts/test-logs/instrument-sr-03/<log-run-id>.jsonl`: `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId` (`am-sr-03-rod-simultaneity-0l5i`), `paper`, `anchor`, `instrumentId`, `instanceId`, `runId`, `inputRevision`, `acceptedInputRevision`, `snapshotVersion`, `modelVersion`, `artifactDigest` (or pinned source hash), `executionLabel`, `resultStatus`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `comparisonKind`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `message`, and `extra: {commandClass, selectedEvents, measuringFrame, simultaneity, tapeId, scenarioId}`. No `seed` (closed-form).
- Browser steps add `browser`, `viewport`, `reducedMotion`, `jsEnabled`, `evidence`; failures retain screenshot, trace, DOM snapshot, console and network logs, and the accepted snapshot JSON.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- The event diagram is a later aid; the instrument must be fully usable from the strip view and table.
- Never animate a rod visibly compressing as a physical process when the reader changes only the description.
- Keep "measured in the measuring frame at one of its times" in every caption.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
- `am-ref-events-yvl`: rod measurement and simultaneity classification.
- `am-bm-slice-retrospective-pp09`: frozen platform contracts.
- `am-inst-show-the-code-4brv`, `am-inst-predict-mode-ti7m`, `am-inst-permalink-tape-s677`: instrument contract items.
- `am-inst-interaction-families-m2ps`: the `EventSelector` primitive for endpoint selection and the simultaneity query.
- `am-rt-control-tapes-0gc` (round-2 proposal): this instrument authors the named teaching tape "the boost to 0.6c," validated by that bead's tape format and audit.

Unblocks: `am-srk-e2e-4qkd`; `am-srk-sphere-clock-studio-lpxr` (3D projection of the same snapshot); `am-sr-misconceptions-cyci` and `am-sr-results-cards-k9ck` (round-2 proposals: presets and the tape); `am-disc-journey-iii-chain-hpr7`; `am-later-deep-optical-appearance-f6ni`.

title: Build SR-04 construct the Lorentz map, including the Galilean shelf step
description:
# Build SR-04 construct the Lorentz map, including the Galilean shelf step

**Epic:** `am-ep-relativity-kinematics-q2g` · **Batch:** batch-e · **Priority:** P1 · **Plan sections:** §3.5 §3, §5.5, §8.3, §9.4 (the move), §10.2, §11.6, §12.11, §13.2, §13.3, §14.3 (traceability only)

## Background

Most explanations hand over $x' = \gamma(x - vt)$ and $t' = \gamma(t - vx/c^2)$. SR-04 lets the reader **construct** the map from the postulates, so the reader sees exactly which requirement fixes which coefficient, that a scale factor survives the light constraints, and that the transverse equations need their own argument. It begins with the Galilean shelf step: the ordinary map works for slow objects and fails to keep light at $c$, so the conflict is between two stated commitments, and the reader decides what to reconsider. This is the side door of Journey III and a pedagogical reconstruction. The front door (Einstein's functional equation) lives in the §3 readings; both routes are formal chains in `am-srk-equations-30cq`, and SR-04's steps render from those chain steps.

The Galilean step also sits on the `/1904` desk (`am-disc-desk-1904-9hgd`), where it must be framed in 1904 terms. With light traveling at $c$ relative to the ether, the speeds $c - v$ and $c + v$ that the Galilean map gives a moving observer are exactly what the ether theory predicted; the puzzle available by the end of 1904 was that ether-drift experiments found none of the consequences, and that Poincaré's 1904 lecture named a principle of relativity. It was not a 1905 postulate. SR-04 therefore declares an `sr-04:1904` mode that shows only that step, in those terms, with every later aid absent.

## Scope

In scope: SR-04 manifest, the constraint engine UI, typed outputs, views, caption readings, named preset scenarios, the authored construction tape, weave predicate records, action contract, predict mode, show-the-code, permalink, embeddable flag, the `sr-04:1904` mode embedded by the `/1904` desk, and tests.

Out of scope: `kinematics.ts` (`am-ref-kinematics-tjq`); §3 readings and chains (`am-srk-readings-s3-odqp`, `am-srk-equations-30cq`); the countermodel comparison with Lorentz's ether kinematics (`am-reason-countermodel-workbench-t07q`); non-collinear composition (`am-sr-06-velocity-composition-7ni4`); the named teaching tape "the boost to 0.6c" (authored by `am-sr-03-rod-simultaneity-0l5i`); the `/1904` desk page and its Lorentz 1904 views (`am-disc-desk-1904-9hgd`, `am-disc-shelf-michelson-fizeau-dauq`).

## Requirements

**Explanatory question (full mode).** What map between two inertial frames keeps both postulates, and what does each requirement decide?

**Explanatory question (`sr-04:1904`).** If light travels at $c$ relative to the ether and frames are related by the ordinary change of frame, what speeds should a moving observer find, and what did the ether-drift experiments look for?

### Construction sequence (full mode, the constraint engine)

1. **Galilean candidate:** $x' = x - vt$, $t' = t$ (`galileanMap`). Test objects: a slow object ($u = 10$ m/s with $v = 30$ m/s: the Galilean result $u' = -20$ m/s differs from the relativistic result by a relative amount $\frac{uv/c^2}{1 - uv/c^2} \approx 3.338\times10^{-15}$ from `galileanRelativisticVelocityDifference`, so it "works"), and light $x = ct$ (transformed speed $c - v$, which fails; at $v = 0.6c$ it is $0.4c$). Subtracting two nearly equal velocities in float64 gives $3.375\times10^{-15}$, about 1.1 percent wrong, so the owner's cancellation-free form is required.
2. **Affine ansatz** with the origin convention explained (the moving origin is at $x = vt$, both origins coincide at $t = 0$): $x' = a(v)(x - vt)$, $t' = b(v)t + d(v)x$. Linearity is presented as following from homogeneity, uniform motion, and inertial coordinates, never as needing no assumptions.
3. **Right-moving light** $x = ct \mapsto x' = ct'$ and **left-moving light** $x = -ct \mapsto x' = -ct'$ together force $b = a$ and $d = -av/c^2$. The output is `underdetermined`: a one-parameter family in $a(v)$.
4. **Inverse (reciprocity):** the unprimed frame moves at $-v$ relative to the primed one, so applying both maps gives $a(v)a(-v)(1 - v^2/c^2) = 1$. Still `underdetermined`.
5. **Isotropy:** $a(v) = a(-v)$, so $a^2 = \gamma^2$.
6. **Branch:** the positive branch continuously connected to the identity, $a = \gamma = (1 - v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$.
7. **Transverse step:** $y' = k(v)y$; symmetry and reciprocity give $k(v)k(-v) = 1$ and $k(v) = k(-v)$; independently, a light ray moving along $y$ in the unprimed frame ($x = 0$, $y = ct$) must still move at $c$ in the primed frame, where $x' = -\gamma vt$, $t' = \gamma t$, $y' = kct$, giving $\gamma^2v^2 + k^2c^2 = \gamma^2c^2$, so $k^2 = 1$ and $k = 1$. The instrument never copies $y' = y$ from the answer.
8. **Later aids (labeled):** the $2\times2$ matrix on $(x, t)$, $\begin{pmatrix}\gamma & -\gamma v\\ -\gamma v/c^2 & \gamma\end{pmatrix}$, determinant 1; eigenvectors on the light lines; eigenvalues $\sqrt{(1 \mp v/c)/(1 \pm v/c)}$, which reappear as Doppler factors; rapidity $\phi = \operatorname{artanh}(v/c)$ with $\gamma = \cosh\phi$, and collinear boosts adding rapidities.

**No answer preinstalled:** the engine solves only the constraints the reader has enabled (`solveCandidateFamily`, `checkCandidateMap`); $\gamma$ appears only as a derived result.

### Modes

- **Full mode (default; `/lab/sr-04`, Journey III, the §3 readings):** the construction sequence above, the later-aid panel, predict prompts, weave predicates; constant set `modern-si-2019`.
- **`sr-04:1904` (an `ExperimentMode` per `am-cm-schemas-experiment-fuu`, embedded by the `/1904` desk):**
  - `historicalStatus`: the shared enum's "available before the cutoff" value for its content (the Galilean change of frame and light moving at $c$ relative to the ether); the instrument is labeled a pedagogical reconstruction. `notModeledAdditions`: "the 1905 construction of a new map from two principles; later geometric aids." No parent `notModeled` entry is removed.
  - Content: the Galilean candidate only, with fixed coefficients. Test objects: the slow object ($u = 10$ m/s, $v = 30$ m/s gives $u' = -20$ m/s, "the ordinary addition of velocities used in mechanics," with no relativistic comparison) and light rays moving with and against the observer (speeds $c - v$ and $c + v$, shown in units of $c$: $0.4c$ and $1.6c$ at $v = 0.6c$).
  - Authored framing text (with R0-R3): "If light travels at $c$ relative to the ether and frames are related by this map, an observer moving through the ether at $v$ finds $c - v$ for light moving the same way and $c + v$ for light moving the other way. The ether theory predicts exactly that. The ether-drift experiments on the desk looked for consequences of these speeds (the Michelson and Morley round-trip comparison is sensitive at second order in $v/c$) and found none, and Poincaré's 1904 lecture named a principle of relativity. Decide what you would reconsider."
  - Absent from the rendered DOM, the accessibility tree, the tables, and the no-JavaScript HTML (and, in a host that locks the mode, from the tapes): the affine ansatz and constraint steps 2-7, the enabled-constraints checklist, candidate-coefficient editing, the admissible family and final map, the Lorentz factor, the matrix, determinant, eigenvectors and eigenvalues, rapidity, any space-time ($x$-$t$) diagram, interval language, "postulate" in the 1905 sense, "relativistic," the slow-object comparison with the relativistic result, predict prompts for later steps, and weave predicates into the relativity paper (no paper 3 sentence lights on the desk).
  - Lorentz's 1904 transformation is not duplicated here; the desk presents it through the `lorentz-1904-transformation` card and the 1904 view of `shelf-maxwell-galilean`.
  - Constants: the historical-constant-set rule of the review paragraph below applies to every constant this mode presents, and at present it presents none. Light-related speeds are expressed in units of $c$ and slow speeds in m/s, so no numeric value of $c$ is needed or displayed, and the modern SI value of $c$ never appears in this mode. If a 1904-mode output ever needs a numeric value of $c$, it must come from a registered pre-1905 historical constant set with its stated uncertainty (none is registered yet; recorded as a review issue), never `modern-si-2019`.
  - Controls: frame speed $v$ (typed entry in fractions of $c$, and m/s for the slow object) and the choice of test object; out-of-domain entries explain that no speed through the ether at or above light speed is admitted in this model, with the admissible boundary, never a silent clamp.
  - Views: a track view with velocity arrows and a table; no $x$-$t$ diagram.
  - Predict (1904 mode): "An observer moves through the ether at 0.6 of the speed of light, in the direction a light ray travels. Under the ordinary change of frame, how fast does the observer find that light to move?" (0.4 of light speed; light speed; 1.6 of light speed).
  - Show the code: the pinned `galileanMap` source only.
  - Mode switching and tapes: the owner computes the same accepted snapshot in both modes, and the mode selects only which outputs, controls, and views are presented. On the standalone instrument the reader may switch between `sr-04:1904` and full mode; the switch is a presentation-change recorded on the tape that keeps `runId` and `snapshotVersion`. A host that locks the mode (the `/1904` desk) renders no switch, offers only Galilean-step commands, and refuses a `?tape=` containing any later command with the typed reason `mode-mismatch`, so the desk's tapes contain only Galilean-step commands.

### Controls (full mode)

| Control | Dimension | Unit | Model domain | Numerical domain | Default | Class |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frame speed $v$ | velocity | fraction of $c$ | $\lvert v\rvert < c$ | $\lvert v\rvert \le 0.95c$ | $0.6c$ | observer-change |
| Candidate coefficients $a, b, k$ (dimensionless) and $d$ (s/m) | as stated | typed | finite reals | $\pm10^{6}$ in the displayed unit | Galilean values | setup-change of the candidate map (not of the world) |
| Enabled constraints | checklist | n/a | any subset | any subset | none | estimator-change (they change inference about the map, never events) |
| Test objects | list | n/a | slow objects, light rays, transverse ray | finite | slow object and $\pm c$ rays | measurement-change |
| Show later aids | toggle | n/a | n/a | n/a | off | presentation-change |

### Outputs and statuses (full mode)

Constraint residuals for the current candidate (`value`); admissible family (`symbolic` or `underdetermined` until fixed); final map (`value`); test-object table with pass or fail per postulate; determinant, eigenpairs, rapidity (`value`, labeled later aid). $\lvert v\rvert \ge c$: `outside-domain`.

### `notModeled`, owner, views, captions

- `notModeled`: non-aligned axes and rotations; accelerated frames; gravity; a fully rigorous derivation of linearity; origins that do not coincide; non-collinear composition (SR-06).
- Owner: `kinematics.ts` (`galileanMap`, `galileanRelativisticVelocityDifference`, `solveCandidateFamily`, `checkCandidateMap`, `boostMatrixXT`, `transformEvent`, `inverseBoost`, `rapidity`); nothing is computed in a view. Label "Ideal model, host calculation" until upstream adoption.
- Views (full mode): a constraint panel (primary) that renders each applied constraint as the matching chain step from `am-srk-equations-30cq`, an SVG plot of the light lines and a transformed grid (labeled later aid when shown as a spacetime diagram), and a matrix panel. Every caption in both modes carries authored R0-R3 texts in the manifest.

### Named preset scenarios and the construction tape

- `sr-04-galilean-shelf`: full mode, the Galilean candidate with the slow object and both light rays (light at $0.4c$ and $1.6c$); used by Journey III.
- `sr-04-galilean-1904`: mode `sr-04:1904`, $v = 0.6c$, slow object $-20$ m/s, light rays $0.4c$ and $1.6c$; used by the `/1904` desk.
- `sr-04-light-constraints-0.6c`: both light constraints enabled; the family is `underdetermined`.
- `sr-04-construct-0.6c`: the final map at $0.6c$; also the starting and end states of the authored tape "construct the map at 0.6c" (`content/experiments/tapes/construct-the-map-0.6c.yaml`), which steps Galilean candidate → light constraints → inverse → isotropy → branch → transverse ray.
- `sr-04-later-aids-0.6c`: determinant 1, eigenvalues 0.5 and 2, rapidity $\ln 2$.

### Action contract (derivations and boosts families)

Full mode: select a named constraint, read its role, and apply it as a justified step with the shared `ExpressionActionPicker` (named subexpressions from the compiled chain trees of `am-srk-equations-30cq`, each with its role; "advance a justified step" uses a rule from the derivation-chain rule set, and an unknown subexpression id or rule fails validation); enter or adjust candidate coefficients with the shared `CoefficientEditor` (a coefficient handle or a typed signed value, always a setup change of the candidate map and never of the world); both primitives come from `am-inst-interaction-families-m2ps`. Query "Does this candidate keep right-moving light at $c$?"; every committed step is announced with the chain step's authored spoken form. 1904 mode: choose a test object and read its transformed speed. Visual and equivalent paths produce identical commands.

### Predict, code, tape identity, permalink, embed

- Predict (full mode) before step 3: "Once both light directions are required, what must $b$ be?" (choices: $b = 1$, $b = a$, $b = \gamma^2$); before step 4: "Is the map now fully fixed?"
- Show the code: pinned source of `checkCandidateMap`, `solveCandidateFamily`, and the boost functions, with identifier bindings.
- Tape model identity `sr-04@<modelVersion>` with the mode recorded; permalink `?tape=`; manifest `embeddable: true` (embed rendered by `am-inst-embed-route-rnyg`).

### Weave (predicate records owned here), fork, misconceptions

In full mode, predicates light the §3 sentences for the unknown function (after step 3), $\varphi(v)\varphi(-v) = 1$ (after step 4), the symmetry argument (after step 5), and the printed result (after step 6); weave predicates are disabled in `sr-04:1904`. Journey III Fork A notes that Lorentz's 1904 ether-and-local-time kinematics yields the same formulas and is not declared refuted by this construction. Addresses "Einstein's $\beta$ is $v/c$" through the concordance note on the result.

**Added in review (1904 mode for the desk).** The manifest declares a `mode: 1904` preset that the /1904 desk embeds: only the Galilean map applied to low-speed objects and to light rays, the historical constant set, no rapidity, spacetime diagram, interval, or other later aid, and labels restricted to knowledge available by 1904. Switching between the desk mode and the full instrument is a presentation-change that preserves the run. Tests assert that the 1904 mode renders no later-aid label or control, that its light-ray check reproduces the Galilean failure to preserve $x = \pm ct$, and that the mode switch keeps `runId` and `snapshotVersion` unchanged.

## Technical Approach

- Manifest `content/experiments/sr-04.yaml` with `modes: [sr-04:1904]`; the dispatcher resolves the mode id; instance owner.
- Each constraint application is a derivation-chain step rendered by the equation system from `am-srk-equations-30cq`, so the same steps appear in the readings.
- Mode filtering happens in the manifest's parameter and output overrides and the view registry, so later views are never rendered and then hidden.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Steps 1-8 work in order and out of order in full mode; the engine never uses $\gamma$ as an input.
- [ ] Fixtures at $0.6c$: after light constraints $b = a$, $d = -0.6a$ (in units $c = 1$); after the inverse $a(v)a(-v) = 1.5625$; isotropy gives $a = \pm1.25$; the positive branch gives 1.25; transverse $k = 1$; determinant 1; eigenvalues 0.5 and 2; rapidity $\ln 2 \approx 0.693147$; the Galilean map sends light to speed $0.4c$; the slow-object relative deviation is $3.338\times10^{-15}$ from the cancellation-free helper.
- [ ] Identity at $v = 0$; inverse round trip within $10^{-12}$.
- [ ] `sr-04:1904` is declared with its historical status and `notModeledAdditions` and removes no parent `notModeled` entry; rendered by mode id through the dispatcher it shows the Galilean step with the authored ether framing, the slow object at $-20$ m/s without a relativistic comparison, and light rays at $0.4c$ and $1.6c$ for $v = 0.6c$.
- [ ] In `sr-04:1904` every listed later view is absent from the DOM, the accessibility tree, the tables, the tapes, and the no-JavaScript HTML; no weave predicate fires; no constant value, in particular no modern SI value of $c$, is presented; on the standalone instrument a mode switch keeps `runId` and `snapshotVersion`; a host that locks the mode renders no switch and refuses a tape containing a later command with `mode-mismatch`.
- [ ] Later aids are labeled in full mode; the construction tape and presets replay deterministically; every caption has R0-R3; contract items present including `embeddable: true`.

## Test Plan

### Unit and integration tests

- `sr-04.test.ts` against the real `kinematics.ts` with `expectClose`: every full-mode fixture (relative $10^{-12}$; the slow-object deviation against a 50-digit reference within $10^{-9}$ relative, and a test demonstrating that the naive subtraction misses that tolerance); the solver's family is `underdetermined` exactly until steps 4-6; property tests at a fixed seeded list of 200 speeds $\lvert v\rvert < 0.95c$ that the final map preserves $x = \pm ct$ and the transverse ray; removing isotropy leaves a two-branch result and removing the branch rule leaves $\pm\gamma$.
- Guard test: the constraint path does not import or reference the Lorentz factor function before step 6 (static import-graph check with a planted-violation fixture).
- Chain-rendering test: each applied constraint renders the matching chain step id from `am-srk-equations-30cq`; a renamed step id fails.
- Primitive parity (with `am-inst-interaction-families-m2ps` and the real `kinematics.ts`): highlighting a subexpression and choosing it from the list yield the same subexpression id and justified step, and an unknown id fails; dragging a coefficient handle and typing the same signed value issue the same `setup-change` of the candidate and reach the same accepted snapshot id.
- `sr-04.mode1904.test.tsx` with the real dispatcher, runtime, and owner: renders `sr-04:1904` by mode id; asserts every absence in the list above over the rendered markup and the accessibility tree (a planted later-view string fixture fails with its id); asserts the framing text, $-20$ m/s, $0.4c$, and $1.6c$; asserts no weave flags are published; asserts that no presented output carries a constant value, in particular no `modern-si-2019` value of $c$; asserts that switching between `sr-04:1904` and full mode on the standalone instrument is a presentation-change that keeps `runId` and `snapshotVersion` and renders no later-aid label or control while in 1904 mode; asserts that in a host that locks the mode no switch renders, the tape contains only Galilean-step commands, and a tape containing a later command is refused with `mode-mismatch`.
- Manifest validation through the experiment schema: the mode's `historicalStatus` and `notModeledAdditions` validate; a fixture mode that drops a parent `notModeled` entry fails.
- Anachronism lint over the 1904-mode captions and framing text.
- Tape test: "construct the map at 0.6c" replays to identical digests; weave predicate tests on scripted snapshots; caption audit; `audit-instruments.ts` columns satisfied.

### End-to-end tests

- Full mode: keyboard-only construction from Galilean candidate to final map; screen-reader summaries after each committed step; JavaScript disabled shows the static constructed derivation; 320 px, WebKit, reduced motion; return-stack round trip from the §3 reading; permalink restores the accepted snapshot id.
- 1904 mode: a harness fixture host page embeds `sr-04:1904` through the dispatcher with the mode locked, as the desk does; select test objects by keyboard; assert the absence list in the DOM and accessibility tree and that no mode switch renders; JavaScript disabled shows the static 1904 worked example; 320 px, reduced motion. On `/lab/sr-04`, switch to 1904 mode and back by keyboard and assert unchanged `data-run-id` and `data-snapshot-version`.

### Structured logging

- Unit suite `instrument-sr-04` to `artifacts/test-logs/instrument-sr-04/<log-run-id>.jsonl`: `timestamp`, `suite`, `logRunId`, `testId`, `beadId` (`am-sr-04-lorentz-map-px1k`), `paper`, `anchor`, `instrumentId`, `instanceId`, `runId`, `inputRevision`, `acceptedInputRevision`, `snapshotVersion`, `modelVersion`, `artifactDigest` (or pinned source hash), `executionLabel`, `resultStatus`, `expected`, `actual`, `tolerance`, `comparisonKind`, `outcome`, `durationMs`, `message`, and `extra: {mode, modeLocked, constantSetId, laterViewsPresent, step, enabledConstraints, candidate, residuals, chainStepId, commandClass, tapeId}`.
- Browser steps add `browser`, `viewport`, `reducedMotion`, `jsEnabled`, `evidence`; failures retain screenshot, trace, DOM snapshot, console and network logs, and the accepted snapshot JSON.

## Considerations and Pitfalls

- Do not present the Minkowski interval as a premise; it may appear only as a verification oracle in the later-aid panel.
- Changing the candidate map is not a change of the world; label it so.
- Never compute a tiny velocity difference by subtracting nearly equal numbers.
- In 1904 mode, $c - v$ is not a failure of the Galilean map; it is the ether theory's prediction. The tension lies with the null results and the principle of relativity, so the framing must never smuggle in the 1905 light postulate.

## Dependencies

Blocked by:
